kept.title: The Outlook calendar only ever sees the date range of its first sync
kept.location: src/application/calendar.rs:1315-1355 and 1438-1449; src/service/microsoft_graph.rs:570-585 and 1192-1218
kept.what_this_is: The Outlook calendar sync uses Graph's calendarView/delta. The first request gives a start and end (180 days back, 365 days ahead). Each sync after that sends only the stored delta link.
kept.problem: Microsoft's page on calendar view delta says the delta and next links encode the startDateTime and endDateTime of the first request, and that tracking is specific to that range. The code keeps one delta link for ever. It starts a new round only after a 410, and even then it reuses the old link's absence check rather than a new range. So the window never moves forward. last_full_sync is stored (sync_marker.rs:56-60) but nothing reads it here.
kept.concrete_case: First sync on 1 Oct 2026, so the range ends on 1 Oct 2027. On 1 Feb 2027 a meeting is booked in Outlook for 15 Nov 2027. It is outside the stored range and never arrives here. From 1 Oct 2027 on, no new Outlook meeting arrives at all, and Due Now never alerts for them.
kept.fix: In sync_microsoft_calendar, treat the stored link as absent when the state's last_full_sync is older than about 30 days: `let delta_link = state.as_ref().filter(|s| still_fresh(s.last_full_sync.as_deref())).and_then(|s| s.delta_link.as_deref());`. The existing `delta_link.is_none()` then records the new full sync. While there, use one named window (caldav_sync.rs:675-678 already has HOW_FAR_BACK_THE_READ_ASKS and HOW_FAR_AHEAD_THE_READ_ASKS) instead of the three copies of 180 and 365 at calendar.rs:927-928, 951-952 and 1322-1323.
kept.if_skipped: An Outlook calendar slowly goes blind. After a year it shows nothing new, and a missed meeting is the first sign.
kept.ledger_entry: none

verdict.reason:
Confirmed by reading the code. In calendar.rs:1315-1327 the window (180 days back, 365 ahead) is built only when no delta link is stored. After the first sync a link is always stored (1438-1449), and nothing ever clears it: there is no clear or reset of sync state anywhere in src, and last_full_sync is written by sync_marker.rs:56-60 but never read. list_events (microsoft_graph.rs:1201-1204) uses the stored link and ignores start and end. Microsoft's event-delta page (fetched 2026-10-14) says a delta round is "bound by the date range of a calendarView", and that the start and end are encoded into the nextLink and deltaLink tokens. It also says events outside that range that are added or changed come back under @removed. So the window stays fixed at the first sync's dates. The path runs in production (wx_app.rs:31401). It is not in .planning/WINDOWS.md. No test covers it: the tests that sync more than once call forget_the_delta_marker between syncs, so each read starts again.

Two things make it worse than the finding says. (1) The 410 fallback at 1346-1352 is broken. It only runs when a link was stored, and then start and end are None (line 1326). The retry therefore asks for calendarView/delta?$top=100 with no window, which Graph refuses. The error goes up through `?`, the dead link stays stored, and every later sync fails the same way. That is the exact failure the comment at 1331-1334 says was fixed. No test exercises this retry. (2) An event created here, dated after the stored window's end, is pushed to Outlook. The next delta reports it under @removed, as Microsoft's page says. Lines 1380-1388 delete any stored row with that id without checking the date range, so the meeting disappears here.

The proposed fix (ignore the link when last_full_sync is older than about 30 days) is not enough on its own. A 410 on a fresh link still retries with no window.
verdict.corrected_problem: The Outlook calendar view's delta link carries the date range of the first request, and the code keeps that link for ever. last_full_sync is stored and never read. So from the first sync on, the app only ever sees meetings dated between 180 days before and 365 days after that sync. Outlook reports a meeting outside that range under @removed, and lines 1380-1388 delete the copy here without checking dates. So a meeting created here and dated past the window's end vanishes from this program at the next sync. The 410 recovery cannot work either. The window is built only when no link is stored, so the retry after Gone sends no startDateTime or endDateTime. Graph refuses that, the error returns before the marker is saved, the dead link stays stored, and the Outlook calendar stops syncing for good.
verdict.corrected_fix: In sync_microsoft_calendar: (a) always compute (start, end), removing the `if delta_link.is_none()` gate at 1320-1327. list_events ignores them when a link is passed, and the 410 retry then carries a window. (b) Treat the stored link as absent once state.last_full_sync is more than about 30 days old (`state.as_ref().filter(|s| still_fresh(s.last_full_sync.as_deref())).and_then(|s| s.delta_link.as_deref())`). (c) Pass "this run read a window", meaning no usable link or the 410 branch was taken, as is_a_full_sync instead of `delta_link.is_none()`. That way last_full_sync also moves after a 410 recovery. Red tests first: one with a stale last_full_sync whose request must contain startDateTime, and one where the server answers 410 and then 200, whose second request must contain startDateTime and endDateTime. Known cost to note in the commit: a fresh full read does not report deletions made since the last delta call, so a meeting deleted at Outlook within one sync interval of a refresh can linger here. The 410 path already has that gap. Using HOW_FAR_BACK_THE_READ_ASKS and HOW_FAR_AHEAD_THE_READ_ASKS in place of the three 180/365 copies is optional cleanup, not part of the fix.

kept.title: A subscribed calendar feed shows a moved or cancelled day of a repeating event wrongly
kept.location: src/application/caldav_sync.rs:1150-1201 (refresh_subscription); compare the CalDAV path at 841-843 and 950-963; src/service/ical_subscription.rs:98-112; RECURRENCE-ID kept at src/service/caldav.rs:1039
kept.what_this_is: A subscribed .ics feed (holidays, a school or team calendar) is fetched in full on each refresh and written into one calendar here.
kept.problem: A feed carries a repeating event and its changed days as separate VEVENTs with the same UID, told apart by RECURRENCE-ID. parse_ics keeps all of them. The CalDAV sync splits them and folds each changed day into its series with one_caldav_day_kept_out_of_its_series. refresh_subscription does not: it saves every VEVENT as a plain event under the shared UID. The CalDAV comment at 831-840 describes exactly the overwrite this causes.
kept.concrete_case: A feed has "Assembly", weekly on Tuesday at 09:00, and one VEVENT with RECURRENCE-ID for 3 Nov moved to 14:00. On first refresh two rows are stored with the same provider id: the series and a one-off at 14:00. The series still draws 3 Nov at 09:00 (no exception added), so that Tuesday shows twice. A cancelled day (STATUS:CANCELLED) still shows at 09:00. On the next refresh both VEVENTs map to the one row held_by_uid kept, so each is written over it in turn. If the feed lists the changed day before the series, that row becomes a second copy of the series, and every Tuesday then shows twice.
kept.fix: Split remote_events by `recurrence_id.is_none()` as the CalDAV path does. Save the whole events in the existing loop. Pass each changed day to one_caldav_day_kept_out_of_its_series, with in_feed as a HashSet<String> standing in for seen_uids. About ten lines, and it reuses the code that already handles this.
kept.if_skipped: Subscribed calendars show moved meetings at both times and cancelled ones as still on, and a later refresh can double a whole series.
kept.ledger_entry: none

verdict.reason: The defect is real and reachable: wx_app.rs:31459 calls refresh_subscription for every feed calendar. The finding gets the mechanism wrong, though, and the real outcome is worse than it says. Each step checks out against the code. parse_ics (ical_subscription.rs:98-112) hands each VEVENT to parse_ical_vevent on its own, and event_from_its_own_lines keeps RECURRENCE-ID (caldav.rs:1039). refresh_subscription (caldav_sync.rs:1164-1201) saves every VEVENT through caldav_event_to_local with provider_event_id = UID and never splits on recurrence_id. The CalDAV path does split (841-843, 950-963). The claim of "two rows with the same provider id" is wrong. calendar_events has UNIQUE(account_id, calendar_id, provider_event_id) (mod.rs:2458), and save_calendar_event upserts on that key (calendar.rs:233), so the changed day lands on the series' row even on the first refresh, when held_by_uid is empty. The outcome is last-written-wins on every refresh, decided by feed order. Series first, moved or cancelled day after: the series row becomes that one day, with no RRULE, its own start and status, and provider_recurrence_id set. Every other occurrence of the repeating event disappears from the calendar. Changed day first, series after: the series survives, but the move and the cancellation are lost, so the day shows at the old time or still shows when it was called off. Nothing ever adds the day to the series' exception_dates, and only exception_dates suppress an occurrence (occurrences.rs:112). No subscription test uses RECURRENCE-ID (the only RECURRENCE-ID fixtures in caldav_sync.rs are CalDAV ones). The ledger has no entry for this: entries 635, 638 and 729-734 are about invitations and Google/Outlook days, not feeds. The proposed fix is the smallest one that works and reuses tested code. one_caldav_day_kept_out_of_its_series already takes the calendar pair, deleted_here and a HashSet<String>. one_day_kept_out_of_the_series, called with TheProviderItself, does not mark the series pending, so say_the_change_cannot_be_saved does not fire. And because carry_over_local_only does not carry provider_recurrence_id, a row already damaged this way is corrected by the series VEVENT on the first refresh after the fix. Must: a subscribed team or school calendar silently loses a whole weekly series, or shows moved and cancelled days wrongly, and the fix is small.
verdict.corrected_problem: A feed carries a repeating event and its changed days as separate VEVENTs with the same UID, told apart by RECURRENCE-ID. parse_ics keeps all of them, each with recurrence_id set (caldav.rs:1039). refresh_subscription (caldav_sync.rs:1164-1201) saves every VEVENT as a plain event with provider_event_id = UID. The table's UNIQUE(account_id, calendar_id, provider_event_id) (mod.rs:2458) and save_calendar_event's ON CONFLICT on that key (calendar.rs:233) collapse them onto one row, on the first refresh and on every one after, so the VEVENT written last wins. Take "Assembly", weekly on Tuesday at 09:00, with a VEVENT for 3 Nov moved to 14:00 (or STATUS:CANCELLED). If the feed lists the series first, the row becomes a single 3 Nov event with no RRULE: every other Tuesday disappears, and with a cancelled day the whole series shows as one cancelled event. If the changed day comes first, the series overwrites it: 3 Nov shows at 09:00, and a cancelled day still shows as on, because nothing adds it to the series' exception_dates. The CalDAV path avoids this by splitting on recurrence_id (841-843) and folding each changed day with one_caldav_day_kept_out_of_its_series (950-963). result.created is also counted once per VEVENT for what is one row.
verdict.corrected_fix: In refresh_subscription, make in_feed a HashSet<String>. Split remote_events with .iter().partition(|e| e.recurrence_id.is_none()). Run the existing loop over the whole events only, inserting remote.uid.clone(). Then, for each changed day with a recurrence_id, call one_caldav_day_kept_out_of_its_series(cache, (account_id, &calendar.id), changed, the_day_it_was, &deleted_here, &mut in_feed, &mut result)?, the same call the CalDAV path makes at 950-963. The compound "uid:recurrence-id" ids it inserts keep the removal pass from deleting the changed-day rows. That is about ten lines. The red test is a feed holding a weekly series and one moved RECURRENCE-ID VEVENT, run in both orders. Assert that the series keeps its RRULE and gains the moved day as an exception date, and that the moved day is stored under the compound id at its new time. Add a cancelled-day case that asserts the day goes onto the series' exception_dates.

kept.title: A full read never removes what the provider deleted while the marker was stale
kept.location: src/application/contacts_sync.rs:2379-2385 and 2389-2490 (Google), 2599-2608 and 2610-2704 (Outlook); src/application/calendar.rs:945-959 and 975-1034 (Google), 1344-1355 and 1366-1421 (Outlook); compare tasks_sync.rs:1024-1032 and caldav_sync.rs:965-981
kept.what_this_is: With a valid marker, each provider reports deletions outright: Google marks a contact deleted or an event cancelled, and Graph sends @removed. When the marker is refused, the sync reads everything again.
kept.problem: A full read lists only what still exists, so deletions made since the last good read are simply missing from it. The contacts and Google or Outlook calendar reads never remove a row for being missing. The tasks sync and the CalDAV sync both do, with guards. The Google calendar read also starts a full read after any error with a token, not only after Gone (945-959), so a single 503 has the same effect.
kept.concrete_case: The laptop is shut for two weeks. During that time a meeting is cancelled on the phone and a contact is deleted. On return the stored marker is refused, the full read does not list either item, and the new marker is stored. The cancelled meeting stays here for good and its alert still fires. The contact stays, and if somebody edits it, each sync then reports a failed update for a contact Google no longer has.
kept.fix: After a read that was a full read, take off every row this provider knows that the read did not name and that has no unsent change. For contacts, call the existing one_address_book_deleted_them for each one. For calendars, use drop_synced_calendar_event, limited to the window asked for, as caldav_sync's may_be_taken_off_this_computer already does. In read_one_google_calendar, fall back to a full read only on 410, as contacts_sync already does.
kept.if_skipped: After any break of a week or so, deleted meetings and contacts come back as ghosts that never leave, and a cancelled meeting still alerts.
kept.ledger_entry: none for contacts or calendars; ledger 253 records the same gap for notes only

verdict.reason:
I checked this line by line and the gap is real. When the marker is refused, the Google contacts read (contacts_sync.rs 2379-2385) and the Outlook contacts read (2601-2606) both read the whole address book again. After that, the loops (2389-2490, 2610-2704) only act on people the answer names: deleted ones are taken off through `metadata.deleted` or `removed`, and the rest are written. No pass compares the rows held here with what came back. Neither full read lists a deleted person (`connections_url` sends no syncToken, and a Graph delta with no link has no @removed). So anybody deleted at the provider while the marker was stale stays here.

The Google calendar is the same. `events_url` never asks for showDeleted, so a full read with timeMin and timeMax leaves out a cancelled single meeting. The loop at 975-1034 removes a row only when Google says `status == "cancelled"`. The tasks sync (tasks_sync.rs 1024-1032, `gone_from` when every list was read) and CalDAV (caldav_sync.rs 965-981, `may_be_taken_off_this_computer` plus `drop_synced_calendar_event`) both remove rows that are missing from a complete answer, and both have guards.

`read_one_google_calendar` 947-959 does fall back to a full read on any error when a marker exists. `is_expired_sync_token` in contacts_sync limits the contacts fallback to 410 on purpose (861 and its test at 6035). The finding's "a single 503" overstates it, though: `list_events` already retries 429 and 5xx three times through `with_retry`, so only a lasting fault or a non-retried error, such as a body that will not parse or a 4xx, reaches the fallback. One test pins the any-error fallback: every_google_calendar.rs about line 695 uses a 200 response whose body is `refused`. A change to fall back only on 410 has to change that test.

The finding gets one quarter wrong: the Outlook calendar. In `sync_microsoft_calendar`, `start` and `end` are only set when `delta_link.is_none()` (1320-1327). The 410 fallback at 1350-1351 passes those same `None` values. So `calendar_view_url` asks for `calendarView/delta?$top=100` with no startDateTime or endDateTime. Graph requires both on a first calendarView delta request, so the fallback most likely fails and returns Err through `?`. The dead link stays stored, and the Outlook calendar stops syncing for good, which is worse than ghost rows. Nothing tests this fallback; a grep for 410 in the calendar tests finds nothing.

There is a caveat on Google contacts that I cannot settle from the repo. The fallback assumes People API answers 410 for an expired token. As I recall, Google documents that error as reason EXPIRED_SYNC_TOKEN and it may arrive as 400 FAILED_PRECONDITION. In that case the full read never happens and every sync fails instead. It needs a live check.

None of this is in .planning/WINDOWS.md. Ledger 253 is about notes only, and 825 is a different calendar matter. No doc records a decision not to remove rows that are missing from the answer. The comment at contacts_sync 1137 contrasts "merely missing" only when explaining why an explicit deletion takes waiting work with it.

The finding's estimate of 12 lines is low. The work is four sites with different scoping: Google calendar rows per calendar (`its_rows`), the window, the days of a series, and contacts that more than one address book knows. That is closer to 40-60 lines plus tests. I put it at should rather than must: the rows are stale and nothing is lost, but a cancelled meeting still alerting is visible, and phase 14 is about to exercise exactly these accounts.
verdict.corrected_problem:
After a full read, the Google and Outlook contact reads and the Google calendar read never remove a row for being missing. A full read lists only what still exists, so anything deleted or cancelled at the provider while the marker was stale stays here. The tasks sync and CalDAV both remove rows missing from a complete answer, with guards. Two more defects sit beside this one.

(a) read_one_google_calendar (calendar.rs 947-959) falls back to a full read on any error once a marker exists, not only on 410. Only failures that outlast with_retry, or that it does not retry, reach that fallback.

(b) The Outlook calendar's 410 fallback (calendar.rs 1350-1351) passes the start and end that were left as None because a delta link existed. It therefore asks calendarView/delta for no time window, which Graph refuses. The dead link stays stored and the Outlook calendar stops syncing rather than reading in full.

Unverified: the Google contacts fallback assumes People API answers an expired token with 410. If Google answers 400 FAILED_PRECONDITION or EXPIRED_SYNC_TOKEN instead, that sync fails every time instead.
verdict.corrected_fix:
1. In sync_microsoft_calendar's 410 arm, compute the 180-day-back and 365-day-ahead window and pass it. Today it passes the None start and end.

2. In read_one_google_calendar, fall back only on Error::Api { status: 410 }. Change the every_google_calendar test to answer 410 instead of the unparseable `refused` body.

3. Have each read report whether it was a full read. Google contacts already has read_the_whole_address_book; the other three reads need the same flag. After the loop of a full read that succeeded, go through the rows this provider knows that the answer did not name. Skip any row that has an unsent change, is held for a choice, or is in deleted_here.
   - Contacts: call one_address_book_deleted_them for the rows the account holds whose id_in(that address book) the answer did not name.
   - Calendars: use drop_synced_calendar_event, limited to the calendar the read was filed under (its_rows or filed_under). Only drop a row whose stored times fall inside the window asked for. Reuse caldav_sync's WhatTheAnswerCovers::OnlyBetween and would_have_named, made pub(crate), so a series that starts before the window is kept.

4. Write a red test for each of the four reads first: a stored row, a refused marker, then a full answer that omits the row. Also add the Outlook test that the fallback URL carries startDateTime.

kept.title: The contacts sync reloads the whole address book once per contact it reads
kept.location: src/application/contacts_sync.rs:2404, 2416 (Google) and 2623, 2635 (Outlook); src/data/message_cache/contacts.rs:259-276
kept.what_this_is: For each person the provider returns, the read loop calls cache.get_contacts_for_account(account_id) again so it can find the matching stored contact.
kept.problem: That call reads every contact row (31 columns, including the vCard text and the JSON lists) and then builds a map of every identity. Doing it once per arriving contact makes the read quadratic in the size of the address book. The test fixtures hold one or two contacts, so no test feels it.
kept.concrete_case: A Google address book of 3,000 contacts on the first sync, or on every full read after a token expires, means 3,000 full loads: about 9 million rows decoded and 3,000 identity maps of 3,000 entries each, on the worker that also runs the calendar and tasks syncs. Five thousand contacts is about 25 million rows. This is an estimate from the code; I did not run it.
kept.fix: Load `let mut locals = cache.get_contacts_for_account(account_id)?;` once before the loop. After each save_contact or drop, update that Vec: replace the entry by id, push a newly created one, or remove a dropped one. Then two people arriving with the same address still match the way they do now. Do the same in both syncs.
kept.if_skipped: The first sync of a large address book, and every full read after that, takes far longer than it needs to.
kept.ledger_entry: none

verdict.reason:
Confirmed line by line. In sync_google_contacts the loop over every person from list_contacts calls cache.get_contacts_for_account(account_id) at contacts_sync.rs:2416, and at :2404 for deletions. sync_microsoft_contacts does the same at :2635 and :2623. get_contacts_for_account (contacts.rs:259-276) selects 31 columns for every contact in the account, then with_their_address_books builds a HashMap of every identity. google_api.rs:717-742 pages through the whole address book, so on a full read (no sync token, or a token Google reports as too old, :2374-2387) the loop runs once per contact and each pass re-reads the whole table. The code admits the cost in a comment at contacts.rs:195-197: "a sync reads the contacts once per remote contact already". There is no ledger entry. A grep of .planning/WINDOWS.md for the function name, the file lines, "once per remote contact" and "quadratic" found nothing.

The finding gets three details wrong and misses a third site:
1. The sync does not share a worker with the calendar and tasks syncs. spawn_contacts_sync (wx_app.rs:30904-30933) runs on its own spawn_blocking thread with its own MessageCache. The cost is a slow background sync, not other syncs held up behind it.
2. On a first sync the table grows from empty, so the total is about N squared over 2 rows (about 4.5 million for 3,000 contacts). The full N squared applies to a re-read after an expired token.
3. The deletion reloads only fire on delta reads, so their cost is deletions times N.
4. Missed site: carddav_sync.rs:384. take_in_one_card reloads the whole account once per card, and whats_in (:195) reads every card on every sync. For a large CardDAV book the cost is quadratic on every sync, not only on a full read.

The fix works with two caveats:
- The snapshot widens the window in which a contact edited in the interface during the sync is missed. The sync uses a separate connection, and today it re-reads just before each decision.
- The deletion helper decides whether to drop a contact or only take this address book off it, so the caller cannot update the snapshot without knowing which happened.

Matching order is safe. Every created or merged contact already lists this address book in known_to (for example google_person_to_contact sets it, :2952), so it only matches by id. Appending to the snapshot therefore cannot change which contact an address match finds.
verdict.corrected_problem:
Three contact syncs reload the whole account's contacts once per contact the provider sends: Google (contacts_sync.rs:2416, plus :2404 for deletions), Outlook (:2635 and :2623) and CardDAV (carddav_sync.rs:384, in take_in_one_card). Each reload selects all 31 columns for every contact in the account, including vcard_raw and avatar_data_base64 that CardDAV and imported contacts carry. It then builds an identity map of the whole account (contacts.rs:259-276).

For Google and Outlook this is quadratic on a full read: the first sync, and a re-read after the stored marker expires. A first sync of 3,000 contacts decodes about 4.5 million rows. A re-read of an existing 3,000 decodes about 9 million. CardDAV reads every card on every sync (whats_in, carddav_sync.rs:195), so a large CardDAV book pays the quadratic cost every time it syncs.

The work runs on the contacts sync's own blocking thread (wx_app.rs:30904), so the interface stays responsive and no other sync waits on it. The contacts sync itself takes far longer than it needs to. The comment at contacts.rs:195-197 acknowledges the per-contact read, and no ledger entry tracks it.
verdict.corrected_fix:
In each of the three syncs, load the account's contacts once before the loop, as `let mut locals = cache.get_contacts_for_account(account_id)?;`, and keep that Vec in step with every write:
- In the match arm, take the index of the matched contact instead of holding a reference to it.
- On a merge, bind the struct returned by a_change_here_that_lost, save that exact struct, and write it to `locals[i]`.
- On a create, push the created contact onto the Vec. Order does not matter, because a new contact already lists this address book in known_to and only ever matches by id.
- On a deletion, have one_address_book_deleted_them return what it did. Either it returns the remaining contact (`local.no_longer_in(book)`), which replaces `locals[i]`, or it dropped the contact, which is removed from the Vec. Do not copy that decision into the caller.
- Leave the per-contact `cache.is_held_for_a_choice(&local.id)?` check as it is. It is a single-row query and stays fresh.
- In take_in_one_card, pass `&mut Vec<ContactEntry>` from the caller's loop in place of the read at :384.

Say in a comment that the snapshot misses an edit made in the interface while the loop runs, and that the window is now the loop's length rather than one iteration.

Red test first: a sync of two people with the same address must still produce one contact and one create, as it does now. Pair it with a count of contact reads per sync, through a test-only counter on MessageCache or a test that the reads do not grow with the number of people.

kept.title: Two Outbox passes can send the same message twice
kept.location: src/presentation/wx_app.rs:24529-24786 (flush_outbox; callers 6005, 6012, 6535, 16836, 19319, 31844); src/data/message_cache/outbox.rs:122-133
kept.what_this_is: flush_outbox is the send loop. Each call spawns a task that reads every ready row in the Outbox, sends each one over SMTP, and deletes the row only after the send returns (24701).
kept.problem: Nothing stops a second pass while the first is still running, and reading a row does not claim it. A second pass reads rows the first pass is still sending. Each send builds a fresh Message-ID (src/service/protocols/smtp.rs:152), so recipients get two separate messages and Sent gets two copies.
kept.concrete_case: Undo Send hold set to 0. Send message A with a 15 MB attachment; the upload takes 30 seconds. Ten seconds later send message B from a second composer; its Send calls flush_outbox (19319). Pass 2 reads A (its row is still there) and B, and A goes out twice. The same happens with holds on: two held messages whose holds end a few seconds apart start two passes from the 1-second tick (6518-6535). Pressing Send Queued Mail twice does it too.
kept.fix: A process-wide `static SENDING: AtomicBool` and `static AGAIN: AtomicBool`. At the top of flush_outbox: if `SENDING.swap(true)` then `AGAIN.store(true)` and return. At the end of the task, run the pass again while `AGAIN.swap(false)`, then clear SENDING. About 10 lines, no schema change. One test: two calls against a stub whose first send blocks, asserting one send per row.
kept.if_skipped: People receive duplicate mail that cannot be taken back, and Sent holds both copies.
kept.ledger_entry: None. Searched .planning/WINDOWS.md for flush_outbox, 'twice' and 'second pass'.

verdict.reason:
I read the code and the race is there. flush_outbox (src/presentation/wx_app.rs:24529) spawns a task. That task reads every ready row (24590, through outbox_messages_that_may_go_now at outbox.rs:122-133, which only filters on time and claims nothing), signs in to IMAP for the Sent copy (24663), sends, and deletes the row only after the send returns (24701). Nothing holds a second pass back. I grepped src for a flag or lock: OutboxFlushComplete (23704) only updates the status line, ID_FLUSH_OUTBOX is never disabled, and MessageCache uses busy_timeout and takes no exclusive lock. All six callers are as the finding lists them.

The case happens with the default 10-second hold:
- Message A's hold ends at t=10, and the 1-second tick (6518-6535) starts pass 1, which reads [A].
- Message B, sent 3 seconds after A, comes due at t=13, and `anything_reached_its_moment` starts pass 2. Each row triggers its own pass when its moment comes.
- Pass 1 is still signing in to IMAP, so A's row is still there. Pass 2 reads [A, B], and A goes out twice. Both passes also file a Sent copy (24723-24736).

Pressing Send Queued Mail during a pass does the same, and so does a failed row being retried by every trigger, which ledger 720 widened to every account.

One part of the finding is wrong. Queued mail does not get a fresh Message-ID. mail_controller.rs:248 uses message_id::derived(queue_id, from), so both copies carry the same ID; smtp.rs:152 is Email::simple, which the queue path does not use. The SMTP server still delivers twice. Gmail may fold the two copies into one; Outlook and Thunderbird show both, and Sent gets two copies.

There is no ledger entry. I searched .planning/WINDOWS.md for flush_outbox, twice, second pass and concurrent, and read every line about the Outbox; none is about this.

The proposed AtomicBool pair is not the smallest safe fix:
- A request that arrives between the final AGAIN check and clearing SENDING is lost.
- A panic inside the task leaves SENDING set, and no mail sends again until restart.
- The task has five early returns, and every one of them would have to clear the flag.

A tokio Mutex (tokio has "full" features, so const_new works) avoids all three.
verdict.corrected_problem: Nothing stops a second Outbox pass while one is running, and reading a row does not claim it. A second pass reads the rows the first is still sending, because the first deletes each row only after its send returns (wx_app.rs:24701). Both passes then send the row and file a Sent copy. Both copies carry the same Message-ID, derived from the queue row (mail_controller.rs:248), but SMTP still delivers both. Some clients, such as Gmail, may fold them into one; Outlook and Thunderbird show both, and Sent holds two copies. This happens with the default 10-second hold when two messages come due a few seconds apart: each due row starts its own pass on the 1-second tick (6518-6535), and a pass spends seconds signing in to IMAP and SMTP before it deletes anything. Pressing Send Queued Mail while a pass is running does the same.
verdict.corrected_fix: Make the passes run one at a time. Add `static ONE_PASS_AT_A_TIME: tokio::sync::Mutex<()> = tokio::sync::Mutex::const_new(());` and make `let _one_pass = ONE_PASS_AT_A_TIME.lock().await;` the first line inside the spawned task, before the queue is read at 24590. A second pass then waits, reads the queue after the first has deleted what it sent, and finds only what is still due. The lock is released on all five early returns and on a panic, and no request is lost. That is about 3 lines and needs no schema change. For the test, give the lock to a small helper that the pass goes through. Run two concurrent passes over one queued row against the loopback SMTP server already in the tree (smtp::against_a_server_that_answers). Assert that the server received one DATA command and that the row is gone. Without the lock the test should fail with two.

kept.title: Announcements made close together overwrite each other, so only the last one is heard
kept.location: src/presentation/accessibility.rs:347-398 (every announce* flushes at once) and 435-468 (flush_announcements delivers each line separately); src/presentation/accessibility/screen_reader.rs:120-134, 600-608; src/presentation/wx_app.rs:6392-6420
kept.what_this_is: Every announcement ends as SetWindowTextW on one hidden static control plus EVENT_OBJECT_LIVEREGIONCHANGED. The queue releases up to 4 lines a second plus every Urgent line, and every announce call flushes at once. The tick drains all pending UI updates in one go, and many arms announce.
kept.problem: Lines released together are written to the same window microseconds apart. The screen reader reads the window's name when it handles the event, so it reads the last text. The code already knows this: handed_over_together (screen_reader.rs:448-484) joins held lines for exactly this reason, and docs/changelog.md:9676 says 'several status sentences in a row leave only the last one heard'. The join was applied to the startup hold and to one Calendar window, not to the path every other announcement takes. The Urgent/Important mapping is also ignored on this path; it only reaches the notification API, which is skipped when the live region works. The unit tests count lines released to the bridge, so they stay green while a person hears one line.
kept.concrete_case: A POP account with a wrong SMTP password. flush_outbox sends OutboxSendResult (failure with the server's reason), ConnectionStatusChanged(Error) and OutboxFlushComplete back to back with no network wait between them (24743-24779). The next 50 ms tick drains all three, each arm announces, and the window text ends as 'The Outbox is done: 0 sent, 1 not sent.' The reason the mail did not go is never spoken. The same happens at the end of a check, where WhatArrived and the closing updates arrive in the same instant.
kept.fix: Deliver at most one live-region write per flush: in flush_announcements, join what drain released with the existing handed_over_together (most urgent wins) and call deliver once. During the tick's drain loop, queue only, then flush once after the loop (a hold flag on Accessibility that announce* checks before flushing). About 15 lines. Test: two announcements in one tick reach the bridge as one joined line.
kept.if_skipped: The product's main channel drops a line whenever two things happen at once, and the one dropped is usually the more important first line.
kept.ledger_entry: None. The symptom is recorded only in docs/changelog.md:9676, fixed for the Calendar window alone.

verdict.reason:
I confirmed this from the code, line by line. Every announce, announce_topic, announce_what_was_typed and announce_content call flushes straight away (accessibility.rs:347-398). flush_announcements sends each released line to announce_with on its own (435-468). deliver returns once announce_via_live_region has run (screen_reader.rs:600-608), and that function is SetWindowTextW on one control followed by EVENT_OBJECT_LIVEREGIONCHANGED (120-134). Urgency only reaches the notification path, which is skipped whenever the live region works.

The tick runs every queued update in one synchronous loop (wx_app.rs:6392-6415). Nothing joins the lines in between, so each write replaces the last before the screen reader reads the control's name. The code says this happens: the comment on handed_over_together (screen_reader.rs:448-454) and commit 1c46a214 both state that lines handed over one after another overwrite each other. The join was only ever applied to the startup hold.

The concrete case checks out. On a send failure, flush_outbox (24743-24779) sends four updates back to back: OutboxSendResult, ConnectionStatusChanged(Error), OutboxFlushComplete and OutboxQueueCount. For a POP account, nothing in that stretch should need the network. The first arm signals SendFailed, which is Urgent and spoken by default (feedback.rs:280, 655-660), so "Message not sent: <reason>" is written to the control. The second signals ConnectionLost (ui_types.rs:281-283), writing "Disconnected". The third announces "The Outbox is done: 0 sent, 1 not sent." at Normal priority; the rate limit has budget left (4 - 2), so it is written straight away. The last write wins, and the reason is never spoken.

The tests count lines handed to the bridge, so they stay green. test_flush_announcements_priority_order (accessibility.rs:1050) asserts three separate lines and so pins the current behaviour. Nothing in .planning/WINDOWS.md records this. The ledger searches for live region, overwrite, "in a row", the rate limit and the join found nothing.
verdict.corrected_problem:
Lines released close together are written to the same live-region control a few microseconds apart. The screen reader reads the control's name after the UI thread returns, so only the last line is heard. The Urgent and Important markings never reach that path.

Two corrections to the finding:

1. docs/changelog.md:9676 and commit 7b34ef86 blame the Calendar-window symptom on topic superseding in the queue, not on this overwrite. The finding's claim that "the code already knows this" rests on the handed_over_together comment and commit 1c46a214, not on the changelog line.

2. The visual channel loses the reason in the same case. signal() keeps only the latest shown line, so after the tick the status bar shows "Disconnected", not the failure reason.

The tick-level hold proposed below also leaves one case uncovered: a single event handler outside the tick that announces twice in a row.
verdict.corrected_fix:
1. In Accessibility::flush_announcements, join everything drain() released into one line, most urgent first, then call announce_with once. Use the most urgent priority among the lines and no topic, as handed_over_together does. Either make that join callable from accessibility.rs or repeat it over Spoken. Keep the per-line log calls.

2. Add a hold flag to Accessibility. While it is set, the announce* functions push to the queue and skip the flush. In the tick closure in wx_app.rs, set the flag before the ui_rx.try_recv loop and clear it after. The flush_announcements call already sitting at line 6420 then releases a single joined line.

Write the failing test first: two announcements made while the hold is set reach the bridge as one joined line. Change test_flush_announcements_priority_order to expect one line, "urgent. high. normal", and re-measure every guard record that names it.

That is roughly 20 lines.

kept.title: Removing or disabling an account leaves its inbox watch running
kept.location: src/presentation/wx_app.rs:22153-22237 (handle_account_mgr), 24160-24185 (MailboxChanged arm), 27840-27859 (spawn_mail_watch), 30423-30426
kept.what_this_is: Each IMAP account has an IDLE watch on a connection of its own, kept in WxUIState.mail_watches. A watch is only ever stopped when a new watch for the same account replaces it (27853-27858).
kept.problem: handle_account_mgr signs off a removed account's held session (22229-22234, under a comment saying an account that has gone is signed out of) but never touches mail_watches, and does nothing at all for an account switched to disabled. The MailboxChanged arm picks accounts by id only, not by enabled, and a check that ends asks for a new watch (30808).
kept.concrete_case: (a) Disable account B in the Account Manager. Its watch keeps its connection. When mail arrives for B, the watch sends MailboxChanged, spawn_mail_sync checks B (rules run, moves and deletes go to the server, the unattended Trash empty runs), then asks for a new watch, so B keeps being checked for the rest of the session. (b) Remove account C. Its watch stays connected. When C's inbox changes, the woken list is empty and spawn_mail_sync says 'Error: Add an account before checking for mail' at High priority, although other accounts exist.
kept.fix: In handle_account_mgr, for each id that was removed or is now disabled, `mail_watches.remove(id)` and `rt.spawn(handle.stop())` on its handle. In the MailboxChanged arm, add `&& account.enabled` to the filter. About 10 lines.
kept.if_skipped: Switching an account off does not switch it off until restart, and removing one produces a false error read aloud.
kept.ledger_entry: None.

verdict.reason:
I checked every cited line and the bug is real. I put it at should rather than must because it lasts only until restart, loses no data, and everything it does at the server is something the person set up: their own queued moves, flags and rules.

- handle_account_mgr (22153-22237) signs off the held session of a removed account and never touches mail_watches. It does nothing at all for an account whose "Enable this account" box was unticked (wx_account_manager.rs:2261).
- The watch runs on its own connection, opened by watch_folder (mail_sync.rs:2060). no_longer_signed_in_to only closes sessions in the held-session map, so it never reaches the watch.
- The MailboxChanged arm (24173-24178) matches on id only. spawn_mail_sync never checks enabled, and at 30808 it asks for a new watch.
- spawn_mail_watch (27848) never checks enabled either. start_the_watches_whose_wait_is_over (27712) re-arms a disabled account's watch after a dropped connection. The only enabled filters are in the schedule (which_are_due), in watch_every_enabled_account and in the download.

Case (a): a disabled account goes on being watched and checked for the rest of the session. Each check replays its waiting moves, deletes and flag changes, and runs its rules.

Case (b): when a removed account's inbox changes, woken is empty. spawn_mail_sync then fails with "Add an account before checking for mail", and the ErrorOccurred arm (23164) announces it at High priority. The watch's connection to the removed account's server stays open until it wakes or drops.

Not in .planning/WINDOWS.md, and no test covers it.

Two corrections:
1. The unattended Trash empty does not run on a watch wake. It is gated by `if only.is_none()` at 30729.
2. The proposed fix is incomplete. A check already running when the account is disabled still ends by asking for a watch (30808). A failed watch's wait also re-arms it through start_the_watches_whose_wait_is_over. Both reach spawn_mail_watch, which has no enabled check, so the watch comes back.

Stopping the old watch is safe. stop() ends with "the watch was stopped", and whether_to_watch_again answers Never for that, so nothing re-arms it.
verdict.corrected_problem:
The Account Manager never stops the inbox watch of an account that was removed or switched off. Nothing that starts a watch checks enabled: spawn_mail_watch (27848), the MailboxChanged arm (24173-24178) and the watch request at the end of every check (30808) all go ahead for a disabled account.

A disabled account stays watched and checked until restart. Each wake replays its waiting moves, deletes and flag changes and runs its rules. The Trash empty does not run on a wake, because a check of one folder skips it (30729).

A removed account keeps its watch connection open. If its inbox changes, the woken list is empty and spawn_mail_sync announces "Error: Add an account before checking for mail" at High priority.
verdict.corrected_fix:
Three changes:

1. In handle_account_mgr, before the sign-off loop, take out the mail_watches entry for each id that was removed or is now disabled, and stop its handle with `rt.spawn(async move { let _ = handle.stop().await; })`. A stop ends with "the watch was stopped", which whether_to_watch_again answers with Never, so nothing re-arms it.
2. In spawn_mail_watch at 27848, change the lookup to `find(|a| a.id == account_id && a.enabled)`. This covers a check that was already running and the retry after a failed watch.
3. In the MailboxChanged arm, add `&& account.enabled` to the filter, and return without calling spawn_mail_sync when woken is empty. That removes the false "Add an account" error.

About 12 lines. Pull the "removed or now disabled ids" calculation out as a pure function beside added_in_this_visit, so the failing test comes first.

kept.title: Empty Folder says a server folder was emptied when the server only marked or copied the messages
kept.location: src/presentation/wx_app.rs:10250-10269 (spawn_the_folder_empty); src/service/protocols/imap.rs:1648-1675; src/application/server_delete.rs:62-66
kept.what_this_is: Empty Folder on a server folder loops over every UID and calls delete_message, which returns a Deletion naming what really happened: Removed, MovedToTrash, CopiedToTrashAndFlagged, CopiedToTrashAndNotFlagged or MarkedOnly.
kept.problem: The loop checks only Err. Any Ok counts as done, so MarkedOnly (no UIDPLUS, or UID EXPUNGE refused) and CopiedToTrashAndNotFlagged (copy made, original left) are reported as emptied. The single-message delete reads the same value correctly (server_delete.rs:62-66). It is also one STORE plus one UID EXPUNGE round trip per message, so a 10,000-message Trash is about 20,000 round trips.
kept.concrete_case: Empty Trash on a server without UIDPLUS: every message gets \Deleted and stays, the window says 'Emptied Trash.', and the next check lists them all again. Empty Archive on a server without MOVE where STORE is refused: every message is copied into Trash and stays in Archive, the sentence says it was emptied, and running it again copies everything into Trash a second time.
kept.fix: Match the outcome: Removed and MovedToTrash count as done; any other variant stops that folder with its reason in StoppedAt, as an Err does now. About 8 lines, plus one test with a stub mailbox that answers MarkedOnly.
kept.if_skipped: People believe mail is gone or moved when it is not, and duplicates pile up in Trash.
kept.ledger_entry: None. Ledger 190 covers only remove_these's wording, which is why this path deletes one message at a time.

verdict.reason:
I read the code and the finding holds. In src/presentation/wx_app.rs:10250-10258, spawn_the_folder_empty only tests `if let Err(why)` on `controller.delete_message(...)`. MailController::delete_message (src/application/mail_controller.rs:696) returns Result<Deletion>, and ImapSession::delete_message (src/service/protocols/imap.rs:1648-1675) returns three kinds of Ok that leave the message in the folder:
- MarkedOnly: no UIDPLUS, or UID EXPUNGE refused, with trash None (emptying the Trash).
- CopiedToTrashAndFlagged: no MOVE, then no UIDPLUS or expunge refused (move_message :1479-1492).
- CopiedToTrashAndNotFlagged: no MOVE and STORE refused.

All three count as done, so the folder lands in got.done and what_emptying_did says "Emptied Trash." (how_far_it_got.rs:70-80). Nothing checks abilities before the dialog (wx_app.rs:10030-10142), and no test reaches spawn_the_folder_empty.

The single delete does read the outcome: server_delete::after_a_delete speaks Deletion::spoken(), including "Trying again would make a second copy."

list_uids searches ALL (imap.rs:1174), so flagged messages are listed again. On a server with neither MOVE nor UIDPLUS (hMailServer, for example), a second Empty Archive copies every message into Trash again. That contradicts the function's own comment, "Running it again finishes the job", and the changelog's "Running it again finishes the job" (changelog.md:6602).

The ledger does not cover this:
- Ledger 772 is the waiting-replay path (moves_waiting delete_it), used by the Trash-emptying setting and by Delete inside the Trash. It does not cover Empty Folder, which calls the controller directly.
- Ledger 190 is only about remove_these's wording.

Why should rather than must: Gmail, Outlook.com, Yahoo, iCloud, Fastmail and Dovecot all advertise UIDPLUS, and all but iCloud advertise MOVE too (iCloud's copy, flag and expunge path still ends as moved). So the fault shows only on less common servers or when the server refuses the command.

Two parts of the finding are overstated:
- "The next check lists them all again" is loose. The sync stores \Deleted on the row (messages.rs:2047), so the messages come back marked deleted, not as fresh mail. What is wrong is the sentence, and that the server still holds them.
- The 20,000 round trips claim is accurate, but one message at a time is a choice the code's own comment records (to avoid remove_these's refusal wording). It is not part of this fix.
verdict.corrected_problem:
Empty Folder at a server reports a folder as emptied whenever every delete_message call returned Ok. That includes Deletion::MarkedOnly (no UIDPLUS, or UID EXPUNGE refused), CopiedToTrashAndFlagged (no MOVE, then no UIDPLUS or expunge refused) and CopiedToTrashAndNotFlagged (no MOVE, STORE refused). In all three the message is still in the folder. The single delete reads the same value and says what happened (server_delete.rs:57-72). Empty Folder throws it away, says "Emptied Trash." or "Emptied Archive.", and ends as CommandAnswered.

list_uids asks the server for ALL, which includes messages flagged \Deleted. So on a server with neither MOVE nor UIDPLUS, running Empty Archive again copies every message into Trash a second time. That contradicts "Running it again finishes the job" in the function's comment and in the changelog.
verdict.corrected_fix:
Put the decision in application::emptying as a pure function over &Deletion, for example a function returning Result<(), String>:
- Removed and MovedToTrash are Ok.
- Every other variant is Err(deletion.spoken()).
- Write the match out in full, with no wildcard arm, so a new variant forces a decision here.

In the spawn_the_folder_empty loop, turn the delete's Ok value into that result. A message that is still there then stops that folder with its reason in StoppedAt, the same way an Err does now. left_behind stays uids.len() - done, which correctly counts the message that is still there.

Test the pure function over every Deletion variant. It needs no stub mailbox, because the loop is inside a closure holding a concrete MailController.

Expect this result: on a server without UIDPLUS, Empty Trash stops at the first message and says why ("Marked for removal, and still in this folder, because ..."), where it now claims success.

Leave out the round-trip cost and any batching. They are a separate, deliberate trade-off.

kept.title: Sending a draft leaves its copy in the Drafts folder, here and on the server
kept.location: src/presentation/wx_app.rs:19292-19298 (Send removes only the drafts table row), 19436-19505 (every save files a copy), 24329-24352 (Undo Send's too-late path); src/data/message_cache/drafts.rs:110-116; docs/changelog.md:8510-8513
kept.what_this_is: save_as_draft writes the drafts table row and also files a copy in the account's Drafts folder: on the IMAP server through spawn_draft_append, or as a message row in the local Drafts folder for POP. Autosave does this every few minutes.
kept.problem: After Send, only cache.delete_draft(id) runs, which is DELETE FROM drafts. Nothing removes the filed copy (git grep finds no caller that removes it). The changelog says 'A draft is removed once its message has been sent', which is true only for the Open Draft list. Undo Send's too-late branch deletes the drafts row because 'Left in Drafts it would be sent a second time by whoever found it', but the filed copy save_as_draft just made stays.
kept.concrete_case: Write a reply on an IMAP account for five minutes, so autosave files it in the server's Drafts, then press Send. The message goes, and the Drafts folder on the phone, and in this program after the next check, still shows it as an unsent draft. On a POP account the local Drafts row stays for ever.
kept.fix: After a successful queue (19292) and in undo_send's Ok(false) branch, remove the filed copy by its Message-ID (draft_message::message_id_for(id)): for IMAP, a spawned task using the existing KeepsTheDraft copies_already_there then remove_these; for a local Drafts folder, delete the row with that message_id. About 20 lines. Run it on the same account session after any append still in flight, or a late autosave lands after the removal.
kept.if_skipped: Every message that was saved before it was sent stays in Drafts on every device, and somebody may send it again.
kept.ledger_entry: None. docs/changelog.md:8510 claims it was fixed.

verdict.reason:
I read every line the finding cites, and it holds.

- **Where the copy comes from.** `save_as_draft` (wx_app.rs:19436-19445) saves the drafts-table row and then calls `file_draft_copy`. On a POP account, `file_draft_copy` writes a message row into the local Drafts folder (`replace_local_draft`, 19474-19489). On an IMAP account it calls `spawn_draft_append` (19505), which puts a copy in the server's Drafts folder.
- **When it happens.** Autosave runs the same save (19235). It is on by default every 2 minutes (`autosave.rs:67-76`), so any message written for more than 2 minutes has a filed copy.
- **What Send does.** After a successful queue, the Send arm runs only `cache.delete_draft(id)` (19292-19297), and `drafts.rs:110-116` shows that is `DELETE FROM drafts`. No production code removes the filed copy:
  - `MailController::remove_by_message_id` (mail_controller.rs:739) exists, but only tests call it.
  - `message_id_for` has no production caller apart from the two filing paths.
  - Nothing under `FolderType::Drafts` in the send code removes anything.
- **Undo Send's too-late branch.** At 24329 it calls `save_as_draft(..., None)`, which files a fresh copy (on IMAP, an append spawned in that same call). On `Ok(false)` or an error it deletes only the drafts row (24343), so the copy of an already-sent message stays in Drafts. That is exactly the double-send its own comment warns about.
- **The changelog and the test.** `docs/changelog.md:8510-8513` claims the draft is removed once sent, but that is true only of the Open Draft list. The guard `tests/wired.rs:1425` is a source-text check that asserts only that `delete_draft` appears after `queue_for_sending`, so it cannot see this.
- **Ledger.** No entry in `.planning/WINDOWS.md` covers it. The only nearby entry, 190, is about the refusal wording of `remove_these`.

**Why must:** this hits the ordinary path, every message written for more than two minutes. It shows on every device and in Gmail's Drafts, it would be seen right away in the phase 14 real-account sittings, and the changelog says it was fixed.

**Correction to the proposed fix:** in Undo Send, removing the copy after the fact would race the append spawned a moment earlier. Filing later avoids that.
verdict.corrected_problem:
Send removes only the drafts-table row (wx_app.rs:19292-19297, `DELETE FROM drafts`). The copy that every save and every 2-minute autosave files does not go away: it is a local Drafts message row on POP, or a server Drafts message on IMAP via `spawn_draft_append`. `MailController::remove_by_message_id` exists, but only tests call it.

Undo Send's too-late branch (24337-24352) has the same gap. `save_as_draft` has just filed a fresh copy, an append spawned in that same call on IMAP. Only the drafts row is deleted, so a copy of a message that has already gone stays in Drafts. That is the double-send its own comment warns about.

`docs/changelog.md:8510` claims the draft is removed once sent. The `tests/wired.rs:1425` guard only checks the source text for `delete_draft`, so it cannot see this. Not in the ledger.
verdict.corrected_fix:
1. **Send path.** At wx_app.rs:19292, after `delete_draft`, take away the filed copy whose Message-ID is `draft_message::message_id_for(id)`:
   - **Local Drafts folder (POP):** look up the folder row, find the message with `message_uid_by_message_id`, and delete that row.
   - **IMAP:** use `spawn_blocking` with `mail_session::a_session_at(&account)`, the same shape as `spawn_draft_append`, and call the existing, currently unused `MailController::remove_by_message_id(drafts_folder, &message_id)`. That keeps it under the account's Allow Changes gate. Report a failure in a status line rather than staying silent.
2. **Undo Send.** Do not remove anything afterwards; reorder instead. Save only the drafts row first, which means splitting `save_as_draft` so `file_draft_copy` can be called separately. Call `file_draft_copy` only after `delete_outbox_message` returns `Ok(true)`. The too-late branch then has no copy to clean up, and nothing races the append.
3. **Remaining race.** An autosave append still running on its own session can land after the Send-path removal. Either say so, or have the removal re-search once after a short delay.
4. **Tests and docs.** Write the failing test first: a cache-level test for the local copy and a `KeepsTheDraft`-style scripted test for the IMAP removal. Correct `docs/changelog.md:8510` in the same commit.

About 25 to 30 lines.

kept.title: The download of everything re-reads the whole open folder on the UI thread after every chunk

kept.problem: Each re-read costs the size of the folder on the UI thread and runs once per chunk, so total work grows with the square of the folder size. Ledger 58 measured the conversation listing alone at about 0.75 to 1.2 seconds for 200,000 rows. In flat view every reload also speaks 'N messages, M unread' at Normal (23012-23016), whatever the Say level is set to.
kept.concrete_case: First run on an account whose Inbox holds 100,000 messages, with the Inbox open: 200 chunks. Near the end each chunk freezes the window for about a second (no keys, nothing spoken), every few seconds, for the whole download. In flat view the count is spoken about 200 times over whatever the person is reading.
kept.fix: The MoreOfTheFolderArrived arm only marks the open folder stale; the tick re-reads a stale open folder at most once every 10 seconds (one Instant in state), and a background re-read does not announce the count. About 12 lines. Moving the Vec out of MessagesLoaded instead of cloning it (22945) also halves the copy.
kept.if_skipped: The window is close to unusable during the first download, which is when a new user first tries it.
kept.ledger_entry: Ledger 523 expects one sentence per download and does not know about the per-chunk count line; ledger 58 measured the listing cost but not its repetition.

verdict.reason:
I read every link in the chain and it holds. The download runner sends MoreOfTheFolderArrived after each chunk of 500 headers (wx_app.rs:30026, INITIAL_FETCH_LIMIT = 500 at mail_sync.rs:49). Its arm (24189-24198) calls reread_folder_if_open. That function (22686-22709) runs load_folder_messages on the UI thread: the sorted read of the whole folder, the threading and the labels (17664-17671). In conversation view, which has been the default since #92 (config.rs:846), it also runs load_folder_conversations (17805). Updates are handled inside the 50 ms timer (6392), so all of this runs on the UI thread. Nothing coalesces or throttles it, and the only tests (everything_comes_down_without_being_asked.rs:602) require the arm to re-read on every chunk.

measurements.md:184-187 puts the three message steps at 817 ms for 200,000 rows and 39 ms for the tester's 12,872. Ledger 58 puts the conversation listing at 0.75 to 1.2 s for 200,000. Each chunk costs time in proportion to the rows already held, so the total grows with the square of the folder size. Near the end of a 100,000-message folder in conversation view, the freeze per chunk comes to roughly 0.8 to 1 s.

In flat view, the MessagesLoaded arm (23012-23016) calls announce_topic("N messages, M unread", Normal) with no check on HowMuchToSay. The queue (announcements.rs:22-26, 187-197, 270-306) merges lines on one topic only while one is still waiting. It speaks up to 4 a second, and chunks arrive seconds apart, so every chunk is spoken. That is about 26 times for the tester's own folder, so the flood is not limited to big folders.

Neither problem is in the ledger. Ledger 523 expects one sentence at the end of the download under "Say what arrived" and does not know about this line. Ledger 58 measured one listing, not that it repeats per chunk. Ledgers 449, 522 and 564 cover other things.

Corrections to the finding:
- The freeze only matters for folders of roughly 50,000 messages or more. The tester's folder pays about 40 to 90 ms per chunk.
- The spoken flood needs flat view, which is not the default. It happens at any folder size.
- "Move the Vec out instead of cloning" is not a small change. handle_update takes &UIUpdate (22793), so moving it means changing the signature that every arm uses. Drop that part.
- "About 12 lines" leaves out three things the fix has to touch: the test that requires reread_folder_if_open( in the arm, the guard record anchored on that arm (guards.toml:4822-4836), and a way to tell MessagesLoaded that a re-read came from a chunk, because FolderMessagesArrived shares the same path.

It is "should" rather than "must": the default view says nothing per chunk, and the freeze only bites on large folders. It breaks guardrail 5 (bounded feedback while a mailbox syncs), and new users with large Gmail inboxes will hit it on first run.
verdict.corrected_problem: During the download of everything, each chunk of 500 headers that lands in the open folder makes the UI thread re-read the whole folder: messages, threading and labels, plus the conversation listing in conversation view (the default). The total work therefore grows with the square of the folder size. Measured costs (817 ms of message steps at 200,000 rows, conversation listing 0.75 to 1.2 s at 200,000) give freezes of roughly 0.8 to 1 s per chunk near the end of a 100,000-message folder in conversation view. A 12,872-message folder pays about 40 to 90 ms, which nobody notices. Separately, in flat view every re-read speaks "N messages, M unread" at Normal with no check on the Say level. That is once per chunk at any folder size, about 26 times for the tester's folder, against ledger 523's expectation of one sentence at the end.
verdict.corrected_fix:
Throttle the re-read on the UI side:
1. MoreOfTheFolderArrived records the folder id as stale in WxUIState and keeps an Instant of the last chunk re-read.
2. The timer tick calls reread_folder_if_open for a stale folder when 10 s have passed since the last re-read, then clears the mark.
3. Because the mark survives until the tick takes it, the folder still gets a last re-read after the final chunk or a pause.
4. Give MessagesLoaded a reason, the way ConversationsLoaded already has WhyTheRowsWereRead, so a re-read caused by a chunk does not speak the count. FolderMessagesArrived and opening a folder keep speaking it.

Change test_a_chunk_arriving_rereads_the_folder_and_grows_no_limit to accept the stale mark instead of a direct reread_folder_if_open( in the arm. Rewrite and re-measure the guard record "a chunk of the download that lands is shown, and no limit grows" in the same commit. Leave out the clone-to-move idea, because handle_update borrows the update. Expect roughly 30 to 40 lines including tests, not 12.

verdict.reason:
I checked each claim against the code and they hold. That includes `announce_content`, which `wire_read_aloud` (wx_app.rs:12216) calls with the whole text of a reading. For mail that text comes from `read_the_whole_message` (wx_app.rs:4015). There is one long-lived `Arc<Accessibility>` per process (wx_app.rs:1012), so the log lasts until exit. The rate limit of 4 a second slows the growth but does not bound it.

Nothing in production reads the log. Outside `#[cfg(test)]` code, `ScreenReaderBridge::events()` has no caller in src, tests or scripts. The same is true of `automation_snapshot`, `update_node_state`, `live_region_update`, `FocusManager::current_focus` and `KeyboardHandler::action_for_key`. `initialize`'s own comment at lines 71-74 says nothing reads the shortcut map. `Accessibility::set_focus` does have one production call: `initialize` calls `set_focus("folder_tree")` before any window exists, and the startup handover then says "Focus moved to Folders", a line built from this model and not from where Windows put focus.

Add a second case for the one-line red form.

verdict.reason:
I checked each claim against the code and they hold. release.yml:52-53 checks out with no fetch-depth, which gives one commit, and other-platforms.yml:86-87 and 164-165 do the same. All three jobs then run cargo test. Cargo.toml has no autotests or [[test]] override, so a plain `cargo test --quiet` runs the integration tests too. The history test is a plain #[test] at every_number_carries_its_command_and_its_date.rs:1491. On a shallow clone, `rev-parse --git-dir` succeeds, so the test does not take the NoHistoryHere branch. `merge-base --is-ancestor 18a02454 HEAD` then fails, and line 1492 panics. The project chose that behaviour on purpose in 1336-1338 and 1482-1488, so the checkout depth is the thing to fix, not the test.

The guard at house_style.rs:4665 reads only ci.yml. Ledger 464, still open, says the fix added "a reading that holds every job running cargo test to it", which claims more than the guard does. Ledger 616, also open, covers only the missing WIXEN_NO_AUDIO. No ledger entry, STATE line or ROADMAP line records the shallow checkout in release.yml or other-platforms.yml. The repository has no tags, so release.yml has never got past this point. Widening the guard to every workflow is cheap: accessibility.yml and nvda.yml only run cargo build, and guards.yml and mutants.yml already set fetch-depth 0. The only new names it would flag are quality-gate, linux and macos.

One correction to the concrete case. With no --no-fail-fast and no WIXEN_NO_AUDIO, the release gate today probably dies first on the audio fault in the library tests, which is ledger 616. The history panic is the second failure, and it will still stop every release after 616 is fixed. For other-platforms, the history panic is the first certain failure, because that workflow already sets WIXEN_NO_AUDIO.
verdict.corrected_problem: Three jobs run the test suite on a one-commit checkout: release.yml's quality-gate, and other-platforms.yml's linux and macos jobs. On such a checkout test_the_share_of_history_before_red_green_is_computed_and_printed panics with "18a02454 is not in this history". The release gate fails today on the missing WIXEN_NO_AUDIO (ledger 616, open and waiting on Pratik). Once that is settled, it would still fail on the history test, and that second failure is recorded nowhere. Both other-platforms jobs already set WIXEN_NO_AUDIO, so they go red on the history test for a reason unrelated to the platform, which muddies SHIP-05's question. The guard test_every_job_that_runs_the_tests_checks_out_the_whole_history (house_style.rs:4665) reads only ci.yml, so it sees none of these jobs. Ledger 464 describes that guard as covering every job that runs cargo test, which is more than it does.

2. In house_style.rs:4665, loop over every *.yml file in .github/workflows instead of ci.yml alone, and prefix each complaint with the file name. Only the three jobs above will be newly named. This is the red half of the change.
