kept.title: The hook decides on the staged files but builds and tests the working tree, so a commit can pass while its own snapshot is broken
kept.location: scripts/check.sh:282-284 and 646-655 (mode and scope taken from git diff --cached) against 714-720 and 875-935 (cargo fmt, clippy and test run over the working tree); .githooks/commit-msg:53-54
kept.what_this_is: The commit-msg hook runs check.sh, which works out from the index what the commit changes and then runs cargo over the files on disk.
kept.problem: Nothing stashes or refuses unstaged changes, so what is tested is the index plus whatever is unstaged. A file left out of git add, or a partial commit (git commit -- path), is tested together with code the commit does not contain. The comment at 646-648 says the scope is staged 'because that is what the hook is deciding about', but cargo never sees the staged version.
kept.concrete_case: A green commit stages src/application/a.rs, which calls a new helper, and forgets src/application/b.rs, which defines it. The working tree compiles and the scoped tests pass, so the commit is accepted. The committed tree does not compile, and the branch now holds a 'green' commit that is not one. The same thing at a merge: with unrelated unstaged edits under src/ in the checkout, the merge commit's run tests those edits plus the merge result, and can pass while the merge result on its own fails.
kept.fix: In check.sh, when --message-file is given, refuse before rustfmt if git diff --quiet -- src tests build.rs Cargo.toml Cargo.lock fails (that compares the working tree with the index the hook was handed, including a partial commit's temporary index), with a line telling the person to stage the files or run git stash --keep-index first. About six lines.
kept.if_skipped: Red/green evidence in the history can be wrong in both directions, bisects meet commits that never built, and a merge made from a dirty checkout can land a broken main that only the phase-close gate or CI sees.

verdict.reason:
The finding is real. I checked each claim against the lines.

- **Scope comes from the index.** `the_staged_paths` (check.sh:282-284) runs `git diff --cached`, and `decide_the_mode_for_this_commit` (397-399) and the shell-suite reading (545) both take it.
- **Cargo runs over the files on disk.** `touch src/lib.rs`, `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy` (714-720) and every scoped `cargo test` (875-935) build from the working tree. The hook (commit-msg:53-54) just runs check.sh with the message file.
- **Nothing refuses or stashes unstaged work.** A grep of `scripts/` for stash, `diff --quiet` and unstaged found nothing in check.sh. The only refusal of a dirty tree is in `build-installer.sh`.

The case happens in practice. Executors already work around the false-refusal direction by hand:
- 13-08-SUMMARY:188 says "the hook tests the working tree".
- 13-44.1-SUMMARY:143 says a green commit was refused because unstaged readings were counted.
- 14-03-SUMMARY:172 records a 344 s refusal because house_style read an unstaged page.
- 12-03.2-PLAN:1713 (T-12-03.2-09) handles the same threat for scripts with a manual `git status --porcelain` before each commit.

The false-pass direction is not recorded anywhere. A green commit can leave out a file the build needs and still pass. A merge commit made from a dirty checkout tests edits the merge does not contain. The only open ledger entry nearby is WINDOWS.md 325, about one guard reading planning files from disk. It is narrower, and it raises "whether a tree guard should read the index rather than the disk" without settling it. So the ledger understates this.

It is "should", not "must". It needs a missed `git add`, a partial commit or a dirty tree. CI on push and the phase-close `check.sh all` catch the branch tip, but not the commits in between.

The proposed fix has one gap. `git diff --quiet` compares the working tree with the index and does not see untracked files. The most common missed add is a new file: the parent's `mod b;` is staged, `b.rs` is untracked, the working tree compiles and the commit does not. The pathspec also leaves out `locales/`, which is compiled in through `include_str!`, and `scripts/` and `.githooks/`, which run the gate itself.
verdict.corrected_problem: check.sh picks the mode and scope from the index (the_staged_paths, 282-284; decide_the_mode_for_this_commit, 397-399). It then runs rustfmt, clippy and every cargo test over the working tree (714-720, 875-935), and nothing stashes or refuses what the index does not hold. So under the hook, cargo tests the index plus any unstaged changes and untracked files. This includes the temporary index of a partial commit, and a merge commit made from a dirty checkout. A commit can pass while its own snapshot does not build, and it can be refused over work it does not contain. The refusal direction is already worked around by hand (13-08, 13-44.1 and 14-03 summaries; a manual check in 12-03.2-PLAN T-12-03.2-09). The pass direction is not recorded. Ledger 325 covers only one guard reading planning files from disk.
verdict.corrected_fix:
In check.sh, when message_file is set and before `touch src/lib.rs`, refuse with exit 1 in either of two cases, and print a line telling the person to stage the files or run `git stash --keep-index -u` first:

1. `git diff --quiet -- src tests build.rs Cargo.toml Cargo.lock locales scripts .githooks` fails. This compares the working tree with the index the hook was handed, which for a partial commit is the temporary GIT_INDEX_FILE.
2. `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -- src tests locales` prints anything. `git diff` cannot see untracked files, and a new file someone forgot to add is the usual case.

That is about eight lines. Leave `.planning`, `docs` and `guards` out of the pathspec, so planning and remeasure work in the same checkout does not start being refused.

kept.title: A commit that changes only build.rs or rust-toolchain.toml runs no library or unit test at all
kept.location: scripts/which-checks.sh:432-547 (only Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock, *.iss and .github/workflows/* earn all; everything else that is not a document answers affected); scripts/check.sh:347-376 (affected maps only src/*.rs and tests/*.rs)
kept.what_this_is: which-checks.sh charges the full gate to build inputs that 'reach every target' (the manifest rule) and maps other non-document files to tests by path.
kept.problem: build.rs and rust-toolchain.toml reach every target as surely as Cargo.toml does, but neither is matched. They answer affected, which maps them to no module, and no guard record names either file, so the run is fmt, clippy and the nine whole-tree targets. The merge answers the same way, so the first full run against the change is the phase's closing gate.
kept.concrete_case: A branch commit moves rust-toolchain.toml from 1.98.1 to a newer compiler. Clippy runs with the new lints, the nine whole-tree targets run, and none of the roughly 10,500 library and integration tests outside them runs under the new compiler at the commit or at its merge. Likewise, a commit changing how build.rs:20-21 builds WIXEN_BUILD, which src/common/version.rs:31 compiles in, runs no common::version test.
kept.fix: Add build.rs and rust-toolchain.toml to the case arm that already answers all for *.iss in which-checks.sh, with one which-checks.test.sh case each.
kept.if_skipped: A compiler bump or build-script change goes untested on every commit and merge until the phase closes, which is the risk the manifest rule was written to remove.

verdict.reason:
Only the build.rs half holds, and only narrowly. The rust-toolchain.toml half is refuted. The pin's own header says "Bump the channel here and in every workflow in the same commit", and tests/house_style.rs:6577 (test_ci_and_this_machine_are_told_to_use_the_same_compiler) enforces it: it checks that every workflow names the pinned compiler, and it fails if no workflow names one at all. house_style is in guards_that_read_the_whole_tree (check.sh:62), so it runs on every `affected` commit. That means a channel bump without the workflows is refused. A bump with them stages .github/workflows/*, which answers `all` at which-checks.sh:527-534, both on the branch and at the merge. The one commit that has ever changed the pin, 6e31f895, staged all six workflows. 

build.rs is confirmed. A commit staging only build.rs gets past the manifest, .iss and workflow arms and answers `affected` (which-checks.sh:542-545). the_scoped_runs (check.sh:347-364) maps only src/*.rs and tests/*.rs. No src file compiles build.rs in, and no guard record has file = "build.rs" (the only mention, guards.toml:30033, is a comment in a record whose file is src/application/about.rs). So no library test runs. Of the three test files that read build.rs, house_style and the_words_that_say_nothing are whole-tree guards and do run. The third does not: tests/the_about_dialog_names_its_owners_and_its_links.rs:588, test_the_build_script_stamps_the_same_copyright_on_the_executable. 

The finding's WIXEN_BUILD example is weak. Dropping the rustc-env line breaks env! at src/common/version.rs:31, and clippy catches that by compiling. The only version test that touches BUILD (version.rs:782) checks current().starts_with(NUMBER), which holds for any value. 

Real exposure is small. build.rs has changed 5 times since March, always beside src/ files, and the about.rs record already couples a copyright change to the target that reads build.rs. The phase gate and CI's Test Suite cover the rest. Not in the ledger: 583 is the sibling hole for documents read at test time, and 354 is the MSRV floor.
verdict.corrected_problem: A commit staging only build.rs answers `affected`. It maps to no module and no guard record, so the one test that reads build.rs as data, test_the_build_script_stamps_the_same_copyright_on_the_executable in tests/the_about_dialog_names_its_owners_and_its_links.rs:588, does not run at the commit or at its merge. It runs only at the phase's closing gate or in CI. rust-toolchain.toml is not exposed: house_style, which runs on every scoped commit, refuses a channel bump unless every workflow moves in the same commit, and a workflow path answers `all`.
verdict.corrected_fix: Add build.rs only, not rust-toolchain.toml, to the arm that answers `all` for *.iss (which-checks.sh:481, `*.iss | build.rs)`), with one which-checks.test.sh case. A smaller alternative uses the coupling the gate already reads: a guards.toml record with file = "build.rs" and suite = "the_about_dialog_names_its_owners_and_its_links" that breaks the LegalCopyright line, measured with scripts/guards.sh --remeasure.

kept.title: The release quality gate runs every dependency's build script and the whole suite holding a token that can push to the repository
kept.location: .github/workflows/release.yml:43-67 (workflow-level permissions: contents: write; quality-gate sets no job permissions; actions/checkout persists the token by default)
kept.what_this_is: The quality gate only reads the code: fmt, clippy and cargo test. The write permission exists for the next job, which runs cargo release and pushes the tag.
kept.problem: Workflow-level contents: write applies to every job without its own permissions block, and actions/checkout leaves the token in .git/config. So in quality-gate, every build.rs and proc macro in the dependency tree and every test can read a token that can push commits and move tags. ci.yml is read-only for the same work.
kept.concrete_case: A compromised release of any crate in Cargo.lock adds a build.rs that reads http.https://github.com/.extraheader from .git/config. In ci.yml it gets a read-only token. In the release quality gate, the job a person dispatches deliberately to publish, it gets a token that can push to main or retag a release before build-release-assets runs.
kept.fix: Add 'permissions: contents: read' under the quality-gate job. Optionally also 'persist-credentials: false' on its checkout.
kept.if_skipped: The one workflow that publishes binaries to testers is also the one where a dependency compromise can write to the repository.

verdict.reason:
The lines say what the finding claims. release.yml:43-44 sets contents: write for the whole workflow. quality-gate (47-67) has no permissions block of its own. Its checkout at 52-53 is plain actions/checkout@v4, which persists the token in .git/config by default. ci.yml:22-31 is contents: read. No ledger entry in .planning/WINDOWS.md covers it: the release.yml rows are 326, 327, 483 and 616, and none is about token scope.

The finding overstates what the fix buys, though. Its own concrete case, a compromised crate in Cargo.lock whose build.rs reads the extraheader, still happens in the very next job. build-release-assets checks out with the write token persisted (89-93). It then runs `cargo install cargo-release --locked` (99) and `bash scripts/build-installer.sh`, which runs `cargo build --release` at line 208. That compiles every build.rs and proc macro in the dependency tree with a token that can push, and it does so after the tag is already on the remote. So the 'if skipped' line ('the one workflow where a dependency compromise can write to the repository') is still true after the two-line fix.

What the fix does remove is the write token from code that only quality-gate runs: test code, dev-dependencies, and crates enabled only by --all-features. That is real defence in depth for two lines, but it is narrow. The workflow has also never been dispatched (ledger 326), so for now the risk only exists on paper. Worth doing as cheap hardening, not as a fix for the stated case.
verdict.corrected_problem: quality-gate takes contents: write from the workflow level and keeps the token in .git/config, though it only reads. So test code, dev-dependencies and --all-features-only crates run holding a token that can push. The same exposure for the main dependency tree stays in build-release-assets: its checkout persists the write token, and it then runs cargo install cargo-release and cargo build --release. Scoping quality-gate narrows the exposure and does not remove it.
verdict.corrected_fix: Add `permissions: contents: read` under the quality-gate job, and optionally `persist-credentials: false` on its checkout. Say plainly that this does not cover build-release-assets. Closing that would mean building in a read-only job and only tagging and publishing in a write job, which changes when a tag exists. Guardrail 7 and ledger 327 put that decision with Pratik.

kept.title: An all-users uninstall erases the administrator's data, not the mail of the person who used the program, and the comment says the opposite
kept.location: installer/Wixen-Mail-Setup.iss:586-602 ([UninstallRun] --erase-all-data with runascurrentuser), 604-607 ([UninstallDelete] {localappdata}), 474-502 (the leftovers message, shown only when the exe is already gone)
kept.what_this_is: Uninstalling runs wixen-mail.exe --erase-all-data, which clears the unencrypted mail cache and the credential-store entries of whoever it runs as.
kept.problem: runascurrentuser makes the step inherit the uninstaller's account, and an all-users uninstall runs elevated. When the elevation is another account's (the borrowed-password case the [Run] comment at 205-211 describes), the erase clears that account's data and leaves the user's. The comment at 592-595 claims this flag prevents exactly that. To my reading [UninstallRun] has no runasoriginaluser, which the [Run] section uses for this case. Not verified against the Inno help, because it sits under AppData.
kept.concrete_case: A standard user picks 'Install for all users', types an administrator's password at the prompt, uses the program, and later uninstalls the same way. --erase-all-data runs as the administrator: it finds nothing of theirs, and the user's %LOCALAPPDATA%\wixen-mail cache and their Credential Manager tokens stay on disk. No message appears, because TheProgramIsAlreadyGone() is false.
kept.fix: In CurUninstallStepChanged, also show the existing 'your mail and settings are still on this computer' message when IsAdminInstallMode() is true, since the erase cannot be known to have reached the right account. Correct the comment at 592-595.
kept.if_skipped: People who uninstall to get rid of their mail are told nothing while an unencrypted copy and their sign-in tokens remain.

verdict.reason:
Confirmed by reading the code and its history. Line 602 runs `--erase-all-data` with `runascurrentuser`. Inno's help describes that flag as inheriting "Setup/Uninstall's user credentials (typically, full administrative privileges)", and it is already the default for entries that are not postinstall, so the flag changes nothing. `runasoriginaluser` is valid only in [Run]. Commit d6fe9361 (2026-07-28) shows how this happened: the compiler refused `runasoriginaluser` in [UninstallRun], and the commit message says that section "spells the same idea runascurrentuser". It does the opposite. So the comment at 592-595 is wrong, and the step runs as whatever account the uninstaller runs as.

The case is real. The setup offers "for all users" through `PrivilegesRequired=lowest` plus a dialog override, and an uninstall of an all-users install is elevated. A standard user who typed an administrator's password gets the erase run as that administrator. That account's credential store and %LOCALAPPDATA% are cleared, which is a no-op. The [UninstallDelete] entry for `{localappdata}` (604-607) resolves the same way. The message at 489-502 is gated on `TheProgramIsAlreadyGone()`, which is false here, so nobody is told.

The same gap also hits any second Windows account that used an all-users install, even when the elevation is the person's own. The code half-admits this at 443-446 ("has not been measured"), which contradicts the confident comment at 592-595. Nothing about it is open in `.planning/WINDOWS.md`, and no test pins the flag.

The proposed fix is wrong as written, so I corrected it. Reusing the existing message would open with "could not clear its own data, because the program was already gone", which is false here. It would also tell the common case (an administrator uninstalling their own install, where the erase did reach them) that their mail is still on the computer, which is also false.

One thing I could not check: the [Code] at 513 already calls `ExecAsOriginalUser` during uninstall. If Inno supports that call at uninstall time, a later change could move the erase there and check its exit code. Whether it does is in the Inno help under AppData, which I was not allowed to read, and the message is needed either way for other accounts.

Group is should rather than must: it is a privacy gap (the cache is unencrypted and the tokens stay), but it needs an all-users install plus a second account.
verdict.corrected_problem: installer/Wixen-Mail-Setup.iss:602 runs `--erase-all-data` with `runascurrentuser`, which per Inno's help inherits the uninstaller's credentials and is already the default. An all-users uninstall is elevated, so the erase, and the [UninstallDelete] `{localappdata}` line at 607, act on the elevating account only. A standard user who borrowed an administrator's password, or any other Windows account that used an all-users install, keeps its unencrypted %LOCALAPPDATA%\wixen-mail cache and its Credential Manager tokens. No message appears, because `TheProgramIsAlreadyGone()` is false. The comment at 592-595 (from d6fe9361) says this flag prevents exactly that, and it does not.
verdict.corrected_fix:
1. Correct the comment at 592-595 to say what is true: `runascurrentuser` is the default here, and it runs the erase as whoever the uninstaller runs as, which is the elevating account in an all-users uninstall. `runasoriginaluser` is not allowed in [UninstallRun].

2. In CurUninstallStepChanged, add a separate MsgBox when `IsAdminInstallMode() and not TheProgramIsAlreadyGone()`. Do not reuse the existing message, whose first line blames the missing program and whose "still on this computer" would be false for the account that was erased. Suggested wording: "Wixen Mail cleared its data for the Windows account '<GetUserNameString>'. If Wixen Mail was used under any other Windows account on this computer, that account's mail (%LOCALAPPDATA%\wixen-mail, not encrypted) and its wixen-mail entries in Credential Manager are still there; sign in as that account to remove them." That is about 8 lines and true in both the common case and the borrowed-password case. Leave per-user installs unchanged, since there the erase runs as the person.

kept.title: A red commit passes even when a test binary in its scoped run crashes, because red mode discards cargo's exit status and the verdict reads only FAILED lines
kept.location: scripts/check.sh:948 (run_the_tests_that_reach_what_changed || true); scripts/red-commit.sh:137-205
kept.what_this_is: In red mode, red-commit.sh verdict holds the run to 'every named test ran, every named test failed, nothing else failed', reading cargo's 'test NAME ... ok|FAILED' lines.
kept.problem: A test binary that aborts (an access violation in a wx call, a stack overflow, a process exit) prints no FAILED line for the rest of its tests and no 'test result:' line. Affected mode catches that through cargo's exit status. Red mode throws the status away, and the verdict sees no unnamed failure. This is the 'one named failure carries the unnamed ones through' case the verdict's own comment says it stops.
kept.concrete_case: A red commit names application::foo::tests::test_x and also makes the wired target's binary crash in its third test. --lib application::foo:: reports test_x FAILED. The --test line prints 'Running ... wired', two ok lines, then cargo's 'process didn't exit successfully ... 0xc0000005'. The verdict counts nothing unnamed as failed, and the commit is accepted with most of wired unrun.
kept.fix: In verdict, count lines beginning '     Running ' and lines beginning 'test result: ' in the log, and refuse when the first count is larger, with 'a test binary stopped before reporting'.
kept.if_skipped: The red path, which the project calls stronger evidence than an ordinary commit, is the one path where a crash reads as clean.

verdict.reason:
I read the code and the finding holds. scripts/check.sh:948 runs the scoped tests as `run_the_tests_that_reach_what_changed || true`, so in red mode cargo's exit status never reaches anything. The verdict in scripts/red-commit.sh (lines 137-205) only looks at `test NAME ... ok|FAILED|ignored` lines. It checks the log for `error:` lines only when no test ran at all (line 168).

Here is how a crash gets through. A test binary dies from an access violation, a stack overflow or a process exit. Cargo prints `error: test failed` and `process didn't exit successfully ... (exit code: 0xc0000005 ...)`, and with --no-fail-fast it carries on to the next target. The tests that never ran print nothing, so none of them shows up as failed. Meanwhile the named test, which lives in the separate `--lib` binary, reports FAILED. So `ran` > 0, `problems` = 0, and the commit is accepted.

Checks on the premise:
- Compile errors cannot get through this way, because `cargo clippy --all-targets` runs first (check.sh:720). Only runtime crashes are left.
- No case in red-commit.test.sh or check.test.sh feeds the verdict a log with a crashed binary.
- .planning/WINDOWS.md has no entry for this. Ledger 39 is about shell suites and is fixed.
- Crashes really happen here: CLAUDE.md records the 2026-09-03 rodio crash, where about 3,500 tests never ran.
- check.sh:788-802 already refuses a shell suite that "died partway through" for exactly this reason. Its comment says in red mode such a run "would read as a clean run with one expected failure in it". So the same reasoning was applied to shell suites and never to cargo binaries.

Why the group is nice and not should:
- Red commits are refused on main, so this only happens on a branch.
- The green commit that follows runs in affected mode, which keeps the exit status (check.sh:966). If the crash happens again, that commit is refused.
- So the damage is limited to one red commit falsely claiming that nothing else failed.

The proposed fix works and is close to minimal:
- Cargo prints exactly one `     Running ` line (status padded to 12 columns) per test binary. Libtest prints one `test result: ` line per binary that finishes, including runs where the filter matched 0 tests.
- The shell suites write to the same log but print neither line (shell-suite.sh only prints `test ... ok|FAILED`, `FAIL [..]` and summary lines), so they do not upset the count.
- The only thing that could inflate the second count is a failing test whose captured output contains `test result: ` at column 0, which is negligible.
verdict.corrected_problem:
The red-mode verdict misses a test binary that crashes, and so does everything else in red mode. When a binary aborts, its remaining tests print no lines and libtest's `test result:` line never appears. Red mode discards cargo's exit status (check.sh:948), so a red commit whose named test fails in one binary is accepted even though another binary died partway through.

There is also a second case. If the crash is in the same binary as the named test, before that test reports, the commit is refused, but the message is the wrong one: "named as failing and never ran ... Either the name is wrong, or this commit's scoped tests do not reach the module". The real cause, a crash, is not mentioned.

check.sh:788-802 already guards shell suites against exactly this, but nothing does the same for cargo binaries.
verdict.corrected_fix:
TDD:
- Red: add a case to scripts/red-commit.test.sh. Feed the verdict a log with two `     Running ` lines, a `test a::named ... FAILED` line, and a `test result:` line for the first binary only. Assert that the verdict refuses.
- Green: in `verdict`, after the ran==0 block, add the check below. It counts problems, so every problem is still reported together.

```
local started finished
started=$(grep -c '^     Running ' "$output_file" || true)
finished=$(grep -c '^test result: ' "$output_file" || true)
if [ "$started" -gt "$finished" ]; then
    echo "red-commit: $((started - finished)) test binary(ies) stopped before reporting, so the tests after the stop said nothing." >&2
    problems=$((problems + 1))
fi
```

This needs no change to check.sh.

kept.title: A documents-only commit pays a full clippy run and a forced crate rebuild for Rust that by definition did not change
kept.location: scripts/check.sh:714-720 (touch src/lib.rs and clippy run in every mode, after the mode is already known at 653-655); 827-852 (docs_only branch)
kept.what_this_is: docs_only is the answer for a commit whose paths are all .md or .txt files that no source compiles in (which-checks.sh:165-178).
kept.problem: The mode is decided before the touch, but touch src/lib.rs and clippy --all-targets run anyway. With no Rust, manifest or compiled-in file changed, clippy cannot find anything the previous gated commit did not. The touch also makes the crate and the eight document-reading test binaries rebuild before they run. Measured clippy median per hook run: 27 s (docs/development/measurements.md:570-571). CLAUDE.md records a documents-only run of 2m56s against 36 s warm.
kept.concrete_case: A plan's closing commit that touches only docs/changelog.md and .planning/*.md re-lints all 149 integration targets and relinks the eight document targets just to read markdown.
kept.fix: Wrap the touch and the clippy stage in if [ "$mode" != docs_only ]. Keep rustfmt. Update the one CLAUDE.md sentence that lists clippy for documents-only commits.
kept.if_skipped: About half a minute or more on every documents commit, the most common commit in a plan's wrap-up.

verdict.reason:
The finding is real. I read the code and confirmed it.

- **The lines say what the finding claims.** `check.sh:653-655` settles the mode, then `:714` runs `touch src/lib.rs` and `:719-720` runs `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` in every mode, with no mode check. The `docs_only` branch only starts at `:827`.
- **`docs_only` really means no Rust changed.** `which-checks.sh` answers it only when every staged path is a `.md` or `.txt` file that `is_a_document` (`:165-178`) clears. Anything compiled in under `src/` is excluded by the include scan, and `tests/` compiles in no `.md` (its one include is an `.html` fixture). `build.rs` watches only `assets/icon.ico`. So clippy has no changed Rust to judge.
- **What clippy can still see is not the commit.** It lints the working tree, so in this mode it can only report unstaged Rust or a new lint from a toolchain upgrade. CI and the once-a-phase full gate both run clippy anyway.
- **The touch only exists for clippy.** The comment at `:8-11` says so, and cargo tracks includes and mtimes for the tests on its own. The touch also forces the crate and the eight document targets in `:102` to rebuild.
- **The cost is measured.** 12-04 and 12-05 record `docs_only` hook runs of 86 s and 83 s, of which clippy was 30 s and 28 s. The `tests/*.rs` count is 149, as the finding says.
- **Not already in the ledger.** No entry in `.planning/WINDOWS.md` covers it.

It stays at **nice**, not should. The saving is about 30 s or more per documents commit, but `CLAUDE.md:304` and `:312` record Pratik's settled rule that a documents commit runs formatting, clippy and the document targets. Changing what the gate runs is his call.

The fix as written is incomplete:

- **It breaks a test.** Two cases in `check.test.sh` run `check.sh docs_only` from an empty `mktemp -d` folder and rely on it stopping at `touch src/lib.rs`. The case at `:686-693` greps for `stopped in start after N s: start N s`. With the touch skipped, the run reaches `cargo fmt`, fails there and reports "stopped in rustfmt", so the check suite goes red. The comments at `:617-618` and `:672-675` say the same thing.
- **The guard has to be spelled `!=`.** The ordering reading at `check.test.sh:778` finds the first mode branch by `if [ "$mode" = `. A guard spelled with `=` above the suite loop would turn "the suites run before any mode branch" red. The finding's `!=` happens to avoid this.
- **More than one sentence names clippy for documents commits.** `CLAUDE.md` has two (`:304` and `:312`), plus `which-checks.sh:43` and the message `check.sh` prints at `:847`.
- **The size is wrong.** The change adds lines rather than removing two (`lean_lines` says -2).
verdict.corrected_problem:
The gate settles the mode at `scripts/check.sh:653-655`. It then runs `touch src/lib.rs` (`:714`) and `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` (`:720`) in every mode, `docs_only` included.

A `docs_only` commit stages only `.md` and `.txt` files that no source compiles in (`which-checks.sh:165-178`), so clippy has no changed Rust to judge. It can only report:

- unstaged Rust in the working tree, which is not part of the commit, or
- a new lint from a toolchain upgrade, which CI's Clippy job and the once-a-phase full gate already catch.

The touch is there only to keep clippy's fingerprint fresh (`check.sh:8-11`). It also forces the crate and the eight document-reading targets (`check.sh:102`) to rebuild before they run.

Measured `docs_only` hook runs: 86 s with clippy at 30 s (12-04-SUMMARY), and 83 s with clippy at 28 s (12-05-SUMMARY). Every plan's closing documents commit pays this.
verdict.corrected_fix:
1. **Red first, in `scripts/check.test.sh`.** Add a case named, for example, "a documents-only run does not lint":
   - Put a fake `cargo` first on PATH in `$work` that logs its arguments and exits 0.
   - Run `check.sh docs_only` from `$work`.
   - Assert that no logged call holds `clippy`. Today this is red, because the run stops at `touch src/lib.rs` before it.

2. **Fix the existing cases this change would break.** The timing cases at `check.test.sh:676-693` rely on `docs_only` stopping at the touch. Switch them to ask `affected`, which still touches and so still stops in start, and update the comments at `:617-618` and `:672-675`.

3. **Green, in `scripts/check.sh`.** Wrap only the touch and the clippy stage:

   ```bash
   if [ "$mode" != docs_only ]; then
       touch src/lib.rs
       begin_stage "clippy"
       cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
   fi
   ```

   Keep the touch before the rustfmt stage, as it is today. Spell the test `!=`: `check.test.sh:778` treats any `if [ "$mode" = ` line as the first mode branch, and that line must stay below the suite loop.

4. **Update the text that lists clippy for documents commits.** Change the `docs_only` message at `check.sh:847`, the `docs_only` row of the table at `which-checks.sh:43`, the comment at `check.sh:8-11`, and the two sentences at `CLAUDE.md:304` and `:312`. `CLAUDE.md` states the current behaviour as Pratik's rule, so confirm the change with him before landing it.

kept.title: The calendar's XML reader never decodes XML escapes, though the address-book copy of the same reader does
kept.location: src/service/caldav.rs:1283-1293 (extract_xml_value), used raw at 746, 755-757, 822-827, 457-460; compare src/service/carddav.rs:350-386 (value_in, xml_unescaped)
kept.what_this_is: CalDAV and CardDAV answers are multistatus XML that the code reads by hand. CardDAV wraps the shared extract_xml_value in value_in, which turns & < > " ' back into characters. CalDAV calls extract_xml_value directly and never decodes anything, so calendar-data, href, getetag and displayname reach the rest of the program still escaped. carddav.rs:357-359 says so ("a gap there rather than a decision") and STATE.md:3937 says the gap is "recorded", but no WINDOWS.md entry holds it.
kept.problem: One rule (take XML's escaping off a value) is applied in one reader and not in its twin. XML requires every & and < in element text to be escaped, so any CalDAV server that does not use CDATA sends escaped iCalendar text. Neither reader handles numeric references such as . No test in caldav.rs contains an entity.
kept.concrete_case: Certain: an event titled "Dinner & drinks" arrives in <c:calendar-data> as SUMMARY:Dinner & drinks. parse_report_events (826) hands that to the iCalendar reader unchanged, so the event is stored and read aloud with "&" in its title. A calendar named "Work & Home" is listed as "Work & Home" (755). Probable, not verified here because nothing has met a server: libxml-based writers, which SabreDAV and therefore Nextcloud, ownCloud and Baikal use, write each CR as  and quotes as ". Then every calendar-data line ends in "", component_named_after refuses "VCALENDAR" as a component name, and every event counts as unreadable, so the sync reports "none could be read" on every calendar. Separately, the ETag kept after a write here comes from the PUT response header with plain quotes (caldav_sync.rs:523, 545). The next report's tag is "...", so both_copies_moved (caldav_sync.rs:893) raises a conflict on an event only this computer changed.
kept.fix: Move xml_unescaped from carddav.rs into caldav.rs and apply it inside extract_xml_value. Extend it to decimal and hex character references (, ") in the same single pass. Then delete carddav's value_in wrapper and call extract_xml_value directly. Add one CalDAV fixture with &, " and  in it.
kept.if_skipped: Every CalDAV event or calendar name containing &, < or > is shown and spoken with its escapes, and on SabreDAV-family servers CalDAV, and probably CardDAV too, may read nothing at all. The day phase 14 meets a Nextcloud account will show which.
kept.ledger_entry: Not in WINDOWS.md. Mentioned only in a carddav.rs comment and STATE.md:3937, and both describe only the named entities.

verdict.reason:
I read every line the finding cites and its central claim holds. extract_xml_value (caldav.rs:1283-1293) slices out the raw text between the tags and never decodes it. Every CalDAV caller uses that raw text: hrefs and etags at 457/460 and 822/823, displayname, ctag and color at 755-757, and calendar-data at 826-827, which goes straight into every_event_in_the_resource. carddav.rs:350-402 wraps the same function in value_in/xml_unescaped, and its own comment at 357-359 calls the CalDAV side a gap. No CalDAV test contains an entity: the grep for & finds nothing in caldav.rs. WINDOWS.md has no entry for this. Only STATE.md:3937 and the 05.1-05 summary mention it, and both cover only the five named references.

The finding understates three things.
(1) The bad value travels back to the server. the_properties_this_program_owns (caldav.rs:1916) always rewrites SUMMARY from the local row, so editing only the time of an event called "Dinner & drinks" PUTs "Dinner & drinks" to the server as literal text. Every other client then shows it, and each read and edit cycle adds another layer of escaping.
(2) There is a third copy of the decoder. free_busy.rs:417 (without_the_escapes) is a multi-pass replace chain, and its comment describes exactly the harm CalDAV suffers.
(3) A quoted TZID such as "(US & Canada)" arrives as "...", so delimiter_colon cannot see the quotes and splits at the colon inside them.

Two of its sub-claims are wrong or overstated.
(a) Lines ending in  do not make the sync report "none could be read". component_named_after refuses "VEVENT", so events_in finds nothing. every_event_in_the_resource then falls back and reads the whole document as one event. The result is at most one event per resource, with "" stuck to its UID and its DTSTART possibly taken from the VTIMEZONE block: the events are misread, not counted as unreadable.
(b) The false ETag conflict is real but needs a narrow window. The If-Match tag comes from the GET header (caldav_sync.rs:283/304), and the next pull of a row that is not pending stores the escaped tag. So the conflict fires only when somebody edits again after a push and before the next pull.

The  and " behaviour of SabreDAV comes from libxml's xmlEncodeSpecialChars. Nothing in this repo has met such a server, so that part stays unverified here. The & case needs no server knowledge, because XML itself requires & to be escaped in text.
verdict.corrected_problem:
The CalDAV reader never takes off XML's escaping. extract_xml_value (caldav.rs:1283) returns raw element text, and every CalDAV caller (457, 460, 746, 755-757, 822-827) uses it as-is. CardDAV decodes the five named references (carddav.rs:360-402), and free_busy.rs:417 has its own multi-pass copy. None of the three decodes numeric references.

Certain consequences:
- An event titled "Dinner & drinks" is stored and spoken as "Dinner & drinks", and a calendar called "Work & Home" is listed with "&" in its name.
- Editing any field of that event writes "SUMMARY:Dinner & drinks" back to the server as literal text (caldav.rs:1916), so the damage reaches every other client and gets worse with each round trip.
- A quoted TZID parameter arrives as "..." and delimiter_colon splits inside it.

Probable, on servers whose XML writer encodes CR as  and quotes as " (the SabreDAV family; unverified here):
- No BEGIN:VEVENT line is recognised, so each resource is read whole through the fallback. That gives at most one event, with "" on its UID and possibly a DTSTART taken from the VTIMEZONE block. The events are misread rather than counted unreadable.
- Stored ETags carry ". A row edited again after a push and before the next pull raises a false conflict at caldav_sync.rs:893.
verdict.corrected_fix:
Write the test first (TDD): a parse_report_events fixture whose SUMMARY holds & and <, whose getetag is "v1", whose lines end in , and whose displayname is "Work & Home".

Then make the change:
1. Move carddav's single-pass xml_unescaped into caldav.rs as pub(crate).
2. Extend it to decode &#N; and &#xH; when they name a valid char. Leave anything else as it arrived.
3. Apply it inside extract_xml_value.
4. Remove carddav's value_in wrapper and call extract_xml_value directly. If the wrapper stays, values are decoded twice and carddav's existing test that &lt; reads back as < breaks.
5. Replace free_busy.rs's without_the_escapes with the shared function, so one rule lives in one place.

That is about 10-15 lines of change plus the test.

kept.title: Three dependencies are declared for code that does not use them, and three comments say otherwise
kept.location: Cargo.toml:93, 121-122; src/service/outward.rs:1616, 1622-1623, 1641-1645; src/service/security.rs:436-451; docs/changelog.md:14357; .cargo/audit.toml:43-45
kept.what_this_is: icalendar and quick-xml are direct dependencies with no use anywhere in src, tests or build.rs; both CalDAV and iCalendar are parsed by hand. rand 0.10 is used once, inside #[cfg(test)] impl SecurityService::encrypt (security.rs:436-451), so it is a test-only crate declared as a shipped one.
kept.problem: icalendar alone pulls iso8601 and nom-language into the build (Cargo.lock:2577-2587). The comments mislead a reviewer. The changelog line and audit.toml:43-45 say "the quick-xml 0.41 that parses CalDAV responses", and nothing in the program calls quick-xml. outward.rs:1641-1645 classifies image as decoding only the program's own compiled-in icon with ico, png and bmp, while service/picture.rs:47 decodes strangers' attachments with jpeg on. That is the reason a reviewer would read that entry for.
kept.concrete_case: git grep -E "icalendar::|quick_xml::" across *.rs returns nothing. The only mentions are the name strings in A_CRATE_THAT_CANNOT. A security reviewer reading audit.toml concludes the CalDAV parser is quick-xml and audits the wrong code, while the real hand parser is the one in finding 1.
kept.fix: Delete Cargo.toml:121-122 and the two list entries, since test_neither_list_of_crates_has_gone_stale requires the lists and the manifest to move together. Move rand = "0.10" to [dev-dependencies]; every_dependency already reads that section. Correct the image comment in outward.rs and the quick-xml sentence in audit.toml.
kept.if_skipped: Two unused parsers stay in the dependency audit's scope, and the documents keep pointing at a parser that does not run.
kept.ledger_entry: Map lead C, not in WINDOWS.md. Confirmed here and extended with rand and the three false comments.

verdict.reason:
I checked each claim against the code and confirmed it. Cargo.toml:121-122 declares icalendar 0.17 and quick-xml 0.41. A grep of every .rs file (src, tests, build.rs) finds neither crate's paths anywhere. The only mentions are the two name strings at outward.rs:1622-1623. `git log -S` finds no commit that ever added or removed `quick_xml::` or `icalendar::` in src, so both have been unused since they were added. rand 0.10 (Cargo.toml:93) is used only at security.rs:443/451, inside the `#[cfg(test)] impl SecurityService` that starts at line 436. The image entry at outward.rs:1641-1645 is out of date: Cargo.toml:236-241 now turns on jpeg, and service/picture.rs decodes picture attachments people are sent. audit.toml:43-45 and changelog:14357 both say a quick-xml 0.41 parses CalDAV responses, and nothing in the program does. WINDOWS.md has no entry for icalendar, quick-xml, rand or unused dependencies.

Parts of the finding are overstated, so the payoff is smaller than it says:
(1) quick-xml 0.41 stays in Cargo.lock and in the shipped program either way. phonenumber 0.3.10 lists it as both a normal and a build dependency (its Cargo.toml, and Cargo.lock:4254). Removing our line takes nothing out of the audit's scope.
(2) rand 0.10 stays in the tree through rodio and quinn-proto (Cargo.lock:4584, 4911). Moving it to [dev-dependencies] fixes the label and changes no shipped code.
(3) The two lists in outward.rs answer "can this crate reach a server?", and "image cannot" is still true. Only the description of what image decodes is stale.

Only icalendar really adds weight: icalendar, iso8601 and nom-language, three crates that only it pulls in (nom 8 stays because lettre and pgp use it).

The fix as written also misses three things:
- A_CRATE_THAT_CANNOT is declared `[&str; 56]`, so the length has to change too.
- The rand08 comment at Cargo.toml:337 says "the `rand` 0.10 named above". That stops being true once rand moves below.
- tests/house_style.rs:2154-2158 asserts that "Fixed iCalendar property lookup matching on a prefix" does not fire. That case only tests something because icalendar is a dependency, a word the reader sees and has to leave alone because no version follows it. With icalendar gone it passes for nothing, which is the "guard that reads documents needs a companion" trap CLAUDE.md warns about.

It is still worth doing: about ten lines, no behaviour change, and a security decision record that names the wrong parser. No guard record in guards/guards.toml anchors on any line this touches.
verdict.corrected_problem:
The manifest declares two crates that nothing uses: icalendar 0.17 and quick-xml 0.41 (Cargo.toml:121-122). Both CalDAV and iCalendar are parsed by hand, and git history shows neither crate was ever called from src. rand 0.10 (Cargo.toml:93) is used only inside `#[cfg(test)] impl SecurityService` (security.rs:436-451), yet it is declared as a normal dependency. icalendar alone brings in three crates nothing else needs: icalendar, iso8601 and nom-language.

Removing quick-xml and moving rand only fix the labels. quick-xml 0.41 stays in the program through phonenumber, which lists it as both a normal and a build dependency, and rand 0.10 stays through rodio and quinn-proto. The text is also wrong in three places:
- audit.toml:43-45 and changelog:14357 say "the quick-xml 0.41 that parses CalDAV responses", when that copy belongs to phonenumber.
- outward.rs:1641-1645 says image decodes only the compiled-in icon with ico, png and bmp. Since 0.65.0 it also decodes picture attachments people are sent, and jpeg is on. The entry's real answer, that image cannot reach a server, still holds.
- After the fix, the rand08 comment at Cargo.toml:337 ("the rand 0.10 named above") is wrong.

There is also a hidden coupling. tests/house_style.rs:2154-2158 uses "iCalendar" as its example of a word that matches a dependency and must not fire. Once icalendar is gone, that case checks nothing.
verdict.corrected_fix:
1. Delete the `icalendar` and `quick-xml` lines at Cargo.toml:121-122. Move or reword the "# CalDAV / iCalendar support" header, since it would otherwise sit above scraper, ego-tree and the other crates.
2. In outward.rs, remove "icalendar" and "quick-xml" from A_CRATE_THAT_CANNOT and change its type from `[&str; 56]` to `[&str; 54]`.
3. Move `rand = "0.10"` to [dev-dependencies]. Both every_dependency readers already read that section, so the "rand" list entry stays. Reword the rand08 comment at Cargo.toml:337-338 so it no longer says "named above".
4. In tests/house_style.rs:2154-2158, swap the iCalendar example for another dependency that is also an ordinary word, written without a version, for example "image" or "open". The negative case then keeps exercising the reader.
5. Rewrite the image comment at outward.rs:1641-1645: it decodes the app's own icon and picture attachments, with ico, png, bmp and jpeg on, and has no notion of a destination.
6. Correct audit.toml:43-45 to say quick-xml 0.41.0 arrives with phonenumber, as both a dependency and a build dependency, and that nothing here parses CalDAV with it.
Leave the historical changelog entry as it is, or add one line under [Unreleased]. Optionally correct .planning/codebase/STACK.md:51 and INTEGRATIONS.md:38, which repeat the same claim.

verdict.reason:

kept.title: vCard line unfolding is a hand copy of the iCalendar unfolding, kept in step by comments
kept.location: src/data/message_cache/contacts.rs:2141-2225 (unfold_vcard_lines, put_back_together, laid_out_by_hand, indented, opens_or_closes_a_card); src/service/caldav.rs:2889-2975 (unfolded, put_back_together, laid_out_by_hand, indented)
kept.what_this_is: Both formats fold long lines the same way (RFC 5545 3.1 and RFC 6350 3.2), and both files implement the same "was this indentation folding or somebody's hand layout" heuristic. put_back_together and indented are byte-for-byte the same, and laid_out_by_hand differs only in which marker line it checks.
kept.problem: Each copy's comment says the two "agree on purpose" (contacts.rs:2192-2193). Agreement held by prose is the failure mode this project keeps recording, and the data layer already calls service code freely (messages.rs alone has 45 crate::service:: uses).
kept.concrete_case: caldav's opener check (component_named_after) already accepts BEGIN:VCARD in any case. The next fix to folding, for example a CR-only line ending or a tab rule, lands in caldav.rs, the calendar import gets it, and contacts imported from a file or CardDAV keep the old behaviour with no test noticing.
kept.fix: Make unfold_vcard_lines call crate::service::caldav::unfolded(block) and delete the four copied helpers. caldav's version also drops trailing empty lines, so check that contact_from_vcard_block ignores them first. Mind the 35 guard records fingerprinting contacts.rs; the --remeasure run is the cost.
kept.if_skipped: Two copies of a parser for strangers' bytes drift apart one fix at a time.
kept.ledger_entry: Not in WINDOWS.md.

verdict.reason: The finding holds. I read both copies. `put_back_together` and `indented` are the same code in contacts.rs:2157-2170 and 2209-2211 and in caldav.rs:2914-2927 and 2963-2965. `laid_out_by_hand` (contacts.rs:2194, caldav.rs:2948) differs only in which marker check it calls. The comments at contacts.rs:2129-2130 and 2192-2193 are the only thing keeping the two in step. Contacts is the only reader that keeps its own copy: note_document.rs:41/87, ical_subscription.rs:98, invitations.rs:1354 and when_people_are_free.rs:164 all call `caldav::unfolded`. The data layer already calls into service code in 24 files, so there is no layering reason against it. Nothing about this is in WINDOWS.md. Both copies were written on 2026-08-07 (9c458b20, 8a3a5a9f), and the line-splitting and marker code has not changed in either file since, so they have not drifted yet. That makes this cleanup rather than a live bug, hence nice. A fix to folding made in caldav.rs would still miss contacts imported from a file or over CardDAV, and no test compares the two copies. Three claims needed correcting: (1) the line splitting is not the same in both, since contacts uses `.lines()` with `trim_end_matches('\r')` and caldav splits on CRLF and LF with one `strip_suffix('\r')`, though they agree on real input; (2) caldav's marker check accepts any one-word component on BEGIN or END, so it is broader than the VCARD-only check, which in practice does no harm because base64 and folded values cannot produce one; (3) the real cost is two guard records with byte-identical anchors, not a count remeasure.
verdict.corrected_problem: The vCard reader keeps a hand copy of the iCalendar unfolding: `put_back_together` and `indented` are the same code in both files, and `laid_out_by_hand` differs only in its marker check (VCARD only, where caldav accepts any one-word component). all.title: A change made while a push is in flight is marked sent and never sent (tasks, events, notes)
all.location: src/data/message_cache/tasks.rs:551-575 (mark_task_sent, rename_task); src/application/tasks_sync.rs:899-909 (settle); src/data/message_cache/calendar.rs:822-835 (mark_calendar_event_sent); src/data/message_cache/notes.rs:786-806 (a_backend_took_the_note)
all.what_this_is: After a sync sends a pending task, event or note to the provider, the store clears the row's pending flag so the next sync does not send it again.
all.problem: The flag is cleared with `UPDATE ... SET pending = 0 WHERE id = ?`. Nothing checks that the row is still the one that was sent. The sync reads every pending row at the start (tasks_sync.rs:787-791) and pushes them one by one over the network. The window, which owns its own connection, can edit a row during that time. The edit sets pending = 1 and a new updated_at (tasks.rs:618-631), and the clear then wipes it. For a task made on this computer it is worse: rename_task saves the provider's copy of the original and deletes the local row, so the edit is gone everywhere. notes.rs:786-790 says this one-statement shape exists to keep text typed during the push, yet the same statement sets pending = 0, so that text is never sent. mod.rs:1420-1425 anticipates a task ticked during a sync, but only as a lock wait.
all.concrete_case: The task 'Pay rent' was edited offline, so it is pending. Check Mail runs the tasks sync. While Google answers the update, the person ticks the task done. toggle_task_complete sets pending = 1. Then settle calls mark_task_sent, which sets pending = 0 on the row that now says done. Google still holds 'not done'. The next pull compares remote_updated, which was just set to Google's stamp, and sees no change. From then on the phone says not done and this computer says done. In a second case, someone creates 'Call bank' and corrects it to 'Call the bank' while the create is in flight. rename_task then writes Google's 'Call bank' over the row and drops the local row, so the correction is lost on both sides. Events behave the same way through mark_calendar_event_sent, and notes through a_backend_took_the_note.
all.fix: Clear the flag only if the row is unchanged since the push read it. Pass the updated_at that push_one sent and add `AND updated_at = ?` to the three UPDATEs. In rename_task, when the local updated_at no longer matches, move the row to the provider's id but keep the local content with pending = 1, so the next sync sends the edit. Add one failing test per kind: edit the row between pending_tasks and mark_task_sent, then assert that it is still pending.
all.if_skipped: Ticks, retitles and note text typed during a sync disappear without a word. The two copies then disagree until either side is edited again.
all.ledger_entry: new; no ledger row mentions an edit made during a push

verdict.reason:
I confirmed the race for tasks and notes by reading the code, but the finding gets the calendar location wrong, its retitle example cannot happen, and its fix would cause new harm.

**What holds:**
- The sync opens its own database connection on a worker thread (wx_app.rs:31095-31118; mod.rs:1414-1418 says so). Nothing stops the window from writing while a sync runs. The only sync guard, ASyncUnderWay, is used for undo and nothing else.
- pending_tasks reads every pending row once, at the start (tasks_sync.rs:787-791). For a later task in a backlog, the window therefore covers the whole push phase, not just one network round trip.
- toggle_task_complete (tasks.rs:618-631, called from managers.rs:3239) and complete_task both set pending = 1. settle then calls mark_task_sent (tasks.rs:557-561), which runs `SET pending = 0 ... WHERE id = ?` with nothing else in the WHERE.
- resolve (tasks_sync.rs:306-321) then sees pending false and an unchanged stamp, and returns Nothing. The two copies stay apart until the provider side changes. When it does, the local tick is overwritten without a word.
- rename_task (tasks.rs:569-575) saves the provider's copy and drops the local row. A tick made during a create is lost everywhere.
- Notes: the editor saves the pending flag it read (wx_app.rs:2895-2911). a_backend_took_the_note (notes.rs:797-802) then sets pending = 0, so text typed during the create is kept here and never sent. The doc comment at notes.rs:786-790 claims more protection than the code gives.
- No ledger row and no test covers this. Ledger 220 is about rename_task orphaning subtasks, which is a different problem.

**What is wrong in the finding:**
- mark_calendar_event_sent has no production caller. Its only call is the test at calendar.rs:2619. The real calendar paths are:
  - `settled` in application/calendar.rs:637-653.
  - `settled_here` and `settled_here_for_an_occurrence` in caldav_sync.rs:517-548.
  
  All three clone the event as it was pushed and save the whole row with save_calendar_event. So an event edit made during the push is wiped on this computer too, not only left unsent. That is worse than the finding says, and the proposed fix never reaches it.
- There is no task title editor anywhere in the interface. Tasks can be created, ticked, completed from the due window, moved, copied and deleted. The 'Call bank' retitle case cannot happen. A tick during a create can.
- The fix as written is unsafe because it puts `AND updated_at = ?` on the whole UPDATE:
  - For notes, it would skip recording provider_note_id. The next push would then create a second note at the backend.
  - For tasks, it would skip recording remote_updated. The next sync would see the remote side changed while the row is pending, choose TakeRemoteOverLocal, and replace the edit anyway.
  
  Only the pending flag should depend on the check. The identity and stamp must always be written.
- The move path (managers.rs:8078-8090) sets pending without touching updated_at. A check on updated_at alone would miss a move made during a push.

**Why should, not must:** the cost is silent loss of a person's change, but it needs an edit to the same item while a sync is pushing it.
verdict.corrected_problem:
Each push clears the pending flag, or saves the whole row, without checking that the row is still the one it sent.
- **Tasks:** mark_task_sent (tasks.rs:557-561) and rename_task (tasks.rs:569-575), both called from settle (tasks_sync.rs:899-909).
- **Notes:** a_backend_took_the_note (notes.rs:797-802).
- **Calendar:** `settled` (application/calendar.rs:637-653), `settled_here` and `settled_here_for_an_occurrence` (caldav_sync.rs:517-548). These save the event as it was pushed over the whole row with save_calendar_event, so a concurrent edit is also wiped on this computer. mark_calendar_event_sent has no production caller.

The window owns its own connection, so a tick, a due-window completion or a note or event edit made during the push sets pending = 1, and the settle then clears it or overwrites it.

Reachable cases:
- A task ticked while any pending task is being pushed. Google keeps 'not done', the stamp now matches, resolve returns Nothing, and the two copies disagree until the provider side changes. At that point the local tick is overwritten silently.
- A task created here and ticked during its create. rename_task drops the local row and the tick is lost everywhere.
- A note made here and edited during its create. The edit is never sent.
- An event edited during its push. The edit is overwritten locally by the version that was pushed.

Retitling a task is not reachable, because the interface has no task editor.
verdict.corrected_fix:
Pass the updated_at that the push read. Keep the identity and stamp writes unconditional, and make only the pending flag depend on that value.

1. **Tasks:**
   - mark_task_sent: `UPDATE tasks SET remote_updated = ?1, remote_status = ?2, pending = CASE WHEN updated_at = ?4 THEN 0 ELSE pending END WHERE id = ?3`.
   - rename_task: when the local row's updated_at no longer matches, save the provider id with the local content, Google's remote_updated and pending = 1, so the next sync sends it as an update.
2. **Notes:** a_backend_took_the_note gets the same treatment. It always writes provider_note_id and provider_version and sets `pending = CASE WHEN updated_at = ? THEN 0 ELSE pending END`.
3. **Calendar:** replace the whole-row save in `settled`, `settled_here` and `settled_here_for_an_occurrence` with a targeted UPDATE. It writes calendar_id, provider_event_id, web_link, etag and last_modified_remote as each one does now, plus the conditional pending.
4. **Move path:** make the task move (managers.rs:8078-8090) set updated_at, so a move made during a push is seen.

Tests, red first, one per kind: change the row between the pending read and the settle, then assert that it is still pending and still holds the edit. For notes, also assert that provider_note_id was recorded.

all.title: A flag change kept from offline later overwrites a newer change that already reached the server
all.location: src/presentation/wx_app.rs:28349-28350 (success path keeps the waiting row); src/presentation/wx_app.rs:18458-18494 (replay); src/data/message_cache/waiting_flag_changes.rs:108-121 (stop_waiting deletes by row and flag only)
all.what_this_is: waiting_flag_changes holds read and starred changes that could not reach the server. The next mail check replays them before it syncs folders.
all.problem: When a later direct push for the same message and flag succeeds, the old waiting row is not removed: the Ok branch at 28350 only shows a status line. The next check replays the stale value over the newer one. Separately, stop_waiting_to_send_a_flag_change deletes `WHERE message_row_id = ?1 AND which_flag = ?2`. If the person changes the flag again while the replay's round trip is open, and that change is also kept waiting, the replay deletes the newer row.
all.concrete_case: With no network, the person marks message M read, and a waiting row says read = true. The network comes back. Before any check runs, they mark M unread. The push succeeds and the server has M unread, but the waiting row still says read = true. At the next Check Mail, send_the_flag_changes_that_were_waiting sends \Seen and deletes the row. The flag fetch later in the same check then brings 'read' down. M flips back to read, reversing the last thing the person did.
all.fix: In the Ok(()) branch of the flag push, call cache.stop_waiting_to_send_a_flag_change(message_row_id, which_flag) for Read and Flagged. Make stop_waiting delete only the change that was sent: add `AND changed_to = ?3 AND changed_at = ?4`, with the replay passing the values it sent. Add two tests, one per path, each red today.
all.if_skipped: Read and starred states silently revert after anyone who works partly offline reconnects.
all.ledger_entry: new; ledger 782 is a different ordering problem with moves

verdict.reason:
I read every line the finding cites, and they say what it claims. In wx_app.rs:28349-28350, `Ok(()) => say(StatusUpdated)` touches no waiting row. Only three places write to or delete from waiting_flag_changes: keep (wx_app.rs:28303 and what_rules_tell_the_server.rs:262) and the replay's two stop_waiting calls (wx_app.rs:18480 and 18494). mark_these_read (12456) and mark_what_was_read (12826) call spawn_server_change and never clear a waiting row. No test covers a successful push leaving a stale row behind.

The case is easier to hit than the finding says, because it does not need the network to drop. When Allow Changes is off, imap.rs:1356 raises Error::Security through outward::permitted. why_the_push_failed reads that as ThisComputerRefusedIt, so the change is kept waiting. With changes off, simply reading a message (mark_what_was_read) leaves a waiting row saying read = true.

Then the person turns changes on and marks that message unread before any check runs. The push succeeds, but the row still says read = true. The next check runs send_the_flag_changes_that_were_waiting (wx_app.rs:30514), which comes before any folder is read. It sends \Seen and deletes the row, and the flag read then brings "read" back down. The same thing happens with stars.

A folder read that runs while the row is still there is no help either: the_flags_to_keep (flag_changes_waiting.rs:206) writes the stale value over what the server says.

The second half also holds. stop_waiting deletes by row and flag only (waiting_flag_changes.rs:115-116), so a newer row kept while the replay is waiting for the server is lost. That needs a narrow race, though: the replay succeeds while a concurrent push fails with a network or sign-in error.

Nothing in .planning/WINDOWS.md records this. The finding names the wrong ledger entry: 782 is about Alt+R in a test target, and the moves-ordering entry is 765, which is a different problem.

I grade it should rather than must. No mail is lost, each stale row causes one reversal and then goes away, and the window closes at the next check. Even so, the reversal is silent, it happens at the server, and phase 14 sittings that turn changes on make it likely.

The proposed fix does not fit together. If stop_waiting requires changed_to and changed_at, the direct push's Ok branch cannot call it, because it does not know the waiting row's changed_at. An unconditional delete in the Ok branch would bring back the same race in reverse: an older push still waiting on the server succeeds after a newer change has been kept waiting, and deletes it.
verdict.corrected_problem: A direct read or star push that succeeds leaves any older waiting row for the same message and flag in place. Such a row comes from offline, or from a mark made while Allow Changes was off, which includes every message read with changes off. The next check replays the stale value at the server, and the flag read brings it back here, so the person's last change is reversed. Separately, the replay's stop_waiting deletes by row and flag only, so a newer change kept waiting while the replay is in flight is deleted. That second part is a narrow race.
verdict.corrected_fix:
1. In spawn_server_change, capture the time the change was asked for, before spawn_blocking.
2. Add a cache method `stop_waiting_for_what_came_before(message_row_id, which_flag, asked_at)` that runs `DELETE ... WHERE message_row_id = ?1 AND which_flag = ?2 AND changed_at <= ?3`.
3. Call it in the Ok(()) arm for Read and Flagged. Labelled keeps no waiting row, so it needs nothing.
4. Separately, give the replay's delete `AND changed_to = ?3 AND changed_at = ?4`, using the values it sent, so it cannot remove a newer kept row.
5. Add one red test per delete in waiting_flag_changes.rs:
   - A row written after asked_at survives stop_waiting_for_what_came_before.
   - A row replaced after the replay read it survives the replay's delete.
   - If the Ok arm can be reached from a test, add a case there too: a kept read = true row followed by a successful unread push leaves nothing waiting.

all.title: Saving accounts with INSERT OR REPLACE deletes another account with the same address and wipes the chosen account order
all.location: src/data/message_cache/accounts.rs:21-32 (INSERT OR REPLACE INTO accounts); src/data/message_cache/mod.rs:2486 (email UNIQUE), 3299 (tree_order added later, not in the insert list); accounts.rs:122 (ORDER BY tree_order IS NULL, tree_order, created_at); src/presentation/wx_app.rs:11258-11278 and 22132-22135, 22217
all.what_this_is: save_account writes one account row. replace_accounts calls it for every account whenever the Account Manager closes with OK.
all.problem: REPLACE deletes every row that conflicts on any unique key before it inserts. Because `email` is UNIQUE, saving account B with A's address deletes A's row. The insert also leaves out tree_order (sets it to NULL) and resets created_at to now. load_accounts sorts by exactly those two columns.
all.concrete_case: Order: the person presses Alt+Shift+Up to put account B above A. This writes tree_order (11273), but s.accounts stays [A, B]. They then open the Account Manager and press OK. replace_accounts([A, B]) rewrites both rows with tree_order NULL and created_at in the order A, then B, so the list goes back to A, B with no word. Address: the person adds the same mailbox a second time, for example as POP. B's insert deletes A's row. This session still shows both accounts. On the next start A is gone, while its folders and messages remain in the unencrypted database and its keyring password and tokens remain with no row to name them. delete_account (accounts.rs:262-296) exists precisely to prevent that last outcome.
all.fix: Use `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE SET` with the listed columns, leaving out created_at and tree_order. A second account with an existing address then fails with a constraint error that the Account Manager already announces (wx_app.rs:22217-22223), instead of deleting a row. Add a test that sets an order, calls replace_accounts and reloads.
all.if_skipped: Account order resets after any Account Manager visit in the same session. A duplicate address silently loses an account and leaves its secrets on the machine.
all.ledger_entry: new

verdict.reason:
Confirmed line by line. accounts.rs:23 uses INSERT OR REPLACE. The accounts table has `email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE` (mod.rs:2486), and nothing has a foreign key to accounts, so no cascade hides the effect. The only account column the insert leaves out is tree_order (mod.rs:3299, nullable, no default). REPLACE deletes the old row and inserts a new one, so tree_order comes back NULL and created_at is reset to now on every save. load_accounts sorts by exactly those two columns (accounts.rs:122).

Order case: move_the_chosen_account (wx_app.rs:11258-11286) writes tree_order but never updates s.accounts. s.accounts is only assigned at startup (970) and in handle_account_mgr (22225). Any later Account Manager change calls replace_accounts with the stale order, wipes every tree_order, and the list goes back to the old order without a word.

Duplicate case: show_edit cannot see the other accounts, and nothing in wx_account_manager.rs checks for an existing address. Account::new gives a fresh UUID. So adding the same address twice leaves two ids with one email in `working`. replace_accounts works out `gone` before it saves anything, so it finds nothing to remove. Then save(B) hits the email UNIQUE and deletes A's row. This session still shows A. On the next start A is gone, its folders, messages, identities and quick steps stay in the unencrypted database, and its keyring password and tokens are left with no row to name them. delete_account (262-296) refuses to remove an account for exactly that reason.

Not in .planning/WINDOWS.md: no entry mentions INSERT OR REPLACE, tree_order, replace_accounts, or save_account for this. No test covers either case. test_the_account_list_a_person_ends_up_with_is_the_one_that_is_stored checks the ids sorted, not the order, and uses distinct addresses.

The finding overstates two things. Pressing OK alone saves nothing: the dialog returns AccountManagerAction::None unless something changed. And its fix leaves a hole, covered in the corrected fix.
verdict.corrected_problem: save_account writes with INSERT OR REPLACE. Because email is UNIQUE (mod.rs:2486) and REPLACE deletes every conflicting row before it inserts, saving account B with A's address deletes A's row. Every save also sets tree_order to NULL and created_at to now, and load_accounts sorts by those two columns. Order case: Alt+Shift+Up/Down writes tree_order but never updates s.accounts. Any later change in the Account Manager (add, edit, delete, Set Default or Set Active; pressing OK with no change saves nothing) calls replace_accounts with the stale order, so the move is undone without a word. Duplicate case: nothing in the Account Manager stops the same address being added twice. The second save silently deletes the first account's row. That session still shows both. On the next start the first account is gone, and its mail, identities and quick steps stay in the unencrypted database. Its keyring password and OAuth tokens are left with no row to name them, so uninstall never erases them.
verdict.corrected_fix:
In save_account (accounts.rs:10):
(1) Before credentials::store, refuse an address another account already uses. Run `SELECT 1 FROM accounts WHERE email = ?1 AND id <> ?2` and return a plain sentence such as "Another account already uses this address." This matters because the finding's fix alone would let credentials::store write B's password first and then fail on the insert. That leaves B's secret in the keyring with no row, and the error spoken would be SQLite's "UNIQUE constraint failed: accounts.email". 
(2) Replace INSERT OR REPLACE with `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT(id) DO UPDATE SET` naming the listed columns except created_at, so an existing row keeps its created_at and tree_order. 
Tests, red first: set an order with set_account_order, call replace_accounts with the old order, reload, and the order holds. Save A, then call replace_accounts([A, B]) where B uses A's address: it is refused, A is still stored, and B's password is not in the store. replace_accounts already stops at the first error, and handle_account_mgr already speaks the error (wx_app.rs:22216-22223).

all.title: The calendar's date window compares text in mixed formats, so events made here on the first day of a Week or Month view are missing
all.location: src/data/message_cache/calendar.rs:94-101 (events_that_overlap_query); src/presentation/managers.rs:2225-2241 (editor stores 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM'); callers src/presentation/wx_app.rs:15549-15555, 13599-13601, src/presentation/managers.rs:1663-1665; src/presentation/ui_types.rs:1350-1362
all.what_this_is: events_that_could_fall_between fetches the events a Week, Month or Agenda view draws. Nothing else adds events afterwards: every_day_shown expands only what this query returns.
all.problem: The overlap test compares raw TEXT: `COALESCE(NULLIF(end_datetime,''), start_datetime) >= ?2`. Every caller passes ?2 as 'YYYY-MM-DDT00:00:00Z'. The event editor stores 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM' for timed events and a bare 'YYYY-MM-DD' for all-day ones. A space sorts before 'T', and a bare date sorts before any longer string that starts with it. So an event the person made on the window's first day compares as earlier than the window.
all.concrete_case: The person creates a 09:00-10:00 event on Monday 2026-10-12 in the editor. It is stored as end_datetime '2026-10-12 10:00'. They open Week view for that week, so from = '2026-10-12T00:00:00Z'. SQLite evaluates '2026-10-12 10:00' >= '2026-10-12T00:00:00Z' as false. The event is not drawn, although it is drawn on every other day. An all-day event on the 1st, stored as '2026-11-01', is likewise missing from November's Month view. The tests at calendar.rs:1338-1350 use only 'Z' strings, so none of them catches this.
