The cleaner keeps https `src` plus `width` and `height` (html_renderer.rs:263-283, and ammonia's defaults allow those attributes on img). `set_body` then loads that page into a live WebView2 with `set_page` (wx_compose.rs:1432-1436, 1467, 1479, 1483). The editor WebView has no navigation or resource filter (wx_compose.rs:1091-1100), and `Content-Security-Policy` appears nowhere in src. The default `hold_back_remote_pictures` is false (config.rs:819), so reading the message gives `HeldBackAsABeacon` for a width=1 height=1 picture (pictures.rs:659-666, html_renderer.rs:706-709) and nothing is fetched. Pressing Ctrl+R then fetches the pixel. With the Reading switch on, every remote picture is fetched in the editor. Forward fetches them too, and so does reopening a draft. The ledger has no open entry for this. docs/privacy.md:510 says "Two surfaces do that", meaning the preview pane and the formatted window, so the page is wrong as well, and putting the CSP in makes it true again. The fix is the smallest that works. The body is read back through `#wixen-body.innerHTML` (editor_document.rs:1400), so a meta tag in the head never goes out with the message. Pictures the user inserts are `data:` URIs (pictures.rs:527), so they still show. The page's own inline script is not touched because the policy names only img-src. Images are the only fetch the cleaner leaves possible: no style and no background attribute survive it.
verdict.corrected_problem: The reply and forward editor is a live WebView2 page that holds the quoted original after only the cleaner has run. The reader's hold-back step never runs on it. Any remote `` in the original is fetched as soon as the composer opens. That includes tracking pixels the reader held back under default settings, and every remote picture when the Reading tab's switch is on. Reopening a draft that quotes the original fetches them too. docs/privacy.md says only the preview pane and the formatted window fetch pictures, so the editor is a third surface the page does not mention.
verdict.corrected_fix: Start with a failing test in editor_document.rs that asserts the page from `editor_document` contains `Content-Security-Policy` with `img-src data:`. Then add `<meta http-equiv="Content-Security-Policy" content="img-src data:">` to the head, before the style element. `cid:` adds nothing because the cleaner already drops `cid:` addresses. Do not use default-src, because the page's own script is inline. The outgoing markup does not change: the body is read through innerHTML, and a forward still sends the original's remote references. The cost: in the editor, a forward's remote pictures show as broken images even when the Reading switch allows fetching. That is acceptable, and worth one line in docs/changelog.md.

all.title: Following a webcal: link freezes the window with no timeout and buffers an unbounded feed
all.location: src/presentation/wx_app.rs:18954-18962 (rt.block_on inside open_what_windows_handed_over, called on the UI thread from 6688-6709 and 6747-6748); src/service/ical_subscription.rs:22-49 (reqwest::Client::new(), with no timeout, then response.text()); same client in the background refresh at wx_app.rs:31455-31462
all.what_this_is: Opening a calendar feed that Windows handed over through a webcal:// link, and the periodic refresh of subscribed feeds.
all.problem: The comment says the fetch runs 'on the runtime rather than on the thread drawing the window'. But `rt.block_on` runs the future on the calling thread, and that thread is the UI thread: the same function shows MessageDialogs. The client has no request timeout, and `.text()` reads the whole body into memory with no cap.
all.concrete_case: Someone clicks webcal://slow.example/team.ics on a web page. Windows hands it to the running copy, open_what_windows_handed_over runs on the UI thread, and block_on waits on a host that accepts the connection and never answers. The window stops repainting, NVDA reports it as not responding, and it stays that way with no limit. A feed that streams gigabytes is held whole in memory until the process runs out. The background refresh of a subscribed feed hangs its worker the same way, every check.
all.fix: Build the client with `.timeout(Duration::from_secs(30))`, as google_api.rs:702 and oauth.rs:1183 already do. Read with `response.chunk()` up to a cap, for example 20 MB, as update_download.rs:1037-1052 does. Move the handover fetch to `rt.spawn` and report back through a UIUpdate.
all.if_skipped: A link on any web page can hang the mail window indefinitely, and a hostile feed can run the program out of memory.

verdict.reason:
I read every cited line and the finding holds. It is not in .planning/WINDOWS.md: there are no ledger hits for webcal, the ICS client, block_on, the UI thread or "not responding".

1. The feed client has no time limit. src/service/ical_subscription.rs:22-26 builds the client with reqwest::Client::new(), which waits forever by default. Lines 45-48 then read the whole reply with response.text(), with no size cap.

2. A link from any web page reaches it. default_apps_registration.rs:1009 registers Wixen Mail for webcal links. opening.rs:63-74 turns webcal://host/x into Opening::CalendarSubscription("https://host/x").

3. The fetch blocks the window. Another copy hands the link over as UIUpdate::HandedOver. The UI update handler (wx_app.rs:22817-22830) raises the frame and calls opens_a_handover. That calls open_what_windows_handed_over (6702, and at start-up 6748). That function builds a MessageDialog on the frame (18861-18864), so it runs on the thread that draws the window. At 18958 it calls rt.block_on(fetch_ics), which runs on the calling thread and waits there. The comment at 18954-18957 says the opposite of what happens. A host that accepts the connection and never answers freezes the window with no limit. NVDA then reports the window as not responding.

4. The background refresh hangs the same way, but off-screen. It runs inside rt.spawn_blocking (31318), so the window keeps drawing. But the block_on of refresh_subscription at 31459 waits forever, and that hang does more than the finding says. The ASyncUnderWay guard taken at 31323 is never dropped. taking_back.rs:301 and 324 then answer BeingSyncedNow, so undoing a calendar event deletion for that account is refused for the rest of the session.

5. Every other HTTP client in the tree already has a limit. google_api.rs:703, microsoft_graph.rs:1041 and oauth.rs:1184 set a 30-second timeout; the finding's line numbers are one off. update_download.rs:1037-1052 already shows how to read a reply in chunks up to a cap. The ICS client is the one without either.

Why should and not must: the memory blow-up needs a hostile feed. The freeze needs someone to follow a link to a slow or silent host. But for a screen reader user, a window frozen with no way out is severe, and the fix is small.
verdict.corrected_problem:
The calendar feed client's HTTP client (ical_subscription.rs:24) is built with reqwest::Client::new(), which has no time limit. It then reads the whole reply into memory with no size cap (45-48).

The webcal handover runs this fetch with rt.block_on (wx_app.rs:18958). That code runs on the thread that draws the window: it is reached from the UIUpdate::HandedOver handler at 22817-22830, and from start-up at 6748. So a feed host that accepts the connection and never answers freezes the window with no limit, despite the comment at 18954-18957 saying the fetch is kept off that thread.

The background refresh (31455-31462) runs on a worker thread, so the window keeps drawing. But it can hang forever too, and then its ASyncUnderWay guard (31323) is never dropped. While the guard is held, undoing a deleted calendar event for that account is refused (taking_back.rs:301, 324) until restart. Either path can also hold a huge reply whole in memory.
verdict.corrected_fix:
Three changes, each driven by a failing test first.

1. In ICalSubscriptionClient::new, build the client the way google_api.rs:701-709 does: reqwest::Client::builder().timeout(Duration::from_secs(30)).build(), falling back to Client::new() with a warning if the build fails. This alone bounds both the freeze and the background hang. The red test points the client at a loopback listener that accepts and never answers, with a short timeout passed in.

2. In fetch_ics, replace .text() with a response.chunk() loop that refuses once the total passes a cap, for example 20 MB, as update_download.rs:1037-1052 does. Then decode the bytes as UTF-8.

3. In the CalendarSubscription arm (wx_app.rs:18945-18974), stop calling rt.block_on on the window's thread. Move the fetch and read_calendar_file into rt.spawn or spawn_blocking (the cache is already an Arc). Send the outcome back as a UIUpdate, so the told, went_wrong and switch_to(Calendar) calls still run on the window's thread. Rewrite the comment at 18954-18957 so it says what the code then does.

Changes 1 and 2 are about 15 lines. Change 3 adds one UIUpdate variant and its arm.

all.title: A meeting is moved on opening even when the program itself has labelled the message Phishing
all.location: src/application/reading_a_message.rs:611-705; src/application/meeting_changes.rs:540-562 (only the From address is compared); src/presentation/wx_app.rs:15936-15945; src/service/safety.rs:391-399 (dmarc=fail becomes Safety::Phishing); src/presentation/ui_types.rs:103 (MessageItem.safety)
all.what_this_is: The rule that moves a meeting on the calendar, and queues the move for the provider, when an organiser's update is opened in a reader window.
all.problem: The only proof of authorship is the From header, which anyone can forge. The receiving server's verdict is already parsed into message.safety, but nothing on this path reads it. Ledger 637 is wrong on this point: it says the program 'reads no provider's authentication verdict', yet safety.rs reads Authentication-Results and stores the result on the row.
all.concrete_case: An attacker sends `From: Ada <ada@example.com>` with METHOD:REQUEST, the UID of Ada's meeting and a higher SEQUENCE that moves it to 03:00. Gmail stamps `dmarc=fail header.from=example.com`, and the list shows 'Phishing'. Opening it in the reader calls what_opening_it_changes. the_organiser_sent_it compares addresses only, so the Move is saved and queued to Google or Microsoft (meeting_changes.rs:601-612), and colleagues see the new time.
all.fix: In what_opening_it_changes_on_the_calendar, wx_app.rs:15936, return `MeetingChange::SaidNotApplied(Why::TheMessageLooksForged)` when `message.safety >= Safety::Spam`. That is one new Why arm and a sentence. Correct ledger 637's description.
all.if_skipped: A forged invitation that the program has already flagged still rewrites a shared calendar on a single open.
all.ledger_entry: 637 (understates: the provider verdict is read in safety.rs and stored as MessageItem.safety, just never consulted here)

verdict.reason:
I read every line the finding cites and they say what it claims. Opening a message in a reader window runs open_single_message (wx_app.rs:15814), then what_opening_it_changes_on_the_calendar (15936), then what_opening_it_changed_among (reading_a_message.rs:632). That function sends only `from` to meeting_changes::what_opening_it_changes. The only check on who sent it is why_it_is_not_applied (meeting_changes.rs:540-562), and that compares address_of(sender) with the recorded organiser and nothing else. If they match and Allow Changes is on, what_it_changed_saved (reading_a_message.rs:847-856) saves the_copy_moved with pending: true, which queues the change for the provider.

The program already holds the receiving server's verdict. imap.rs fetches the AUTHENTICATION-RESULTS header (line 102) and turns it into a verdict with safety::from_headers (line 1994). A dmarc=fail becomes Safety::Phishing (safety.rs:394-399). mail_sync.rs:672-675 merges in the junk-folder verdict and stores it, and it reaches MessageItem.safety (ui_types.rs:103). The test test_a_phishing_verdict_survives_being_stored shows it survives storage. Nothing in reading_a_message.rs, meeting_changes.rs or the wx_app seam reads it, and no test covers a flagged message.

Ledger 637 is open. It (and T-13-13-03 in 13-13-PLAN.md) says the forged-From case cannot be told apart "because it reads no provider's authentication verdict". That premise is false, so the ledger understates the gap: it can be closed now without a real account. Phase 14's plans do not mention it.

Two corrections to the finding:
1. The proposed fix is wrong as placed. Returning SaidNotApplied in wx_app before the call would apply to every flagged message, including ones with no calendar part. MeetingChange::said() gives a sentence for every SaidNotApplied, so every spam or phishing message opened would say "Your calendar was not changed". That breaks the module's rule that a message which would change nothing says nothing (meeting_changes.rs:352-354). The check has to come after `wanted` is known.
2. "Colleagues see the new time" holds only when the person is the organiser. For an attendee, only their own copy moves.

The attacker also has to know the meeting's UID and the person has to open the message in a reader, so this is should rather than must.
verdict.corrected_problem: The only proof of who sent a meeting update is the From address, which can be forged, and that alone moves the meeting on the calendar and queues the move for the provider. The receiving server's verdict (Authentication-Results dmarc=fail becomes Safety::Phishing, and the junk folder becomes Spam) is already parsed, stored and carried on MessageItem.safety, but the meeting-change path never reads it. Ledger 637 says the program "reads no provider's authentication verdict", which is false, so it presents a fixable gap as one waiting on a real account. Exposure: someone who knows the meeting's UID (another invitee, or anyone the invitation was forwarded to) forges the organiser's From. The person opens the message in a reader with Allow Changes on, and their copy moves and is queued to Google, Microsoft or the calendar server. Other attendees see the new time only when the person is the organiser.
verdict.corrected_fix:
Do not put the check in wx_app before the call. The function returns early for messages with no calendar part, and a guard placed before it would make every flagged message say "Your calendar was not changed". The fix:
1. Pass the message's stored safety level from what_opening_it_changes_on_the_calendar (wx_app.rs:15936) through what_opening_it_in_a_reader_changed and what_opening_it_changed_among to meeting_changes::what_opening_it_changes. It becomes one more parameter beside `found`.
2. In what_opening_it_changes, right after the InsideEncryptedMail check (meeting_changes.rs:375-377), add `if safety >= Safety::Spam { return SaidNotApplied(Why::TheSenderIsNotConfirmed) }`. At that point a change is known to be wanted, so ordinary mail still says nothing.
3. Add one Why arm and its sentence in Why::said.
4. Write the failing test first, in meeting_changes's tests: an organiser-address update with Safety::Phishing is not applied.
5. Correct ledger 637 and T-13-13-03: the verdict is read; only what a real provider stamps remains to be confirmed.

all.title: Saved attachments carry no Mark of the Web
all.location: src/presentation/wx_app.rs:29202-29211 (fetch_and_write_attachment, plain std::fs::write); the one save path for both surfaces (wx_reader.rs:1147-1151 delegates to it); no Zone.Identifier anywhere in src
all.what_this_is: Saving a stranger's attachment to disk.
all.problem: The file is written with no Zone.Identifier stream. Windows uses that stream to run SmartScreen on executables and scripts and to open Office files and PDFs in Protected View. Outlook, Thunderbird and every browser write it. A grep for Zone.Identifier and IAttachmentExecute in src finds nothing.
all.concrete_case: Someone saves `invoice.docm`, or `report.js` named safely by safe_file_name, to Downloads and later double-clicks it in Explorer. Office opens the macro document outside Protected View, and wscript runs the script with no SmartScreen prompt. The same file saved from webmail would have been gated.
all.fix: After the write in fetch_and_write_attachment, add `let _ = std::fs::write(format!("{destination}:Zone.Identifier"), "[ZoneTransfer]\r\nZoneId=3\r\n");` under cfg(windows), ignoring the failure on non-NTFS volumes. IAttachmentExecute::Save is the fuller answer.
all.if_skipped: Malicious attachments saved through Wixen Mail bypass Windows' own last line of defence.

verdict.reason:
The finding holds. At wx_app.rs:29202-29211, fetch_and_write_attachment writes the bytes with a plain std::fs::write and does nothing else. It is the only place that writes a saved attachment: save_attachment at :29184 calls it, and wx_reader.rs:1147-1151 hands the page window's save to the same handler. A case-insensitive search of the whole repo for Zone.Identifier, ZoneId, IAttachmentExecute and "Mark of the Web" finds nothing in src. The only hits are ICU time-zone code in common/zones.rs. Nothing in .planning/WINDOWS.md records it.

safe_file_name (service/attachment_name.rs:45) removes path segments, control characters and bidi overrides, but keeps the extension. So report.js and invoice.docm are saved under exactly those names.

The app's only other defence is the "program" warning: attachment_summary at wx_reader.rs:289 and the list name at :699-709, both driven by RUNNABLE in reader_text.rs:1717. That list has 21 entries and does not include docm, xlsm, iso, img, one or chm. For those types, Mark of the Web is the only gate, and it is missing. For .js the app does say "a program" aloud, but the file it writes still runs on double-click with no Attachment Manager prompt.

One small overstatement in the finding: without the mark, Office does not run macros by itself. It falls back to the Trust Center's default "Enable Content" bar, instead of opening in Protected View with the internet-macro block. That is still a real downgrade from what Outlook, Thunderbird and every browser give the same file.

The proposed fix is the smallest that works. Rust passes "path:Zone.Identifier" to CreateFileW unchanged. Ignoring the error is correct because FAT, exFAT and some network shares have no alternate streams.

This is "should", not "must": exploiting it still needs the user to save a stranger's file and then open it from Explorer.
verdict.corrected_problem: A saved attachment is written with no Zone.Identifier stream. Windows reads that stream to open Office files and PDFs in Protected View, to apply Office's block on internet macros, and to show the Attachment Manager or SmartScreen prompt before a script or program runs. The app's own "program" warning (RUNNABLE, reader_text.rs:1717) covers 21 extensions and not .docm, .xlsm, .iso, .img or .one. For those, the missing mark means no gate at all.

all.title: A browser sign-in is filed under the account with no check of which account actually consented
all.location: src/service/oauth.rs:211-240 (no login_hint) and 786-830 (authorize stores whatever tokens come back under account_id); src/presentation/wx_account_manager.rs:810-827 (separate Google calendars, contacts and tasks sign-in)
all.what_this_is: Route B's separate Google sign-in for calendars, contacts and tasks, and the shared authorize() flow.
all.problem: The auth URL carries no login_hint, and after the code exchange nothing asks Google whose token it is. For mail, a mismatch at least fails at IMAP (user= differs). The PIM syncs call /users/me/... and /people/me/..., which simply act on the token's owner.
all.concrete_case: Alice's account keeps an app password for mail. She presses Sign In for Calendars while her browser's default Google session is her partner Bob's, and Bob's account consents. The tokens are stored under Alice's account id with no error. The next sync brings Bob's contacts and calendars into Alice's account, and two-way sync pushes Alice's local edits and deletions to Bob's Google data.
all.fix: Add `.add_extra_param("login_hint", account_email)` in build_authorization_url_pkce. After the separate Google sign-in, GET calendars/primary, which is allowed by the calendar scope already granted and whose id is the signed-in address. Refuse to keep the tokens when it differs from the account address.
all.if_skipped: One wrong click in the account chooser silently merges and writes into another person's Google data.

verdict.reason:
Confirmed by reading the code. build_authorization_url_pkce (oauth.rs:211-241) adds the scopes, plus access_type and prompt=consent for Google, and nothing that names the account: no login_hint. AuthManager::authorize (786-830) exchanges the code and calls store_tokens under self.account_id without asking whose token it is. AuthManager does not even hold the address. sign_in_for_calendars (wx_account_manager.rs:810-827) passes only account.id, and the line the person hears first ("Signing in to Google for the account's calendars, contacts and tasks. Finish in the browser.", who_holds_the_calendars.rs:436) does not name the address to choose. The syncs act on whoever owns the token: google_api.rs:532 calls /people/me/connections and :560 calls /users/me/calendarList. a_google_token_with (who_holds_the_calendars.rs:538-566) hands that token to all three syncs. allowed.rs says a new installation lets tasks, contacts and calendar changes go up to the provider, so local edits and deletions would land in the other person's data. None of this is in .planning/WINDOWS.md: searches for login hint, wrong account and whose token turn up only unrelated entries (211, 815).

The finding understates the case in two ways. First, Route A (mail through the browser) has the same gap: run_oauth_flow (wx_account_manager.rs:3116-3159) uses the same authorize(). IMAP would fail on the mismatched user, but the_google_sign_in_for(true) gives the same "gmail" token to the three syncs anyway, so the other person's calendars, contacts and tasks still come in. Second, the Microsoft sign-in has the identical shape, because its Graph calls go to /me.

The fix as written needs two corrections. On Gmail, a strict comparison against the primary calendar's id would refuse correct sign-ins: someone who typed the address with different dots, or with googlemail.com, gets a canonical id that differs. And the tokens are already stored by the time authorize() returns, so the check has to come before store_tokens, or remove the tokens on a mismatch. About 30 to 40 lines, not 12, because the address has to be passed through AuthManager and both callers.
verdict.corrected_problem: No browser sign-in (Google mail, the separate Google calendars sign-in, Microsoft) tells the provider which address to sign in as, and none checks who consented. authorize() stores whatever tokens come back under the account id. The calendar, contacts and tasks syncs call /users/me, /people/me and Graph /me, so they act on the token's owner. With the separate sign-in, a wrong pick in the browser brings another person's calendars, contacts and tasks into this account, and sends this account's local edits and deletions to them, since personal-information changes are allowed by default. With Route A, IMAP fails on the mismatch, but the three syncs still use the same token and do the same.
verdict.corrected_fix: Give AuthManager the account address, set by both callers (sign_in_for_calendars and run_oauth_flow), and in build_authorization_url_pkce add `.add_extra_param("login_hint", address)` for every provider. Google and Microsoft both accept it. For the two Google sign-ins, after the code exchange and before store_tokens, GET https://www.googleapis.com/calendar/v3/calendars/primary. The calendar scope both sign-ins already ask for allows this, and the id is the signed-in address. Compare it with the account address through one pure function: ignore case, and for gmail.com/googlemail.com also ignore dots and treat the two domains as one. On a mismatch, store nothing and return an Error::Authentication that names the address Google signed in as, so the person can try again with the right one. Test-first: one test that the URL carries login_hint, and rows for the comparison (case, dots, googlemail, a different person). Record the matching Microsoft check (Graph /me/calendar owner address) as a ledger entry if it is not done in the same change.

all.title: The update check trusts any installer signed by anyone named 'Pratik Patel'
all.location: src/service/update_download.rs:48 (WHO_SIGNS_THIS), 556-567 (exact name compare), 766-853 (CertGetNameStringW with CERT_NAME_SIMPLE_DISPLAY_TYPE)
all.what_this_is: The second half of the installer check, which the module calls 'the check'.
all.problem: The identity check is a display-name comparison. WinVerifyTrust only proves that some trusted CA issued the certificate. 'Pratik Patel' is a very common personal name, and an individual-validated code-signing certificate in that name can be bought from any public CA. The comment's own argument against 'contains' applies equally to an exact match on a common name.
all.concrete_case: An attacker who can put a file in the GitHub release, through a leaked token or the release workflow, signs a Wixen-Mail-Setup-9.9.9.exe with a certificate issued to a different Pratik Patel. WinVerifyTrust passes, the name matches, the file becomes a Verified, and the program offers to run it. Today every genuine installer is refused, because nothing is signed yet, but this forged one would be accepted.
all.fix: Pin the signing key rather than the name. Hash the signer certificate's SubjectPublicKeyInfo, or read CERT_SHA256_HASH_PROP_ID, compare it with a constant set when the certificate is issued, and refuse while the constant is empty. ring is already a dependency for the hash.
all.if_skipped: The defence against a compromised release channel can be defeated by buying a certificate in a common name.

verdict.reason:
The code does what the finding says. `whether_that_signer_is_ours` (src/service/update_download.rs:556-567) compares the trimmed name with `WHO_SIGNS_THIS = "Pratik Patel"` (line 48), ignoring case. The name comes from `CertGetNameStringW(..., CERT_NAME_SIMPLE_DISPLAY_TYPE, ...)` at 834-842, which returns the leaf certificate's CN. The only other check is `WinVerifyTrust` (646-711), which only proves that a trusted CA issued a code-signing certificate.

The path runs in production when updates are switched on: wx_app.rs:11336-11390 fetches, `verify` (858) checks, and wx_app.rs:23380-23415 asks and then hands over. Nothing else reads the issuer, a key, a thumbprint or an EKU. The tests at 1575-1636 cover only name strings.

It is not in the ledger. Entries 329, 334-336 and 342 cover an unsigned build, an unrun transport, an unrun handover, a check that has never seen a genuine signature, and revocation. None says that the identity rule is a common name.

The finding's own concrete case holds. Anyone who can publish a release asset, which is the one threat this check exists for since HTTPS already covers the path, can sign with a certificate any other Pratik Patel can get. The decided CA is Azure Artifact Signing (decisions-2026-09-06.md item 6, ledger 329), which issues individual certificates whose CN is the validated name. The comment's argument against "contains" applies equally to an exact match on a common name.

The group is should rather than nice for two reasons:
- Builds already given to testers carry this rule and keep it until they update.
- The pin has to be in place before the first signed release, or the field keeps the weak rule.

It is not must, because it needs the release channel compromised and updates are opt-in.

The finding's fix is wrong for this project. Artifact Signing issues short-lived leaf certificates, valid for about three days, with a fresh key each day. Pinning the leaf SPKI or CERT_SHA256_HASH_PROP_ID would therefore refuse every genuine release after the first.
verdict.corrected_problem: The identity half of the installer check (update_download.rs:556-567) is a case-insensitive exact match of the leaf certificate's CN against "Pratik Patel", and nothing else identifies the publisher. Any trusted CA, including Azure Artifact Signing, which this project has chosen, issues individual code-signing certificates with that CN to any person of that name who passes ID validation. So a release asset signed by a different Pratik Patel passes both WinVerifyTrust and the name rule. It becomes a Verified, and the question then tells the user it "is signed by Pratik Patel". Today genuine installers are all refused because nothing is signed, while a forged one with such a certificate would be accepted. This is not in .planning/WINDOWS.md.
verdict.corrected_fix:
Pin the identity that Artifact Signing keeps across certificates, not the leaf key. Do not use the leaf SPKI or the SHA-256 thumbprint, because Artifact Signing rotates both every few days. The fix has three parts:
- Read the signer certificate's enhanced key usages with CertGetEnhancedKeyUsage, in the same `the_name_in` function that already holds the context.
- Require the account's durable-identity EKU OID (1.3.6.1.4.1.311.97.<identity validation id>), held in a constant beside WHO_SIGNS_THIS.
- Keep the name check for the message, and refuse while the constant is empty, which changes nothing today because everything is already refused.

Put the rule in a pure function over the list of OIDs, so a fixture can test it. Set the constant in the plan that closes ledger 329, when the identity validation exists. That is roughly 15 to 20 lines plus one test.

all.title: Google contacts stop syncing for good a week after the first full read
all.location: src/application/contacts_sync.rs:854-869 and 2374-2387 (test pinning the assumption at 6036); src/service/google_api.rs:530-533; caller src/presentation/wx_app.rs:30972-30981
all.what_this_is: The Google contacts sync asks only for what changed since a stored marker (a sync token). When Google says the marker is too old, the code is meant to read the whole address book again and store a fresh marker.
all.problem: The code treats only HTTP 410 as "too old" (SYNC_TOKEN_EXPIRED = 410). Google's own page for people.connections.list says an expired token comes back with the reason word EXPIRED_SYNC_TOKEN and says nothing about 410. The People API reports errors with google.rpc codes, and none of those codes maps to HTTP 410; this kind of refusal normally arrives as 400 with status FAILED_PRECONDITION. The test at line 6036 builds the 410 by hand, so it cannot notice. I have not seen a live answer, so the status code is my reading of Google's error model, not a measurement.
all.concrete_case: The first sync stores a token (requestSyncToken=true). Google's documentation says that token expires 7 days after the full sync. On day 8 Google answers 400 with EXPIRED_SYNC_TOKEN. is_expired_sync_token returns false, sync_google_contacts returns Err at line 2386, the dead token stays stored, and wx_app only adds "Google contacts: ..." to the errors. Every later sync fails the same way, so no change made on the phone ever arrives again. Contacts typed here never reach Google either, because their only push runs on a full read (finding 2). This is the same failure the Outlook side already fixed for its own Gone answer (comment at 2595-2598).
all.fix: In is_expired_sync_token, also accept an Api error whose message contains EXPIRED_SYNC_TOKEN or "sync token is expired" (ignore case): `status == 410 || msg.contains("EXPIRED_SYNC_TOKEN") || msg.to_ascii_lowercase().contains("sync token is expired")`. The provider message keeps up to 500 characters, so match the short phrase too in case the details block is cut off. Change the test at 6036 to use 400 with that body.
all.if_skipped: From one week after setup, Google contacts quietly stop syncing in both directions, and the only sign is one error line on each sync.
all.ledger_entry: none found; the changelog entry near docs/changelog.md:13416 says the recovery "triggers only when Google says the marker is too old", which assumes the 410

verdict.reason:
I checked the code line by line and it matches the finding. contacts_sync.rs:854 sets SYNC_TOKEN_EXPIRED to 410, and is_expired_sync_token (861-869) matches only Error::Api { status: 410 }. The People API answers through google_api.rs list_contacts (717-742), which goes through read_the_body (1038-1050). That turns any status of 400 or above into Error::Api with the real status, and with_retry does not retry a 400. So a 400 falls to `Err(e) => return Err(e)` at 2386. That return comes before the sync state is saved, so the dead token stays stored. wx_app.rs:30979-30980 only pushes "Google contacts: ..." onto the errors. Nothing in src clears or resets a sync state. Every later sync therefore fails the same way.

The premise that Google sends 400 rather than 410 also holds up. The People API uses google.rpc canonical codes, and none of them maps to HTTP 410. 410 is the Calendar API's answer, and calendar.rs:1346 handles it correctly there. The repo already reads the People API this way: contacts_sync.rs:884-890 and the helper at 6553-6569 say Google turns down an etag precondition with "400, with FAILED_PRECONDITION", taken from Google's documentation. The unit test at 6036 even uses Google's own words, "Sync token is expired", yet builds them on a hand-made 410. The scripted test at 6903 fakes the 410 too, so neither test could catch this. Git history shows the 410 has been there since the first contacts-sync commit (6a2601cf, 2026-07-26), and nothing records a live answer. Like the finding, this rests on Google's documented error model and not on a captured response.

The ledger has no entry for it. WINDOWS.md has no mention of a sync token or of a Google marker being too old. The nearby entries (262, 485, 614) are about CardDAV markers and other gaps. The changelog at 13421 assumes the trigger fires.

One overstatement: "stops syncing in both directions" is only partly true. Deletions and edits to contacts Google already knows are pushed before the read (2359, 2363-2365), so they still go out. What stops for good is everything coming in from Google, plus contacts newly made here, because create_contact runs only inside `if read_the_whole_address_book` (2493).

The fix is correct in shape but must not drop 410. The Outlook path at 2601 reuses this same function, and Graph really does answer an expired delta link with 410 Gone. Must: from about a week after setup, Google contacts sync stops for every Google user, the fix is two lines and safe, and phase 14 is putting real Google accounts in front of the tester now.
verdict.corrected_problem: The marker Google stores is treated as too old only when the answer is HTTP 410. Under the People API's error model, an expired sync token comes back as 400 FAILED_PRECONDITION, with the reason EXPIRED_SYNC_TOKEN and the message "Sync token is expired...". That answer falls through to `return Err(e)` at contacts_sync.rs:2386, before the new state is saved, so the dead token is asked with on every later sync. Nothing coming in from Google arrives again, and contacts newly made here are never created at Google, because that create runs only on a full read (2493). Edits and deletions to contacts Google already knows still go out, because they are pushed before the read. This rests on Google's documented error model, which the repo already follows at 884-890 for etags. Nobody has seen a live answer.
verdict.corrected_fix:
Widen is_expired_sync_token and keep 410, because Outlook's Gone path at 2601 shares this function and Graph does send 410:
`Error::Api { status, message, .. } => *status == SYNC_TOKEN_EXPIRED || (*status == 400 && { let m = message.to_ascii_lowercase(); m.contains("expired_sync_token") || m.contains("sync token is expired") })`.
The short phrase matters because redact_provider_message keeps only 500 characters, which can cut off the details block. In test_only_a_gone_answer_makes_the_address_book_be_read_again at 6036, keep the 410 assertion and add a 400 case with Google's body, then rename the test. Add a matching end-to-end case next to the one at 6894, with ScriptedGoogle sending that 400 body; its fixed message "the marker was refused" would not match today. Correct the changelog sentence at 13421 in the same commit.

all.title: A contact typed here after the first sync never reaches Outlook, and reaches Google only on a full read
all.location: src/application/contacts_sync.rs:2492-2543 (Google, `if read_the_whole_address_book`) and 2706-2739 (Microsoft, `if delta_link.is_none()`); new contacts are built at src/presentation/contact_convert.rs:315-317, 341, 345-356
all.what_this_is: A contact made in the Contacts window is saved with pending = true, source_provider = made here and an empty known_to list. The only code that creates it at Google or Outlook is the "push contacts no address book knows" block at the end of each sync.
all.problem: That block runs only when the sync read the whole address book. For Microsoft that is only the very first sync, because it checks whether a delta link was stored before this run, and a link is stored from then on. Even the expired-link fallback at 2599-2608 does not run it. For Google it runs only when there is no token or the token expired. changes_waiting_for (1855-1922) skips any contact with no known_to entry, so nothing else sends it. The tests (7139, 7416) cover only the first sync.
all.concrete_case: Outlook account, synced once. The user adds "Dr Patel" in the Contacts window. Each later sync stores no identity for her, and Outlook never gets her, with no error and no count. On Google she waits until the token expires (7 days), and with finding 1 that full read never happens, so she never arrives there either. The changelog entry at docs/changelog.md:13416 shows this was a side effect: once tokens were stored, "offered on every sync" became "offered on a full read only".
all.fix: Delete the two guards so the create block runs on every sync: remove `if read_the_whole_address_book {` and `if delta_link.is_none() {` and their closing braces. The block already skips anything with an identity or that came from that address book. Add one test per provider: a marker is stored, a pending contact with no identity exists, and created_remote is 1.
all.if_skipped: People add contacts here, see them on this computer, and never find them on their phone. Nothing tells them.
all.ledger_entry: none

verdict.reason:
I read every line the finding cites, and it holds. The Contacts window's new_contact (managers.rs:2796) calls to_stored with replacing = None. That gives pending = true, source_provider = "local" and an empty known_to (contact_convert.rs:315-317, 341, 345-356).

changes_waiting_for drops any contact that has no identity for the address book being synced: the `?` on the known_to lookup at 1892-1895 returns early. So the only code that creates the contact at the provider is the block at 2493 (Google) or 2707 (Microsoft). Those two blocks and the CardDAV path are the only callers of create_contact in src.

Microsoft: list_contacts returns Graph's @odata.deltaLink (microsoft_graph.rs:1113), and remember_this_syncs_marker stores it. Nothing in src deletes a sync_state row. So from the second sync on, `delta_link.is_none()` is false and the create block never runs. The 410 fallback at 2599-2608 also leaves the stored delta_link as Some, so it does not run the block either.

Google: requestSyncToken=true (google_api.rs:532) means a token is stored, so the block runs only when the token is missing or when the error matches is_expired_sync_token. That function matches only status 410 (contacts_sync.rs:854-868).

The existing tests, 7139, 7416 and 8811, store no marker, so they cover only the first sync. Nothing in .planning/WINDOWS.md, docs/ALPHA_TESTING.md or the phase 14 notes records this.

The "avoid duplicates" comment is stale. It dates from 6a2601cf. After the first sync, every provider contact is already stored with an identity. So step 1 of the_stored_contact_this_is matches that stored row by its identifier, and a contact typed here with the same address is pushed as a second copy on a full read too. Pushing on every sync adds no new kind of duplicate.

CardDAV already pushes contacts made here on every sync (carddav_sync.rs:299, made_here at 358), so dropping the guard matches the newest code. No guards.toml record is anchored on either guard line.

The bug is silent: no error and no count. It hits the most common case, someone adding a contact after setup. Every Outlook account is affected for good. Google gets the contact only on a full re-read, and only if that re-read is ever triggered.
verdict.corrected_problem: The code that creates a contact made here at Google or Outlook runs only on a read of the whole address book. For Outlook that means the first sync only. The delta link is stored from then on, and the expired-link fallback still sees a stored link, so it skips the block too. For Google it means only when no token is stored or the error matches is_expired_sync_token. changes_waiting_for needs an identity for that address book, so nothing else sends the contact. A contact typed after the first sync never reaches Outlook. It reaches Google only if a full re-read happens. Nothing reports either case. One more effect: a create that fails during Outlook's first sync is never tried again.
verdict.corrected_fix:
Remove `if read_the_whole_address_book {` (2493) and `if delta_link.is_none() {` (2707), with their closing braces, so both create blocks run on every sync. Keep the existing filter: pending, empty known_to, and not from this address book. Leave the is_a_full_sync arguments to remember_this_syncs_marker as they are.

Update three comments in the same change:
- 2494 "Only push on full sync to avoid duplicates"
- 2706 "Push local-only contacts on full sync"
- 2530 "on the next full read", which becomes "on the next sync"

Red first: add one test per provider. Each one calls a_marker_from_the_last_run, saves a pending contact typed here with no identity, and sets accepts_a_contact: true. Each asserts created_remote == 1 and sent.len() == 1. Both tests are red before the change.

Adding tests to contacts_sync.rs changes its test count. The guard-record count check will then flag the records that name the file. Run the `scripts/guards.sh --remeasure` command it prints, and name the count check in the red commit, as CLAUDE.md describes.

all.title: The Outlook calendar only ever sees the date range of its first sync
all.location: src/application/calendar.rs:1315-1355 and 1438-1449; src/service/microsoft_graph.rs:570-585 and 1192-1218
all.what_this_is: The Outlook calendar sync uses Graph's calendarView/delta. The first request gives a start and end (180 days back, 365 days ahead). Each sync after that sends only the stored delta link.
all.problem: Microsoft's page on calendar view delta says the delta and next links encode the startDateTime and endDateTime of the first request, and that tracking is specific to that range. The code keeps one delta link for ever. It starts a new round only after a 410, and even then it reuses the old link's absence check rather than a new range. So the window never moves forward. last_full_sync is stored (sync_marker.rs:56-60) but nothing reads it here.
all.concrete_case: First sync on 1 Oct 2026, so the range ends on 1 Oct 2027. On 1 Feb 2027 a meeting is booked in Outlook for 15 Nov 2027. It is outside the stored range and never arrives here. From 1 Oct 2027 on, no new Outlook meeting arrives at all, and Due Now never alerts for them.
all.fix: In sync_microsoft_calendar, treat the stored link as absent when the state's last_full_sync is older than about 30 days: `let delta_link = state.as_ref().filter(|s| still_fresh(s.last_full_sync.as_deref())).and_then(|s| s.delta_link.as_deref());`. The existing `delta_link.is_none()` then records the new full sync. While there, use one named window (caldav_sync.rs:675-678 already has HOW_FAR_BACK_THE_READ_ASKS and HOW_FAR_AHEAD_THE_READ_ASKS) instead of the three copies of 180 and 365 at calendar.rs:927-928, 951-952 and 1322-1323.
all.if_skipped: An Outlook calendar slowly goes blind. After a year it shows nothing new, and a missed meeting is the first sign.
all.ledger_entry: none

verdict.reason:
Confirmed by reading the code. In calendar.rs:1315-1327 the window (180 days back, 365 ahead) is built only when no delta link is stored. After the first sync a link is always stored (1438-1449), and nothing ever clears it: there is no clear or reset of sync state anywhere in src, and last_full_sync is written by sync_marker.rs:56-60 but never read. list_events (microsoft_graph.rs:1201-1204) uses the stored link and ignores start and end. Microsoft's event-delta page (fetched 2026-10-14) says a delta round is "bound by the date range of a calendarView", and that the start and end are encoded into the nextLink and deltaLink tokens. It also says events outside that range that are added or changed come back under @removed. So the window stays fixed at the first sync's dates. The path runs in production (wx_app.rs:31401). It is not in .planning/WINDOWS.md. No test covers it: the tests that sync more than once call forget_the_delta_marker between syncs, so each read starts again.

Two things make it worse than the finding says. (1) The 410 fallback at 1346-1352 is broken. It only runs when a link was stored, and then start and end are None (line 1326). The retry therefore asks for calendarView/delta?$top=100 with no window, which Graph refuses. The error goes up through `?`, the dead link stays stored, and every later sync fails the same way. That is the exact failure the comment at 1331-1334 says was fixed. No test exercises this retry. (2) An event created here, dated after the stored window's end, is pushed to Outlook. The next delta reports it under @removed, as Microsoft's page says. Lines 1380-1388 delete any stored row with that id without checking the date range, so the meeting disappears here.

The proposed fix (ignore the link when last_full_sync is older than about 30 days) is not enough on its own. A 410 on a fresh link still retries with no window.
verdict.corrected_problem: The Outlook calendar view's delta link carries the date range of the first request, and the code keeps that link for ever. last_full_sync is stored and never read. So from the first sync on, the app only ever sees meetings dated between 180 days before and 365 days after that sync. Outlook reports a meeting outside that range under @removed, and lines 1380-1388 delete the copy here without checking dates. So a meeting created here and dated past the window's end vanishes from this program at the next sync. The 410 recovery cannot work either. The window is built only when no link is stored, so the retry after Gone sends no startDateTime or endDateTime. Graph refuses that, the error returns before the marker is saved, the dead link stays stored, and the Outlook calendar stops syncing for good.
verdict.corrected_fix: In sync_microsoft_calendar: (a) always compute (start, end), removing the `if delta_link.is_none()` gate at 1320-1327. list_events ignores them when a link is passed, and the 410 retry then carries a window. (b) Treat the stored link as absent once state.last_full_sync is more than about 30 days old (`state.as_ref().filter(|s| still_fresh(s.last_full_sync.as_deref())).and_then(|s| s.delta_link.as_deref())`). (c) Pass "this run read a window", meaning no usable link or the 410 branch was taken, as is_a_full_sync instead of `delta_link.is_none()`. That way last_full_sync also moves after a 410 recovery. Red tests first: one with a stale last_full_sync whose request must contain startDateTime, and one where the server answers 410 and then 200, whose second request must contain startDateTime and endDateTime. Known cost to note in the commit: a fresh full read does not report deletions made since the last delta call, so a meeting deleted at Outlook within one sync interval of a refresh can linger here. The 410 path already has that gap. Using HOW_FAR_BACK_THE_READ_ASKS and HOW_FAR_AHEAD_THE_READ_ASKS in place of the three 180/365 copies is optional cleanup, not part of the fix.

all.title: A subscribed calendar feed shows a moved or cancelled day of a repeating event wrongly
all.location: src/application/caldav_sync.rs:1150-1201 (refresh_subscription); compare the CalDAV path at 841-843 and 950-963; src/service/ical_subscription.rs:98-112; RECURRENCE-ID kept at src/service/caldav.rs:1039
all.what_this_is: A subscribed .ics feed (holidays, a school or team calendar) is fetched in full on each refresh and written into one calendar here.
all.problem: A feed carries a repeating event and its changed days as separate VEVENTs with the same UID, told apart by RECURRENCE-ID. parse_ics keeps all of them. The CalDAV sync splits them and folds each changed day into its series with one_caldav_day_kept_out_of_its_series. refresh_subscription does not: it saves every VEVENT as a plain event under the shared UID. The CalDAV comment at 831-840 describes exactly the overwrite this causes.
all.concrete_case: A feed has "Assembly", weekly on Tuesday at 09:00, and one VEVENT with RECURRENCE-ID for 3 Nov moved to 14:00. On first refresh two rows are stored with the same provider id: the series and a one-off at 14:00. The series still draws 3 Nov at 09:00 (no exception added), so that Tuesday shows twice. A cancelled day (STATUS:CANCELLED) still shows at 09:00. On the next refresh both VEVENTs map to the one row held_by_uid kept, so each is written over it in turn. If the feed lists the changed day before the series, that row becomes a second copy of the series, and every Tuesday then shows twice.
all.fix: Split remote_events by `recurrence_id.is_none()` as the CalDAV path does. Save the whole events in the existing loop. Pass each changed day to one_caldav_day_kept_out_of_its_series, with in_feed as a HashSet<String> standing in for seen_uids. About ten lines, and it reuses the code that already handles this.
all.if_skipped: Subscribed calendars show moved meetings at both times and cancelled ones as still on, and a later refresh can double a whole series.
all.ledger_entry: none

verdict.reason: The defect is real and reachable: wx_app.rs:31459 calls refresh_subscription for every feed calendar. The finding gets the mechanism wrong, though, and the real outcome is worse than it says. Each step checks out against the code. parse_ics (ical_subscription.rs:98-112) hands each VEVENT to parse_ical_vevent on its own, and event_from_its_own_lines keeps RECURRENCE-ID (caldav.rs:1039). refresh_subscription (caldav_sync.rs:1164-1201) saves every VEVENT through caldav_event_to_local with provider_event_id = UID and never splits on recurrence_id. The CalDAV path does split (841-843, 950-963). The claim of "two rows with the same provider id" is wrong. calendar_events has UNIQUE(account_id, calendar_id, provider_event_id) (mod.rs:2458), and save_calendar_event upserts on that key (calendar.rs:233), so the changed day lands on the series' row even on the first refresh, when held_by_uid is empty. The outcome is last-written-wins on every refresh, decided by feed order. Series first, moved or cancelled day after: the series row becomes that one day, with no RRULE, its own start and status, and provider_recurrence_id set. Every other occurrence of the repeating event disappears from the calendar. Changed day first, series after: the series survives, but the move and the cancellation are lost, so the day shows at the old time or still shows when it was called off. Nothing ever adds the day to the series' exception_dates, and only exception_dates suppress an occurrence (occurrences.rs:112). No subscription test uses RECURRENCE-ID (the only RECURRENCE-ID fixtures in caldav_sync.rs are CalDAV ones). The ledger has no entry for this: entries 635, 638 and 729-734 are about invitations and Google/Outlook days, not feeds. The proposed fix is the smallest one that works and reuses tested code. one_caldav_day_kept_out_of_its_series already takes the calendar pair, deleted_here and a HashSet<String>. one_day_kept_out_of_the_series, called with TheProviderItself, does not mark the series pending, so say_the_change_cannot_be_saved does not fire. And because carry_over_local_only does not carry provider_recurrence_id, a row already damaged this way is corrected by the series VEVENT on the first refresh after the fix. Must: a subscribed team or school calendar silently loses a whole weekly series, or shows moved and cancelled days wrongly, and the fix is small.
verdict.corrected_problem: A feed carries a repeating event and its changed days as separate VEVENTs with the same UID, told apart by RECURRENCE-ID. parse_ics keeps all of them, each with recurrence_id set (caldav.rs:1039). refresh_subscription (caldav_sync.rs:1164-1201) saves every VEVENT as a plain event with provider_event_id = UID. The table's UNIQUE(account_id, calendar_id, provider_event_id) (mod.rs:2458) and save_calendar_event's ON CONFLICT on that key (calendar.rs:233) collapse them onto one row, on the first refresh and on every one after, so the VEVENT written last wins. Take "Assembly", weekly on Tuesday at 09:00, with a VEVENT for 3 Nov moved to 14:00 (or STATUS:CANCELLED). If the feed lists the series first, the row becomes a single 3 Nov event with no RRULE: every other Tuesday disappears, and with a cancelled day the whole series shows as one cancelled event. If the changed day comes first, the series overwrites it: 3 Nov shows at 09:00, and a cancelled day still shows as on, because nothing adds it to the series' exception_dates. The CalDAV path avoids this by splitting on recurrence_id (841-843) and folding each changed day with one_caldav_day_kept_out_of_its_series (950-963). result.created is also counted once per VEVENT for what is one row.
verdict.corrected_fix: In refresh_subscription, make in_feed a HashSet<String>. Split remote_events with .iter().partition(|e| e.recurrence_id.is_none()). Run the existing loop over the whole events only, inserting remote.uid.clone(). Then, for each changed day with a recurrence_id, call one_caldav_day_kept_out_of_its_series(cache, (account_id, &calendar.id), changed, the_day_it_was, &deleted_here, &mut in_feed, &mut result)?, the same call the CalDAV path makes at 950-963. The compound "uid:recurrence-id" ids it inserts keep the removal pass from deleting the changed-day rows. That is about ten lines. The red test is a feed holding a weekly series and one moved RECURRENCE-ID VEVENT, run in both orders. Assert that the series keeps its RRULE and gains the moved day as an exception date, and that the moved day is stored under the compound id at its new time. Add a cancelled-day case that asserts the day goes onto the series' exception_dates.

all.title: A full read never removes what the provider deleted while the marker was stale
all.location: src/application/contacts_sync.rs:2379-2385 and 2389-2490 (Google), 2599-2608 and 2610-2704 (Outlook); src/application/calendar.rs:945-959 and 975-1034 (Google), 1344-1355 and 1366-1421 (Outlook); compare tasks_sync.rs:1024-1032 and caldav_sync.rs:965-981
all.what_this_is: With a valid marker, each provider reports deletions outright: Google marks a contact deleted or an event cancelled, and Graph sends @removed. When the marker is refused, the sync reads everything again.
all.problem: A full read lists only what still exists, so deletions made since the last good read are simply missing from it. The contacts and Google or Outlook calendar reads never remove a row for being missing. The tasks sync and the CalDAV sync both do, with guards. The Google calendar read also starts a full read after any error with a token, not only after Gone (945-959), so a single 503 has the same effect.
all.concrete_case: The laptop is shut for two weeks. During that time a meeting is cancelled on the phone and a contact is deleted. On return the stored marker is refused, the full read does not list either item, and the new marker is stored. The cancelled meeting stays here for good and its alert still fires. The contact stays, and if somebody edits it, each sync then reports a failed update for a contact Google no longer has.
all.fix: After a read that was a full read, take off every row this provider knows that the read did not name and that has no unsent change. For contacts, call the existing one_address_book_deleted_them for each one. For calendars, use drop_synced_calendar_event, limited to the window asked for, as caldav_sync's may_be_taken_off_this_computer already does. In read_one_google_calendar, fall back to a full read only on 410, as contacts_sync already does.
all.if_skipped: After any break of a week or so, deleted meetings and contacts come back as ghosts that never leave, and a cancelled meeting still alerts.
all.ledger_entry: none for contacts or calendars; ledger 253 records the same gap for notes only

verdict.reason:
I checked this line by line and the gap is real. When the marker is refused, the Google contacts read (contacts_sync.rs 2379-2385) and the Outlook contacts read (2601-2606) both read the whole address book again. After that, the loops (2389-2490, 2610-2704) only act on people the answer names: deleted ones are taken off through `metadata.deleted` or `removed`, and the rest are written. No pass compares the rows held here with what came back. Neither full read lists a deleted person (`connections_url` sends no syncToken, and a Graph delta with no link has no @removed). So anybody deleted at the provider while the marker was stale stays here.

The Google calendar is the same. `events_url` never asks for showDeleted, so a full read with timeMin and timeMax leaves out a cancelled single meeting. The loop at 975-1034 removes a row only when Google says `status == "cancelled"`. The tasks sync (tasks_sync.rs 1024-1032, `gone_from` when every list was read) and CalDAV (caldav_sync.rs 965-981, `may_be_taken_off_this_computer` plus `drop_synced_calendar_event`) both remove rows that are missing from a complete answer, and both have guards.

`read_one_google_calendar` 947-959 does fall back to a full read on any error when a marker exists. `is_expired_sync_token` in contacts_sync limits the contacts fallback to 410 on purpose (861 and its test at 6035). The finding's "a single 503" overstates it, though: `list_events` already retries 429 and 5xx three times through `with_retry`, so only a lasting fault or a non-retried error, such as a body that will not parse or a 4xx, reaches the fallback. One test pins the any-error fallback: every_google_calendar.rs about line 695 uses a 200 response whose body is `refused`. A change to fall back only on 410 has to change that test.

The finding gets one quarter wrong: the Outlook calendar. In `sync_microsoft_calendar`, `start` and `end` are only set when `delta_link.is_none()` (1320-1327). The 410 fallback at 1350-1351 passes those same `None` values. So `calendar_view_url` asks for `calendarView/delta?$top=100` with no startDateTime or endDateTime. Graph requires both on a first calendarView delta request, so the fallback most likely fails and returns Err through `?`. The dead link stays stored, and the Outlook calendar stops syncing for good, which is worse than ghost rows. Nothing tests this fallback; a grep for 410 in the calendar tests finds nothing.

There is a caveat on Google contacts that I cannot settle from the repo. The fallback assumes People API answers 410 for an expired token. As I recall, Google documents that error as reason EXPIRED_SYNC_TOKEN and it may arrive as 400 FAILED_PRECONDITION. In that case the full read never happens and every sync fails instead. It needs a live check.

None of this is in .planning/WINDOWS.md. Ledger 253 is about notes only, and 825 is a different calendar matter. No doc records a decision not to remove rows that are missing from the answer. The comment at contacts_sync 1137 contrasts "merely missing" only when explaining why an explicit deletion takes waiting work with it.

The finding's estimate of 12 lines is low. The work is four sites with different scoping: Google calendar rows per calendar (`its_rows`), the window, the days of a series, and contacts that more than one address book knows. That is closer to 40-60 lines plus tests. I put it at should rather than must: the rows are stale and nothing is lost, but a cancelled meeting still alerting is visible, and phase 14 is about to exercise exactly these accounts.
verdict.corrected_problem:
After a full read, the Google and Outlook contact reads and the Google calendar read never remove a row for being missing. A full read lists only what still exists, so anything deleted or cancelled at the provider while the marker was stale stays here. The tasks sync and CalDAV both remove rows missing from a complete answer, with guards. Two more defects sit beside this one.

(a) read_one_google_calendar (calendar.rs 947-959) falls back to a full read on any error once a marker exists, not only on 410. Only failures that outlast with_retry, or that it does not retry, reach that fallback.

(b) The Outlook calendar's 410 fallback (calendar.rs 1350-1351) passes the start and end that were left as None because a delta link existed. It therefore asks calendarView/delta for no time window, which Graph refuses. The dead link stays stored and the Outlook calendar stops syncing rather than reading in full.

Unverified: the Google contacts fallback assumes People API answers an expired token with 410. If Google answers 400 FAILED_PRECONDITION or EXPIRED_SYNC_TOKEN instead, that sync fails every time instead.
verdict.corrected_fix:
1. In sync_microsoft_calendar's 410 arm, compute the 180-day-back and 365-day-ahead window and pass it. Today it passes the None start and end.

2. In read_one_google_calendar, fall back only on Error::Api { status: 410 }. Change the every_google_calendar test to answer 410 instead of the unparseable `refused` body.

3. Have each read report whether it was a full read. Google contacts already has read_the_whole_address_book; the other three reads need the same flag. After the loop of a full read that succeeded, go through the rows this provider knows that the answer did not name. Skip any row that has an unsent change, is held for a choice, or is in deleted_here.
   - Contacts: call one_address_book_deleted_them for the rows the account holds whose id_in(that address book) the answer did not name.
   - Calendars: use drop_synced_calendar_event, limited to the calendar the read was filed under (its_rows or filed_under). Only drop a row whose stored times fall inside the window asked for. Reuse caldav_sync's WhatTheAnswerCovers::OnlyBetween and would_have_named, made pub(crate), so a series that starts before the window is kept.

4. Write a red test for each of the four reads first: a stored row, a refused marker, then a full answer that omits the row. Also add the Outlook test that the fallback URL carries startDateTime.

all.title: The contacts sync reloads the whole address book once per contact it reads
all.location: src/application/contacts_sync.rs:2404, 2416 (Google) and 2623, 2635 (Outlook); src/data/message_cache/contacts.rs:259-276
all.what_this_is: For each person the provider returns, the read loop calls cache.get_contacts_for_account(account_id) again so it can find the matching stored contact.
all.problem: That call reads every contact row (31 columns, including the vCard text and the JSON lists) and then builds a map of every identity. Doing it once per arriving contact makes the read quadratic in the size of the address book. The test fixtures hold one or two contacts, so no test feels it.
all.concrete_case: A Google address book of 3,000 contacts on the first sync, or on every full read after a token expires, means 3,000 full loads: about 9 million rows decoded and 3,000 identity maps of 3,000 entries each, on the worker that also runs the calendar and tasks syncs. Five thousand contacts is about 25 million rows. This is an estimate from the code; I did not run it.
all.fix: Load `let mut locals = cache.get_contacts_for_account(account_id)?;` once before the loop. After each save_contact or drop, update that Vec: replace the entry by id, push a newly created one, or remove a dropped one. Then two people arriving with the same address still match the way they do now. Do the same in both syncs.
all.if_skipped: The first sync of a large address book, and every full read after that, takes far longer than it needs to.
all.ledger_entry: none

verdict.reason:
Confirmed line by line. In sync_google_contacts the loop over every person from list_contacts calls cache.get_contacts_for_account(account_id) at contacts_sync.rs:2416, and at :2404 for deletions. sync_microsoft_contacts does the same at :2635 and :2623. get_contacts_for_account (contacts.rs:259-276) selects 31 columns for every contact in the account, then with_their_address_books builds a HashMap of every identity. google_api.rs:717-742 pages through the whole address book, so on a full read (no sync token, or a token Google reports as too old, :2374-2387) the loop runs once per contact and each pass re-reads the whole table. The code admits the cost in a comment at contacts.rs:195-197: "a sync reads the contacts once per remote contact already". There is no ledger entry. A grep of .planning/WINDOWS.md for the function name, the file lines, "once per remote contact" and "quadratic" found nothing.

The finding gets three details wrong and misses a third site:
1. The sync does not share a worker with the calendar and tasks syncs. spawn_contacts_sync (wx_app.rs:30904-30933) runs on its own spawn_blocking thread with its own MessageCache. The cost is a slow background sync, not other syncs held up behind it.
2. On a first sync the table grows from empty, so the total is about N squared over 2 rows (about 4.5 million for 3,000 contacts). The full N squared applies to a re-read after an expired token.
3. The deletion reloads only fire on delta reads, so their cost is deletions times N.
4. Missed site: carddav_sync.rs:384. take_in_one_card reloads the whole account once per card, and whats_in (:195) reads every card on every sync. For a large CardDAV book the cost is quadratic on every sync, not only on a full read.

The fix works with two caveats:
- The snapshot widens the window in which a contact edited in the interface during the sync is missed. The sync uses a separate connection, and today it re-reads just before each decision.
- The deletion helper decides whether to drop a contact or only take this address book off it, so the caller cannot update the snapshot without knowing which happened.

Matching order is safe. Every created or merged contact already lists this address book in known_to (for example google_person_to_contact sets it, :2952), so it only matches by id. Appending to the snapshot therefore cannot change which contact an address match finds.
verdict.corrected_problem:
Three contact syncs reload the whole account's contacts once per contact the provider sends: Google (contacts_sync.rs:2416, plus :2404 for deletions), Outlook (:2635 and :2623) and CardDAV (carddav_sync.rs:384, in take_in_one_card). Each reload selects all 31 columns for every contact in the account, including vcard_raw and avatar_data_base64 that CardDAV and imported contacts carry. It then builds an identity map of the whole account (contacts.rs:259-276).

For Google and Outlook this is quadratic on a full read: the first sync, and a re-read after the stored marker expires. A first sync of 3,000 contacts decodes about 4.5 million rows. A re-read of an existing 3,000 decodes about 9 million. CardDAV reads every card on every sync (whats_in, carddav_sync.rs:195), so a large CardDAV book pays the quadratic cost every time it syncs.

The work runs on the contacts sync's own blocking thread (wx_app.rs:30904), so the interface stays responsive and no other sync waits on it. The contacts sync itself takes far longer than it needs to. The comment at contacts.rs:195-197 acknowledges the per-contact read, and no ledger entry tracks it.
verdict.corrected_fix:
In each of the three syncs, load the account's contacts once before the loop, as `let mut locals = cache.get_contacts_for_account(account_id)?;`, and keep that Vec in step with every write:
- In the match arm, take the index of the matched contact instead of holding a reference to it.
- On a merge, bind the struct returned by a_change_here_that_lost, save that exact struct, and write it to `locals[i]`.
- On a create, push the created contact onto the Vec. Order does not matter, because a new contact already lists this address book in known_to and only ever matches by id.
- On a deletion, have one_address_book_deleted_them return what it did. Either it returns the remaining contact (`local.no_longer_in(book)`), which replaces `locals[i]`, or it dropped the contact, which is removed from the Vec. Do not copy that decision into the caller.
- Leave the per-contact `cache.is_held_for_a_choice(&local.id)?` check as it is. It is a single-row query and stays fresh.
- In take_in_one_card, pass `&mut Vec<ContactEntry>` from the caller's loop in place of the read at :384.

Say in a comment that the snapshot misses an edit made in the interface while the loop runs, and that the window is now the loop's length rather than one iteration.

Red test first: a sync of two people with the same address must still produce one contact and one create, as it does now. Pair it with a count of contact reads per sync, through a test-only counter on MessageCache or a test that the reads do not grow with the number of people.

all.title: Two Outbox passes can send the same message twice
all.location: src/presentation/wx_app.rs:24529-24786 (flush_outbox; callers 6005, 6012, 6535, 16836, 19319, 31844); src/data/message_cache/outbox.rs:122-133
all.what_this_is: flush_outbox is the send loop. Each call spawns a task that reads every ready row in the Outbox, sends each one over SMTP, and deletes the row only after the send returns (24701).
all.problem: Nothing stops a second pass while the first is still running, and reading a row does not claim it. A second pass reads rows the first pass is still sending. Each send builds a fresh Message-ID (src/service/protocols/smtp.rs:152), so recipients get two separate messages and Sent gets two copies.
all.concrete_case: Undo Send hold set to 0. Send message A with a 15 MB attachment; the upload takes 30 seconds. Ten seconds later send message B from a second composer; its Send calls flush_outbox (19319). Pass 2 reads A (its row is still there) and B, and A goes out twice. The same happens with holds on: two held messages whose holds end a few seconds apart start two passes from the 1-second tick (6518-6535). Pressing Send Queued Mail twice does it too.
all.fix: A process-wide `static SENDING: AtomicBool` and `static AGAIN: AtomicBool`. At the top of flush_outbox: if `SENDING.swap(true)` then `AGAIN.store(true)` and return. At the end of the task, run the pass again while `AGAIN.swap(false)`, then clear SENDING. About 10 lines, no schema change. One test: two calls against a stub whose first send blocks, asserting one send per row.
all.if_skipped: People receive duplicate mail that cannot be taken back, and Sent holds both copies.
all.ledger_entry: None. Searched .planning/WINDOWS.md for flush_outbox, 'twice' and 'second pass'.

verdict.reason:
I read the code and the race is there. flush_outbox (src/presentation/wx_app.rs:24529) spawns a task. That task reads every ready row (24590, through outbox_messages_that_may_go_now at outbox.rs:122-133, which only filters on time and claims nothing), signs in to IMAP for the Sent copy (24663), sends, and deletes the row only after the send returns (24701). Nothing holds a second pass back. I grepped src for a flag or lock: OutboxFlushComplete (23704) only updates the status line, ID_FLUSH_OUTBOX is never disabled, and MessageCache uses busy_timeout and takes no exclusive lock. All six callers are as the finding lists them.

The case happens with the default 10-second hold:
- Message A's hold ends at t=10, and the 1-second tick (6518-6535) starts pass 1, which reads [A].
- Message B, sent 3 seconds after A, comes due at t=13, and `anything_reached_its_moment` starts pass 2. Each row triggers its own pass when its moment comes.
- Pass 1 is still signing in to IMAP, so A's row is still there. Pass 2 reads [A, B], and A goes out twice. Both passes also file a Sent copy (24723-24736).

Pressing Send Queued Mail during a pass does the same, and so does a failed row being retried by every trigger, which ledger 720 widened to every account.

One part of the finding is wrong. Queued mail does not get a fresh Message-ID. mail_controller.rs:248 uses message_id::derived(queue_id, from), so both copies carry the same ID; smtp.rs:152 is Email::simple, which the queue path does not use. The SMTP server still delivers twice. Gmail may fold the two copies into one; Outlook and Thunderbird show both, and Sent gets two copies.

There is no ledger entry. I searched .planning/WINDOWS.md for flush_outbox, twice, second pass and concurrent, and read every line about the Outbox; none is about this.

The proposed AtomicBool pair is not the smallest safe fix:
- A request that arrives between the final AGAIN check and clearing SENDING is lost.
- A panic inside the task leaves SENDING set, and no mail sends again until restart.
- The task has five early returns, and every one of them would have to clear the flag.

A tokio Mutex (tokio has "full" features, so const_new works) avoids all three.
verdict.corrected_problem: Nothing stops a second Outbox pass while one is running, and reading a row does not claim it. A second pass reads the rows the first is still sending, because the first deletes each row only after its send returns (wx_app.rs:24701). Both passes then send the row and file a Sent copy. Both copies carry the same Message-ID, derived from the queue row (mail_controller.rs:248), but SMTP still delivers both. Some clients, such as Gmail, may fold them into one; Outlook and Thunderbird show both, and Sent holds two copies. This happens with the default 10-second hold when two messages come due a few seconds apart: each due row starts its own pass on the 1-second tick (6518-6535), and a pass spends seconds signing in to IMAP and SMTP before it deletes anything. Pressing Send Queued Mail while a pass is running does the same.
verdict.corrected_fix: Make the passes run one at a time. Add `static ONE_PASS_AT_A_TIME: tokio::sync::Mutex<()> = tokio::sync::Mutex::const_new(());` and make `let _one_pass = ONE_PASS_AT_A_TIME.lock().await;` the first line inside the spawned task, before the queue is read at 24590. A second pass then waits, reads the queue after the first has deleted what it sent, and finds only what is still due. The lock is released on all five early returns and on a panic, and no request is lost. That is about 3 lines and needs no schema change. For the test, give the lock to a small helper that the pass goes through. Run two concurrent passes over one queued row against the loopback SMTP server already in the tree (smtp::against_a_server_that_answers). Assert that the server received one DATA command and that the row is gone. Without the lock the test should fail with two.

all.title: Announcements made close together overwrite each other, so only the last one is heard
all.location: src/presentation/accessibility.rs:347-398 (every announce* flushes at once) and 435-468 (flush_announcements delivers each line separately); src/presentation/accessibility/screen_reader.rs:120-134, 600-608; src/presentation/wx_app.rs:6392-6420
all.what_this_is: Every announcement ends as SetWindowTextW on one hidden static control plus EVENT_OBJECT_LIVEREGIONCHANGED. The queue releases up to 4 lines a second plus every Urgent line, and every announce call flushes at once. The tick drains all pending UI updates in one go, and many arms announce.
all.problem: Lines released together are written to the same window microseconds apart. The screen reader reads the window's name when it handles the event, so it reads the last text. The code already knows this: handed_over_together (screen_reader.rs:448-484) joins held lines for exactly this reason, and docs/changelog.md:9676 says 'several status sentences in a row leave only the last one heard'. The join was applied to the startup hold and to one Calendar window, not to the path every other announcement takes. The Urgent/Important mapping is also ignored on this path; it only reaches the notification API, which is skipped when the live region works. The unit tests count lines released to the bridge, so they stay green while a person hears one line.
all.concrete_case: A POP account with a wrong SMTP password. flush_outbox sends OutboxSendResult (failure with the server's reason), ConnectionStatusChanged(Error) and OutboxFlushComplete back to back with no network wait between them (24743-24779). The next 50 ms tick drains all three, each arm announces, and the window text ends as 'The Outbox is done: 0 sent, 1 not sent.' The reason the mail did not go is never spoken. The same happens at the end of a check, where WhatArrived and the closing updates arrive in the same instant.
all.fix: Deliver at most one live-region write per flush: in flush_announcements, join what drain released with the existing handed_over_together (most urgent wins) and call deliver once. During the tick's drain loop, queue only, then flush once after the loop (a hold flag on Accessibility that announce* checks before flushing). About 15 lines. Test: two announcements in one tick reach the bridge as one joined line.
all.if_skipped: The product's main channel drops a line whenever two things happen at once, and the one dropped is usually the more important first line.
all.ledger_entry: None. The symptom is recorded only in docs/changelog.md:9676, fixed for the Calendar window alone.

verdict.reason:
I confirmed this from the code, line by line. Every announce, announce_topic, announce_what_was_typed and announce_content call flushes straight away (accessibility.rs:347-398). flush_announcements sends each released line to announce_with on its own (435-468). deliver returns once announce_via_live_region has run (screen_reader.rs:600-608), and that function is SetWindowTextW on one control followed by EVENT_OBJECT_LIVEREGIONCHANGED (120-134). Urgency only reaches the notification path, which is skipped whenever the live region works.

The tick runs every queued update in one synchronous loop (wx_app.rs:6392-6415). Nothing joins the lines in between, so each write replaces the last before the screen reader reads the control's name. The code says this happens: the comment on handed_over_together (screen_reader.rs:448-454) and commit 1c46a214 both state that lines handed over one after another overwrite each other. The join was only ever applied to the startup hold.

The concrete case checks out. On a send failure, flush_outbox (24743-24779) sends four updates back to back: OutboxSendResult, ConnectionStatusChanged(Error), OutboxFlushComplete and OutboxQueueCount. For a POP account, nothing in that stretch should need the network. The first arm signals SendFailed, which is Urgent and spoken by default (feedback.rs:280, 655-660), so "Message not sent: <reason>" is written to the control.
