The second signals ConnectionLost (ui_types.rs:281-283), writing "Disconnected". The third announces "The Outbox is done: 0 sent, 1 not sent." at Normal priority; the rate limit has budget left (4 - 2), so it is written straight away. The last write wins, and the reason is never spoken.

The tests count lines handed to the bridge, so they stay green. test_flush_announcements_priority_order (accessibility.rs:1050) asserts three separate lines and so pins the current behaviour. Nothing in .planning/WINDOWS.md records this. The ledger searches for live region, overwrite, "in a row", the rate limit and the join found nothing.
verdict.corrected_problem:
Lines released close together are written to the same live-region control a few microseconds apart. The screen reader reads the control's name after the UI thread returns, so only the last line is heard. The Urgent and Important markings never reach that path.

Two corrections to the finding:

1. docs/changelog.md:9676 and commit 7b34ef86 blame the Calendar-window symptom on topic superseding in the queue, not on this overwrite. The finding's claim that "the code already knows this" rests on the handed_over_together comment and commit 1c46a214, not on the changelog line.

2. The visual channel loses the reason in the same case. signal() keeps only the latest shown line, so after the tick the status bar shows "Disconnected", not the failure reason.

The tick-level hold proposed below also leaves one case uncovered: a single event handler outside the tick that announces twice in a row.
verdict.corrected_fix:
1. In Accessibility::flush_announcements, join everything drain() released into one line, most urgent first, then call announce_with once. Use the most urgent priority among the lines and no topic, as handed_over_together does. Either make that join callable from accessibility.rs or repeat it over Spoken. Keep the per-line log calls.

2. Add a hold flag to Accessibility. While it is set, the announce* functions push to the queue and skip the flush. In the tick closure in wx_app.rs, set the flag before the ui_rx.try_recv loop and clear it after. The flush_announcements call already sitting at line 6420 then releases a single joined line.

Write the failing test first: two announcements made while the hold is set reach the bridge as one joined line. Change test_flush_announcements_priority_order to expect one line, "urgent. high. normal", and re-measure every guard record that names it.

That is roughly 20 lines.

all.title: Removing or disabling an account leaves its inbox watch running
all.location: src/presentation/wx_app.rs:22153-22237 (handle_account_mgr), 24160-24185 (MailboxChanged arm), 27840-27859 (spawn_mail_watch), 30423-30426
all.what_this_is: Each IMAP account has an IDLE watch on a connection of its own, kept in WxUIState.mail_watches. A watch is only ever stopped when a new watch for the same account replaces it (27853-27858).
all.problem: handle_account_mgr signs off a removed account's held session (22229-22234, under a comment saying an account that has gone is signed out of) but never touches mail_watches, and does nothing at all for an account switched to disabled. The MailboxChanged arm picks accounts by id only, not by enabled, and a check that ends asks for a new watch (30808).
all.concrete_case: (a) Disable account B in the Account Manager. Its watch keeps its connection. When mail arrives for B, the watch sends MailboxChanged, spawn_mail_sync checks B (rules run, moves and deletes go to the server, the unattended Trash empty runs), then asks for a new watch, so B keeps being checked for the rest of the session. (b) Remove account C. Its watch stays connected. When C's inbox changes, the woken list is empty and spawn_mail_sync says 'Error: Add an account before checking for mail' at High priority, although other accounts exist.
all.fix: In handle_account_mgr, for each id that was removed or is now disabled, `mail_watches.remove(id)` and `rt.spawn(handle.stop())` on its handle. In the MailboxChanged arm, add `&& account.enabled` to the filter. About 10 lines.
all.if_skipped: Switching an account off does not switch it off until restart, and removing one produces a false error read aloud.
all.ledger_entry: None.

verdict.reason:
I checked every cited line and the bug is real. I put it at should rather than must because it lasts only until restart, loses no data, and everything it does at the server is something the person set up: their own queued moves, flags and rules.

- handle_account_mgr (22153-22237) signs off the held session of a removed account and never touches mail_watches. It does nothing at all for an account whose "Enable this account" box was unticked (wx_account_manager.rs:2261).
- The watch runs on its own connection, opened by watch_folder (mail_sync.rs:2060). no_longer_signed_in_to only closes sessions in the held-session map, so it never reaches the watch.
- The MailboxChanged arm (24173-24178) matches on id only. spawn_mail_sync never checks enabled, and at 30808 it asks for a new watch.
- spawn_mail_watch (27848) never checks enabled either. start_the_watches_whose_wait_is_over (27712) re-arms a disabled account's watch after a dropped connection. The only enabled filters are in the schedule (which_are_due), in watch_every_enabled_account and in the download.

Case (a): a disabled account goes on being watched and checked for the rest of the session. Each check replays its waiting moves, deletes and flag changes, and runs its rules.

Case (b): when a removed account's inbox changes, woken is empty. spawn_mail_sync then fails with "Add an account before checking for mail", and the ErrorOccurred arm (23164) announces it at High priority. The watch's connection to the removed account's server stays open until it wakes or drops.

Not in .planning/WINDOWS.md, and no test covers it.

Two corrections:
1. The unattended Trash empty does not run on a watch wake. It is gated by `if only.is_none()` at 30729.
2. The proposed fix is incomplete. A check already running when the account is disabled still ends by asking for a watch (30808). A failed watch's wait also re-arms it through start_the_watches_whose_wait_is_over. Both reach spawn_mail_watch, which has no enabled check, so the watch comes back.

Stopping the old watch is safe. stop() ends with "the watch was stopped", and whether_to_watch_again answers Never for that, so nothing re-arms it.
verdict.corrected_problem:
The Account Manager never stops the inbox watch of an account that was removed or switched off. Nothing that starts a watch checks enabled: spawn_mail_watch (27848), the MailboxChanged arm (24173-24178) and the watch request at the end of every check (30808) all go ahead for a disabled account.

A disabled account stays watched and checked until restart. Each wake replays its waiting moves, deletes and flag changes and runs its rules. The Trash empty does not run on a wake, because a check of one folder skips it (30729).

A removed account keeps its watch connection open. If its inbox changes, the woken list is empty and spawn_mail_sync announces "Error: Add an account before checking for mail" at High priority.
verdict.corrected_fix:
Three changes:

1. In handle_account_mgr, before the sign-off loop, take out the mail_watches entry for each id that was removed or is now disabled, and stop its handle with `rt.spawn(async move { let _ = handle.stop().await; })`. A stop ends with "the watch was stopped", which whether_to_watch_again answers with Never, so nothing re-arms it.
2. In spawn_mail_watch at 27848, change the lookup to `find(|a| a.id == account_id && a.enabled)`. This covers a check that was already running and the retry after a failed watch.
3. In the MailboxChanged arm, add `&& account.enabled` to the filter, and return without calling spawn_mail_sync when woken is empty. That removes the false "Add an account" error.

About 12 lines. Pull the "removed or now disabled ids" calculation out as a pure function beside added_in_this_visit, so the failing test comes first.

all.title: Empty Folder says a server folder was emptied when the server only marked or copied the messages
all.location: src/presentation/wx_app.rs:10250-10269 (spawn_the_folder_empty); src/service/protocols/imap.rs:1648-1675; src/application/server_delete.rs:62-66
all.what_this_is: Empty Folder on a server folder loops over every UID and calls delete_message, which returns a Deletion naming what really happened: Removed, MovedToTrash, CopiedToTrashAndFlagged, CopiedToTrashAndNotFlagged or MarkedOnly.
all.problem: The loop checks only Err. Any Ok counts as done, so MarkedOnly (no UIDPLUS, or UID EXPUNGE refused) and CopiedToTrashAndNotFlagged (copy made, original left) are reported as emptied. The single-message delete reads the same value correctly (server_delete.rs:62-66). It is also one STORE plus one UID EXPUNGE round trip per message, so a 10,000-message Trash is about 20,000 round trips.
all.concrete_case: Empty Trash on a server without UIDPLUS: every message gets \Deleted and stays, the window says 'Emptied Trash.', and the next check lists them all again. Empty Archive on a server without MOVE where STORE is refused: every message is copied into Trash and stays in Archive, the sentence says it was emptied, and running it again copies everything into Trash a second time.
all.fix: Match the outcome: Removed and MovedToTrash count as done; any other variant stops that folder with its reason in StoppedAt, as an Err does now. About 8 lines, plus one test with a stub mailbox that answers MarkedOnly.
all.if_skipped: People believe mail is gone or moved when it is not, and duplicates pile up in Trash.
all.ledger_entry: None. Ledger 190 covers only remove_these's wording, which is why this path deletes one message at a time.

verdict.reason:
I read the code and the finding holds. In src/presentation/wx_app.rs:10250-10258, spawn_the_folder_empty only tests `if let Err(why)` on `controller.delete_message(...)`. MailController::delete_message (src/application/mail_controller.rs:696) returns Result<Deletion>, and ImapSession::delete_message (src/service/protocols/imap.rs:1648-1675) returns three kinds of Ok that leave the message in the folder:
- MarkedOnly: no UIDPLUS, or UID EXPUNGE refused, with trash None (emptying the Trash).
- CopiedToTrashAndFlagged: no MOVE, then no UIDPLUS or expunge refused (move_message :1479-1492).
- CopiedToTrashAndNotFlagged: no MOVE and STORE refused.

All three count as done, so the folder lands in got.done and what_emptying_did says "Emptied Trash." (how_far_it_got.rs:70-80). Nothing checks abilities before the dialog (wx_app.rs:10030-10142), and no test reaches spawn_the_folder_empty.

The single delete does read the outcome: server_delete::after_a_delete speaks Deletion::spoken(), including "Trying again would make a second copy."

list_uids searches ALL (imap.rs:1174), so flagged messages are listed again. On a server with neither MOVE nor UIDPLUS (hMailServer, for example), a second Empty Archive copies every message into Trash again. That contradicts the function's own comment, "Running it again finishes the job", and the changelog's "Running it again finishes the job" (changelog.md:6602).

The ledger does not cover this:
- Ledger 772 is the waiting-replay path (moves_waiting delete_it), used by the Trash-emptying setting and by Delete inside the Trash. It does not cover Empty Folder, which calls the controller directly.
- Ledger 190 is only about remove_these's wording.

Why should rather than must: Gmail, Outlook.com, Yahoo, iCloud, Fastmail and Dovecot all advertise UIDPLUS, and all but iCloud advertise MOVE too (iCloud's copy, flag and expunge path still ends as moved). So the fault shows only on less common servers or when the server refuses the command.

Two parts of the finding are overstated:
- "The next check lists them all again" is loose. The sync stores \Deleted on the row (messages.rs:2047), so the messages come back marked deleted, not as fresh mail. What is wrong is the sentence, and that the server still holds them.
- The 20,000 round trips claim is accurate, but one message at a time is a choice the code's own comment records (to avoid remove_these's refusal wording). It is not part of this fix.
verdict.corrected_problem:
Empty Folder at a server reports a folder as emptied whenever every delete_message call returned Ok. That includes Deletion::MarkedOnly (no UIDPLUS, or UID EXPUNGE refused), CopiedToTrashAndFlagged (no MOVE, then no UIDPLUS or expunge refused) and CopiedToTrashAndNotFlagged (no MOVE, STORE refused). In all three the message is still in the folder. The single delete reads the same value and says what happened (server_delete.rs:57-72). Empty Folder throws it away, says "Emptied Trash." or "Emptied Archive.", and ends as CommandAnswered.

list_uids asks the server for ALL, which includes messages flagged \Deleted. So on a server with neither MOVE nor UIDPLUS, running Empty Archive again copies every message into Trash a second time. That contradicts "Running it again finishes the job" in the function's comment and in the changelog.
verdict.corrected_fix:
Put the decision in application::emptying as a pure function over &Deletion, for example a function returning Result<(), String>:
- Removed and MovedToTrash are Ok.
- Every other variant is Err(deletion.spoken()).
- Write the match out in full, with no wildcard arm, so a new variant forces a decision here.

In the spawn_the_folder_empty loop, turn the delete's Ok value into that result. A message that is still there then stops that folder with its reason in StoppedAt, the same way an Err does now. left_behind stays uids.len() - done, which correctly counts the message that is still there.

Test the pure function over every Deletion variant. It needs no stub mailbox, because the loop is inside a closure holding a concrete MailController.

Expect this result: on a server without UIDPLUS, Empty Trash stops at the first message and says why ("Marked for removal, and still in this folder, because ..."), where it now claims success.

Leave out the round-trip cost and any batching. They are a separate, deliberate trade-off.

all.title: Sending a draft leaves its copy in the Drafts folder, here and on the server
all.location: src/presentation/wx_app.rs:19292-19298 (Send removes only the drafts table row), 19436-19505 (every save files a copy), 24329-24352 (Undo Send's too-late path); src/data/message_cache/drafts.rs:110-116; docs/changelog.md:8510-8513
all.what_this_is: save_as_draft writes the drafts table row and also files a copy in the account's Drafts folder: on the IMAP server through spawn_draft_append, or as a message row in the local Drafts folder for POP. Autosave does this every few minutes.
all.problem: After Send, only cache.delete_draft(id) runs, which is DELETE FROM drafts. Nothing removes the filed copy (git grep finds no caller that removes it). The changelog says 'A draft is removed once its message has been sent', which is true only for the Open Draft list. Undo Send's too-late branch deletes the drafts row because 'Left in Drafts it would be sent a second time by whoever found it', but the filed copy save_as_draft just made stays.
all.concrete_case: Write a reply on an IMAP account for five minutes, so autosave files it in the server's Drafts, then press Send. The message goes, and the Drafts folder on the phone, and in this program after the next check, still shows it as an unsent draft. On a POP account the local Drafts row stays for ever.
all.fix: After a successful queue (19292) and in undo_send's Ok(false) branch, remove the filed copy by its Message-ID (draft_message::message_id_for(id)): for IMAP, a spawned task using the existing KeepsTheDraft copies_already_there then remove_these; for a local Drafts folder, delete the row with that message_id. About 20 lines. Run it on the same account session after any append still in flight, or a late autosave lands after the removal.
all.if_skipped: Every message that was saved before it was sent stays in Drafts on every device, and somebody may send it again.
all.ledger_entry: None. docs/changelog.md:8510 claims it was fixed.

verdict.reason:
I read every line the finding cites, and it holds.

- **Where the copy comes from.** `save_as_draft` (wx_app.rs:19436-19445) saves the drafts-table row and then calls `file_draft_copy`. On a POP account, `file_draft_copy` writes a message row into the local Drafts folder (`replace_local_draft`, 19474-19489). On an IMAP account it calls `spawn_draft_append` (19505), which puts a copy in the server's Drafts folder.
- **When it happens.** Autosave runs the same save (19235). It is on by default every 2 minutes (`autosave.rs:67-76`), so any message written for more than 2 minutes has a filed copy.
- **What Send does.** After a successful queue, the Send arm runs only `cache.delete_draft(id)` (19292-19297), and `drafts.rs:110-116` shows that is `DELETE FROM drafts`. No production code removes the filed copy:
  - `MailController::remove_by_message_id` (mail_controller.rs:739) exists, but only tests call it.
  - `message_id_for` has no production caller apart from the two filing paths.
  - Nothing under `FolderType::Drafts` in the send code removes anything.
- **Undo Send's too-late branch.** At 24329 it calls `save_as_draft(..., None)`, which files a fresh copy (on IMAP, an append spawned in that same call). On `Ok(false)` or an error it deletes only the drafts row (24343), so the copy of an already-sent message stays in Drafts. That is exactly the double-send its own comment warns about.
- **The changelog and the test.** `docs/changelog.md:8510-8513` claims the draft is removed once sent, but that is true only of the Open Draft list. The guard `tests/wired.rs:1425` is a source-text check that asserts only that `delete_draft` appears after `queue_for_sending`, so it cannot see this.
- **Ledger.** No entry in `.planning/WINDOWS.md` covers it. The only nearby entry, 190, is about the refusal wording of `remove_these`.

**Why must:** this hits the ordinary path, every message written for more than two minutes. It shows on every device and in Gmail's Drafts, it would be seen right away in the phase 14 real-account sittings, and the changelog says it was fixed.

**Correction to the proposed fix:** in Undo Send, removing the copy after the fact would race the append spawned a moment earlier. Filing later avoids that.
verdict.corrected_problem:
Send removes only the drafts-table row (wx_app.rs:19292-19297, `DELETE FROM drafts`). The copy that every save and every 2-minute autosave files does not go away: it is a local Drafts message row on POP, or a server Drafts message on IMAP via `spawn_draft_append`. `MailController::remove_by_message_id` exists, but only tests call it.

Undo Send's too-late branch (24337-24352) has the same gap. `save_as_draft` has just filed a fresh copy, an append spawned in that same call on IMAP. Only the drafts row is deleted, so a copy of a message that has already gone stays in Drafts. That is the double-send its own comment warns about.

`docs/changelog.md:8510` claims the draft is removed once sent. The `tests/wired.rs:1425` guard only checks the source text for `delete_draft`, so it cannot see this. Not in the ledger.
verdict.corrected_fix:
1. **Send path.** At wx_app.rs:19292, after `delete_draft`, take away the filed copy whose Message-ID is `draft_message::message_id_for(id)`:
   - **Local Drafts folder (POP):** look up the folder row, find the message with `message_uid_by_message_id`, and delete that row.
   - **IMAP:** use `spawn_blocking` with `mail_session::a_session_at(&account)`, the same shape as `spawn_draft_append`, and call the existing, currently unused `MailController::remove_by_message_id(drafts_folder, &message_id)`. That keeps it under the account's Allow Changes gate. Report a failure in a status line rather than staying silent.
2. **Undo Send.** Do not remove anything afterwards; reorder instead. Save only the drafts row first, which means splitting `save_as_draft` so `file_draft_copy` can be called separately. Call `file_draft_copy` only after `delete_outbox_message` returns `Ok(true)`. The too-late branch then has no copy to clean up, and nothing races the append.
3. **Remaining race.** An autosave append still running on its own session can land after the Send-path removal. Either say so, or have the removal re-search once after a short delay.
4. **Tests and docs.** Write the failing test first: a cache-level test for the local copy and a `KeepsTheDraft`-style scripted test for the IMAP removal. Correct `docs/changelog.md:8510` in the same commit.

About 25 to 30 lines.

all.title: The download of everything re-reads the whole open folder on the UI thread after every chunk
all.location: src/presentation/wx_app.rs:30026 (one MoreOfTheFolderArrived per 500-header chunk), 24189-24198, 22686-22709 (reread_folder_if_open), 17626-17681 and 17782-17816 (both listings run on the UI thread), 22935-23017 (MessagesLoaded clones the list and announces its count)
all.what_this_is: While the download of everything runs, each chunk of 500 headers sends MoreOfTheFolderArrived. If that folder is open, the UI thread re-runs the whole folder query, threading and labels, and in conversation view the conversation listing too.
all.problem: Each re-read costs the size of the folder on the UI thread and runs once per chunk, so total work grows with the square of the folder size. Ledger 58 measured the conversation listing alone at about 0.75 to 1.2 seconds for 200,000 rows. In flat view every reload also speaks 'N messages, M unread' at Normal (23012-23016), whatever the Say level is set to.
all.concrete_case: First run on an account whose Inbox holds 100,000 messages, with the Inbox open: 200 chunks. Near the end each chunk freezes the window for about a second (no keys, nothing spoken), every few seconds, for the whole download. In flat view the count is spoken about 200 times over whatever the person is reading.
all.fix: The MoreOfTheFolderArrived arm only marks the open folder stale; the tick re-reads a stale open folder at most once every 10 seconds (one Instant in state), and a background re-read does not announce the count. About 12 lines. Moving the Vec out of MessagesLoaded instead of cloning it (22945) also halves the copy.
all.if_skipped: The window is close to unusable during the first download, which is when a new user first tries it.
all.ledger_entry: Ledger 523 expects one sentence per download and does not know about the per-chunk count line; ledger 58 measured the listing cost but not its repetition.

verdict.reason:
I read every link in the chain and it holds. The download runner sends MoreOfTheFolderArrived after each chunk of 500 headers (wx_app.rs:30026, INITIAL_FETCH_LIMIT = 500 at mail_sync.rs:49). Its arm (24189-24198) calls reread_folder_if_open. That function (22686-22709) runs load_folder_messages on the UI thread: the sorted read of the whole folder, the threading and the labels (17664-17671). In conversation view, which has been the default since #92 (config.rs:846), it also runs load_folder_conversations (17805). Updates are handled inside the 50 ms timer (6392), so all of this runs on the UI thread. Nothing coalesces or throttles it, and the only tests (everything_comes_down_without_being_asked.rs:602) require the arm to re-read on every chunk.

measurements.md:184-187 puts the three message steps at 817 ms for 200,000 rows and 39 ms for the tester's 12,872. Ledger 58 puts the conversation listing at 0.75 to 1.2 s for 200,000. Each chunk costs time in proportion to the rows already held, so the total grows with the square of the folder size. Near the end of a 100,000-message folder in conversation view, the freeze per chunk comes to roughly 0.8 to 1 s.

In flat view, the MessagesLoaded arm (23012-23016) calls announce_topic("N messages, M unread", Normal) with no check on HowMuchToSay. The queue (announcements.rs:22-26, 187-197, 270-306) merges lines on one topic only while one is still waiting. It speaks up to 4 a second, and chunks arrive seconds apart, so every chunk is spoken. That is about 26 times for the tester's own folder, so the flood is not limited to big folders.

Neither problem is in the ledger. Ledger 523 expects one sentence at the end of the download under "Say what arrived" and does not know about this line. Ledger 58 measured one listing, not that it repeats per chunk. Ledgers 449, 522 and 564 cover other things.

Corrections to the finding:
- The freeze only matters for folders of roughly 50,000 messages or more. The tester's folder pays about 40 to 90 ms per chunk.
- The spoken flood needs flat view, which is not the default. It happens at any folder size.
- "Move the Vec out instead of cloning" is not a small change. handle_update takes &UIUpdate (22793), so moving it means changing the signature that every arm uses. Drop that part.
- "About 12 lines" leaves out three things the fix has to touch: the test that requires reread_folder_if_open( in the arm, the guard record anchored on that arm (guards.toml:4822-4836), and a way to tell MessagesLoaded that a re-read came from a chunk, because FolderMessagesArrived shares the same path.

It is "should" rather than "must": the default view says nothing per chunk, and the freeze only bites on large folders. It breaks guardrail 5 (bounded feedback while a mailbox syncs), and new users with large Gmail inboxes will hit it on first run.
verdict.corrected_problem: During the download of everything, each chunk of 500 headers that lands in the open folder makes the UI thread re-read the whole folder: messages, threading and labels, plus the conversation listing in conversation view (the default). The total work therefore grows with the square of the folder size. Measured costs (817 ms of message steps at 200,000 rows, conversation listing 0.75 to 1.2 s at 200,000) give freezes of roughly 0.8 to 1 s per chunk near the end of a 100,000-message folder in conversation view. A 12,872-message folder pays about 40 to 90 ms, which nobody notices. Separately, in flat view every re-read speaks "N messages, M unread" at Normal with no check on the Say level. That is once per chunk at any folder size, about 26 times for the tester's folder, against ledger 523's expectation of one sentence at the end.
verdict.corrected_fix:
Throttle the re-read on the UI side:
1. MoreOfTheFolderArrived records the folder id as stale in WxUIState and keeps an Instant of the last chunk re-read.
2. The timer tick calls reread_folder_if_open for a stale folder when 10 s have passed since the last re-read, then clears the mark.
3. Because the mark survives until the tick takes it, the folder still gets a last re-read after the final chunk or a pause.
4. Give MessagesLoaded a reason, the way ConversationsLoaded already has WhyTheRowsWereRead, so a re-read caused by a chunk does not speak the count. FolderMessagesArrived and opening a folder keep speaking it.

Change test_a_chunk_arriving_rereads_the_folder_and_grows_no_limit to accept the stale mark instead of a direct reread_folder_if_open( in the arm. Rewrite and re-measure the guard record "a chunk of the download that lands is shown, and no limit grows" in the same commit. Leave out the clone-to-move idea, because handle_update borrows the update. Expect roughly 30 to 40 lines including tests, not 12.

all.title: A pretend accessibility tree that only tests read, and an event log that grows for the life of the process
all.location: src/presentation/accessibility/screen_reader.rs:491, 657-684 (event_log); src/presentation/accessibility.rs:67-192, 421-473; src/presentation/accessibility/keyboard.rs, focus.rs, automation.rs; guards/guards.toml:11262-11361
all.what_this_is: ScreenReaderBridge pushes every announcement's full text onto event_log. Accessibility also keeps a shortcut map, a focus model and an automation node store, filled once at start by initialize.
all.problem: In production nothing reads any of them: events(), automation_snapshot(), set_focus, update_node_state and live_region_update are called only from tests (git grep over src, tests and scripts), and initialize's own comment says nothing reads the shortcut map. event_log is never trimmed and holds full message bodies read aloud (announce_content at wx_app.rs:12216 passes the whole text for a full reading). The startup line 'Focus moved to Folders' comes from this model, not from where Windows put focus.
all.concrete_case: A week-long session that reads 500 messages in full keeps all 500 bodies, plus every status line, in memory until exit and in any crash dump, although the module's rule is that a body read aloud is never written down.
all.fix: Delete keyboard.rs, focus.rs, automation.rs, register_node, set_focus, update_node_state, live_region_update, automation_snapshot, the registrations in initialize, their tests and their guard records. Make event_log `#[cfg(test)]` so the remaining tests still read what was released. Keep the 'Wixen Mail is ready' push.
all.if_skipped: Memory grows with use, private text stays in RAM, and about 500 lines plus several guard records are maintained for nothing.
all.ledger_entry: None.

verdict.reason:
I checked each claim against the code and they hold. In screen_reader.rs, `announce_with` (lines 648-663) pushes `LiveRegion("global", text)` with the full text onto `event_log`, a plain `Vec` that `push_event` (670-676) grows and nothing ever trims. `Accessibility::flush_announcements` (accessibility.rs:435-468) sends every released line through `announce_with`. That includes `announce_content`, which `wire_read_aloud` (wx_app.rs:12216) calls with the whole text of a reading. For mail that text comes from `read_the_whole_message` (wx_app.rs:4015). There is one long-lived `Arc<Accessibility>` per process (wx_app.rs:1012), so the log lasts until exit. The rate limit of 4 a second slows the growth but does not bound it.

Nothing in production reads the log. Outside `#[cfg(test)]` code, `ScreenReaderBridge::events()` has no caller in src, tests or scripts. The same is true of `automation_snapshot`, `update_node_state`, `live_region_update`, `FocusManager::current_focus` and `KeyboardHandler::action_for_key`. `initialize`'s own comment at lines 71-74 says nothing reads the shortcut map. `Accessibility::set_focus` does have one production call: `initialize` calls `set_focus("folder_tree")` before any window exists, and the startup handover then says "Focus moved to Folders", a line built from this model and not from where Windows put focus.

None of this is open in WINDOWS.md. The ledger has no entry for automation.rs, focus.rs, keyboard.rs or `event_log`, and the growth of `event_log` is recorded nowhere. The dead model was found once before, in .planning/sweeps/ui-and-storage.md item 9, and 04.2's PLANS-README.md:334-350 handed it to phase 6 to delete or document. Neither happened: automation.rs still has a one-line module doc. docs/architecture.md:79-88 still says the Keyboard Handler and Focus Manager manage focus order and focus trapping, which they do not. The guard records at guards.toml:11265-11367 spend measurement time protecting code nothing uses.

I grouped it as should rather than must. The growth is slow (megabytes over days) and stays in RAM, not on disk, so it is not a crash or a disk leak. But it is unbounded, it holds private bodies the module's rules otherwise keep out of logs, and about 300 lines of source plus 7 guard records are kept for nothing.
verdict.corrected_problem:
The finding is accurate with two corrections.

1. `Accessibility::set_focus` is not test-only. `initialize` calls it once in production, and that call is the only source of the startup line "Focus moved to Folders".
2. The model is already known. A sweep found it (.planning/sweeps/ui-and-storage.md item 9) and it was handed to phase 6 (04.2 PLANS-README.md:334-350), but it was never closed and never ledgered.

The `event_log` growth is new and recorded nowhere. docs/architecture.md:79-88 describes the dead Keyboard Handler and Focus Manager as doing focus order and focus trapping, which they do not.
verdict.corrected_fix:
1. Delete keyboard.rs, focus.rs and automation.rs, and their `pub mod` lines.
2. In accessibility.rs, remove:
   - the fields `keyboard`, `focus` and `automation`, in both `new` and `Default`
   - the shortcut and node registrations in `initialize`, and its `set_focus("folder_tree")` call
   - `register_node`, `set_focus`, `update_node_state`, `live_region_update` and `automation_snapshot`
   - the tests that exist only for these: `test_live_region_update_notifies_the_tree_and_announces_the_text`, `test_every_node_registered_at_startup_is_enabled`, `test_updating_a_nodes_state_reaches_the_tree_and_tells_the_bridge`, `test_accessibility_initialize` and `test_focus_event_and_announce`.

   Keep the "Wixen Mail is ready" push and its flush.
3. In screen_reader.rs, remove `notify_event`. `AutomationEvent` goes away with automation.rs, so `event_log` cannot simply become `#[cfg(test)]` with its current type. Replace it with a `#[cfg(test)] released: Mutex<Vec<String>>` that `announce_with` pushes to under `#[cfg(test)]`. Then point `lines_released` and `test_flush_announcements_priority_order` at it.
4. Drop the "Focus moved to Folders" assertion from `test_the_first_lines_of_a_session_are_still_waiting_when_the_window_arrives`. The screen_reader.rs handover test uses that string only as sample data and can stay.
5. Add a docs/changelog.md entry: startup no longer says "Focus moved to Folders". Correct docs/architecture.md:79-88.
6. Delete the 7 guard records at guards.toml:11265-11367. Run `scripts/guards.sh --remeasure` on the other records whose `tests_last_seen` names accessibility.rs, because its test count changes.

all.title: 73 library guard records never run on the commits that break them, and since 2026-09-23 the merge does not run them either
all.location: scripts/check.sh:174-262 (the_suites_that_guard_what_changed keeps a coupling only when a record has both file and suite, line 194) and 324-376 (the_scoped_runs); example records guards/guards.toml:6712-6722 and 2190-2200
all.what_this_is: The commit gate maps a changed file to tests in two ways: the file's own module (--lib a::b::) and the guard records that couple the file to an integration target (suite = ...). A guard record whose tests are library tests in a different module has no route at all.
all.problem: Read with tomllib on 2026-10-14: guards.toml holds 1,488 records, 1,071 of them library records (no suite) breaking a file under src/, and 73 of those break a file whose own module holds none of their red tests. The scan in check.sh drops every record without a suite, so for those 73 the scoped run never reaches the test that guards the change. This is the exact hole CLAUDE.md describes for guards under tests/ ('runs on every commit except the ones that could break it'), closed for integration targets and left open for library ones. Since 12-03.2 a merge into main answers 'affected' by the same rules, so nothing runs these tests until the phase's closing full gate.
all.concrete_case: Apply the recorded break of 'the copy of a sent message is flagged read at the server': src/application/sent_copy.rs:409 SEEN becomes FLAGGED. The commit stages only sent_copy.rs, so the gate runs --lib application::sent_copy:: (22 tests, none red) plus the nine whole-tree targets, and passes. The only test that goes red, application::mail_controller::against_a_server_that_answers::test_the_copy_of_a_sent_message_is_appended_where_it_was_told_flagged_as_read, never runs. The merge runs the same set and lands it on main: every sent copy is filed unread. Same for src/presentation/wx_which_days.rs (focus guard lives in presentation::wx_calendar::tests) and src/presentation/wx_first_run.rs (guards in presentation::first_run::tests).
all.fix: In the registry scan, also read the red = [ ... ] block of records that carry no suite (track an in_red flag between 'red = [' and the closing ']', so quoted lines inside before/after strings are not read), and for each record whose file is a changed path emit the module prefix of each red name (everything before the last ::, as guards.py the_filters_for does). In the_scoped_runs, print those as --lib <prefix> -- --test-threads=4 lines, deduplicated through the existing modules map.
all.if_skipped: Seventy-three recorded guards, including ones on what is sent to servers and where focus lands for a screen reader user, keep reading as coverage while running only at phase close; a break of any of them sits on main for up to a phase.
all.ledger_entry: scripts/check.sh | library guard records whose red tests live outside the broken file's module (73 of 1,071 on 2026-10-14) are never routed by the scoped run or the merge; the coupling reads only records with a suite

verdict.reason: Confirmed line by line. In check.sh, the_suites_that_guard_what_changed (lines 191-212) only keeps a coupling when a record has both a file and a suite (line 194). the_scoped_runs (347-358) adds a --lib filter only for each changed file's own module, so a record with no suite is reached only when its red tests live in that module. I recounted with tomllib on today's tree: 1,488 records, 1,071 with no suite breaking a src .rs file, and 73 of those with no red test in the broken file's module. That count holds after allowing for the include_str couplings the gate already follows (sent_copy, first_run). Checked the concrete case: sent_copy.rs:409 is the anchored SEEN line, mail_controller.rs does not compile sent_copy.rs in, and the only red test is the one at mail_controller.rs:1949. No integration test mentions SEEN or FLAGGED. house_style's anchor check (house_style.rs:5250) lets the exact recorded break through because of its mid-measurement exemption: the after-text is present and the before-text is gone. A merge is judged by the branch rules (which-checks.sh:285-303), so it adds nothing. check.test.sh:361 deliberately tests that "a record with no suite couples nothing", which assumes the red tests sit in the file's own module, and 73 records break that assumption. The gap is not in WINDOWS.md or in phase 12's list of known gate-mapper holes. I chose should rather than must because it is a gap in the commit gate, not a product bug, and the phase-close full gate and CI's full suite on any push still catch it.
verdict.corrected_problem: The scoped gate never runs the red tests of the 73 records whose tests live outside the broken file's module (counted with tomllib on 2026-10-14, out of 1,071 records with no suite). This happens because the registry scan only maps a file to a target through a suite, and the library run covers only the changed file's own module. A merge uses the same branch rules, so only the phase's closing full gate, or CI on a push or pull request, would catch a break. A tester build cut mid-phase could carry one. One extra detail: the exact recorded break, SEEN to FLAGGED, gets past house_style's "names one place" check only because of its mid-measurement exemption. Other edits to that anchored line would trip that check. Edits elsewhere in the function would not.
verdict.corrected_fix: Change the_scoped_runs, or a small sibling helper, and leave --suites-for's target answer as it is so the check.test.sh case at line 361 still holds. For each record with no suite whose file is a changed path, read its red names and emit `--lib <prefix> -- --test-threads=4`, where prefix is everything before the last `::`, the way guards.py the_filters_for builds it. Skip a prefix that starts with a module already in the modules map followed by `::`, so a record whose tests sit in its own module adds no extra cargo call. The scan must read both ways red is written. The multi-line form needs an in_red flag between a bare `red = [` line and a bare `]` line, so lines inside before and after strings are ignored. The one-line form, `red = ["a::b::test"]`, is used by 137 records and may hold several comma-separated names. None of the 73 use the one-line form today, but a scan that reads only the flagged form would silently miss the next record written that way, which is the same defect again. Extend the grep prefilter at line 209 to pass those lines. Write a failing check.test.sh case first: a record with no suite, on file X, whose red test is in module Y, must make the scoped runs include `--lib Y::`. Add a second case for the one-line red form.

all.title: Three CI jobs run the suite on a one-commit checkout, so the release gate and both other-platform jobs cannot pass, and the guard that should say so reads only ci.yml
all.location: .github/workflows/release.yml:47-67 (checkout with no fetch-depth, no WIXEN_NO_AUDIO, cargo test --quiet); .github/workflows/other-platforms.yml:86-87 and 164-165 (checkout with no fetch-depth, then cargo test --all-targets at 145 and 185); tests/house_style.rs:4661-4672 (reads only ci.yml); tests/every_number_carries_its_command_and_its_date.rs:1339-1356 and 1492
all.what_this_is: test_the_share_of_history_before_red_green_is_computed_and_printed runs git merge-base --is-ancestor 18a02454 HEAD and panics when the commit is not in the clone. A house_style check exists to hold every test-running job to fetch-depth: 0.
all.problem: actions/checkout fetches one commit by default. release.yml's quality gate and both jobs of other-platforms.yml run the integration tests on that checkout, so the history test panics on every run. The release gate also lacks WIXEN_NO_AUDIO, so rodio faults on the runner and kills test binaries (ci.yml:11-20). test_every_job_that_runs_the_tests_checks_out_the_whole_history reads .github/workflows/ci.yml alone, so none of this is caught. Ledger 464 says the fix added 'a reading that holds every job running cargo test to it', which overstates it; ledger 616 names only the missing audio setting, which understates the release gate.
all.concrete_case: Dispatch Release at as-is: quality-gate checks out one commit, cargo test reaches every_number_carries_its_command_and_its_date, and the test panics with '18a02454 is not in this history ... Not a valid commit name'. The job fails, so no release can ever be cut. Dispatch Other platforms: both jobs go red on the same test, so SHIP-05's question 'does it build and pass on Linux and macOS' comes back red for a reason that has nothing to do with the platform.
all.fix: Add 'with: fetch-depth: 0' to the three checkouts and WIXEN_NO_AUDIO: "1" to release.yml's env. In house_style.rs:4665, run jobs_that_run_the_tests_without_the_history over every file in .github/workflows instead of ci.yml alone. Correct ledger 464's wording and widen 616.
all.if_skipped: The first release dispatch fails after a full build and test run, and the first other-platforms dispatch reports a port failure that is really a checkout setting.
all.ledger_entry: release.yml quality-gate and other-platforms.yml linux/macos check out one commit and run the history-reading test; the depth guard reads only ci.yml (ledger 464 overstates, 616 understates)

verdict.reason:
I checked each claim against the code and they hold. release.yml:52-53 checks out with no fetch-depth, which gives one commit, and other-platforms.yml:86-87 and 164-165 do the same. All three jobs then run cargo test. Cargo.toml has no autotests or [[test]] override, so a plain `cargo test --quiet` runs the integration tests too. The history test is a plain #[test] at every_number_carries_its_command_and_its_date.rs:1491. On a shallow clone, `rev-parse --git-dir` succeeds, so the test does not take the NoHistoryHere branch. `merge-base --is-ancestor 18a02454 HEAD` then fails, and line 1492 panics. The project chose that behaviour on purpose in 1336-1338 and 1482-1488, so the checkout depth is the thing to fix, not the test.

The guard at house_style.rs:4665 reads only ci.yml. Ledger 464, still open, says the fix added "a reading that holds every job running cargo test to it", which claims more than the guard does. Ledger 616, also open, covers only the missing WIXEN_NO_AUDIO. No ledger entry, STATE line or ROADMAP line records the shallow checkout in release.yml or other-platforms.yml. The repository has no tags, so release.yml has never got past this point. Widening the guard to every workflow is cheap: accessibility.yml and nvda.yml only run cargo build, and guards.yml and mutants.yml already set fetch-depth 0. The only new names it would flag are quality-gate, linux and macos.

One correction to the concrete case. With no --no-fail-fast and no WIXEN_NO_AUDIO, the release gate today probably dies first on the audio fault in the library tests, which is ledger 616. The history panic is the second failure, and it will still stop every release after 616 is fixed. For other-platforms, the history panic is the first certain failure, because that workflow already sets WIXEN_NO_AUDIO.
verdict.corrected_problem: Three jobs run the test suite on a one-commit checkout: release.yml's quality-gate, and other-platforms.yml's linux and macos jobs. On such a checkout test_the_share_of_history_before_red_green_is_computed_and_printed panics with "18a02454 is not in this history". The release gate fails today on the missing WIXEN_NO_AUDIO (ledger 616, open and waiting on Pratik). Once that is settled, it would still fail on the history test, and that second failure is recorded nowhere. Both other-platforms jobs already set WIXEN_NO_AUDIO, so they go red on the history test for a reason unrelated to the platform, which muddies SHIP-05's question. The guard test_every_job_that_runs_the_tests_checks_out_the_whole_history (house_style.rs:4665) reads only ci.yml, so it sees none of these jobs. Ledger 464 describes that guard as covering every job that runs cargo test, which is more than it does.
verdict.corrected_fix:
1. Add `with: fetch-depth: 0` to the checkout at release.yml:53, and to the checkouts at other-platforms.yml:87 and :165.
2. In house_style.rs:4665, loop over every *.yml file in .github/workflows instead of ci.yml alone, and prefix each complaint with the file name. Only the three jobs above will be newly named. This is the red half of the change.
3. Correct ledger 464 so it names the guard's real scope, or close it with the widening. Open a new entry, or widen 616, for the shallow release gate.
4. Leave the WIXEN_NO_AUDIO line in release.yml's env to Pratik, as ledger 616 already records under guardrail 7. Tell him that adding it alone will not make the gate pass without step 1.

all.title: The hook decides on the staged files but builds and tests the working tree, so a commit can pass while its own snapshot is broken
all.location: scripts/check.sh:282-284 and 646-655 (mode and scope taken from git diff --cached) against 714-720 and 875-935 (cargo fmt, clippy and test run over the working tree); .githooks/commit-msg:53-54
all.what_this_is: The commit-msg hook runs check.sh, which works out from the index what the commit changes and then runs cargo over the files on disk.
all.problem: Nothing stashes or refuses unstaged changes, so what is tested is the index plus whatever is unstaged. A file left out of git add, or a partial commit (git commit -- path), is tested together with code the commit does not contain. The comment at 646-648 says the scope is staged 'because that is what the hook is deciding about', but cargo never sees the staged version.
all.concrete_case: A green commit stages src/application/a.rs, which calls a new helper, and forgets src/application/b.rs, which defines it. The working tree compiles and the scoped tests pass, so the commit is accepted. The committed tree does not compile, and the branch now holds a 'green' commit that is not one. The same thing at a merge: with unrelated unstaged edits under src/ in the checkout, the merge commit's run tests those edits plus the merge result, and can pass while the merge result on its own fails.
all.fix: In check.sh, when --message-file is given, refuse before rustfmt if git diff --quiet -- src tests build.rs Cargo.toml Cargo.lock fails (that compares the working tree with the index the hook was handed, including a partial commit's temporary index), with a line telling the person to stage the files or run git stash --keep-index first. About six lines.
all.if_skipped: Red/green evidence in the history can be wrong in both directions, bisects meet commits that never built, and a merge made from a dirty checkout can land a broken main that only the phase-close gate or CI sees.

verdict.reason:
The finding is real. I checked each claim against the lines.

- **Scope comes from the index.** `the_staged_paths` (check.sh:282-284) runs `git diff --cached`, and `decide_the_mode_for_this_commit` (397-399) and the shell-suite reading (545) both take it.
- **Cargo runs over the files on disk.** `touch src/lib.rs`, `cargo fmt`, `cargo clippy` (714-720) and every scoped `cargo test` (875-935) build from the working tree. The hook (commit-msg:53-54) just runs check.sh with the message file.
- **Nothing refuses or stashes unstaged work.** A grep of `scripts/` for stash, `diff --quiet` and unstaged found nothing in check.sh. The only refusal of a dirty tree is in `build-installer.sh`.

The case happens in practice. Executors already work around the false-refusal direction by hand:
- 13-08-SUMMARY:188 says "the hook tests the working tree".
- 13-44.1-SUMMARY:143 says a green commit was refused because unstaged readings were counted.
- 14-03-SUMMARY:172 records a 344 s refusal because house_style read an unstaged page.
- 12-03.2-PLAN:1713 (T-12-03.2-09) handles the same threat for scripts with a manual `git status --porcelain` before each commit.

The false-pass direction is not recorded anywhere. A green commit can leave out a file the build needs and still pass. A merge commit made from a dirty checkout tests edits the merge does not contain. The only open ledger entry nearby is WINDOWS.md 325, about one guard reading planning files from disk. It is narrower, and it raises "whether a tree guard should read the index rather than the disk" without settling it. So the ledger understates this.

It is "should", not "must". It needs a missed `git add`, a partial commit or a dirty tree. CI on push and the phase-close `check.sh all` catch the branch tip, but not the commits in between.

The proposed fix has one gap. `git diff --quiet` compares the working tree with the index and does not see untracked files. The most common missed add is a new file: the parent's `mod b;` is staged, `b.rs` is untracked, the working tree compiles and the commit does not. The pathspec also leaves out `locales/`, which is compiled in through `include_str!`, and `scripts/` and `.githooks/`, which run the gate itself.
verdict.corrected_problem: check.sh picks the mode and scope from the index (the_staged_paths, 282-284; decide_the_mode_for_this_commit, 397-399). It then runs rustfmt, clippy and every cargo test over the working tree (714-720, 875-935), and nothing stashes or refuses what the index does not hold. So under the hook, cargo tests the index plus any unstaged changes and untracked files. This includes the temporary index of a partial commit, and a merge commit made from a dirty checkout. A commit can pass while its own snapshot does not build, and it can be refused over work it does not contain. The refusal direction is already worked around by hand (13-08, 13-44.1 and 14-03 summaries; a manual check in 12-03.2-PLAN T-12-03.2-09). The pass direction is not recorded. Ledger 325 covers only one guard reading planning files from disk.
verdict.corrected_fix:
In check.sh, when message_file is set and before `touch src/lib.rs`, refuse with exit 1 in either of two cases, and print a line telling the person to stage the files or run `git stash --keep-index -u` first:

1. `git diff --quiet -- src tests build.rs Cargo.toml Cargo.lock locales scripts .githooks` fails. This compares the working tree with the index the hook was handed, which for a partial commit is the temporary GIT_INDEX_FILE.
2. `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -- src tests locales` prints anything. `git diff` cannot see untracked files, and a new file someone forgot to add is the usual case.

That is about eight lines. Leave `.planning`, `docs` and `guards` out of the pathspec, so planning and remeasure work in the same checkout does not start being refused.

all.title: A commit that changes only build.rs or rust-toolchain.toml runs no library or unit test at all
all.location: scripts/which-checks.sh:432-547 (only Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock, *.iss and .github/workflows/* earn all; everything else that is not a document answers affected); scripts/check.sh:347-376 (affected maps only src/*.rs and tests/*.rs)
all.what_this_is: which-checks.sh charges the full gate to build inputs that 'reach every target' (the manifest rule) and maps other non-document files to tests by path.
all.problem: build.rs and rust-toolchain.toml reach every target as surely as Cargo.toml does, but neither is matched. They answer affected, which maps them to no module, and no guard record names either file, so the run is fmt, clippy and the nine whole-tree targets. The merge answers the same way, so the first full run against the change is the phase's closing gate.
all.concrete_case: A branch commit moves rust-toolchain.toml from 1.98.1 to a newer compiler. Clippy runs with the new lints, the nine whole-tree targets run, and none of the roughly 10,500 library and integration tests outside them runs under the new compiler at the commit or at its merge. Likewise, a commit changing how build.rs:20-21 builds WIXEN_BUILD, which src/common/version.rs:31 compiles in, runs no common::version test.
all.fix: Add build.rs and rust-toolchain.toml to the case arm that already answers all for *.iss in which-checks.sh, with one which-checks.test.sh case each.
all.if_skipped: A compiler bump or build-script change goes untested on every commit and merge until the phase closes, which is the risk the manifest rule was written to remove.

verdict.reason:
Only the build.rs half holds, and only narrowly. The rust-toolchain.toml half is refuted. The pin's own header says "Bump the channel here and in every workflow in the same commit", and tests/house_style.rs:6577 (test_ci_and_this_machine_are_told_to_use_the_same_compiler) enforces it: it checks that every workflow names the pinned compiler, and it fails if no workflow names one at all. house_style is in guards_that_read_the_whole_tree (check.sh:62), so it runs on every `affected` commit. That means a channel bump without the workflows is refused. A bump with them stages .github/workflows/*, which answers `all` at which-checks.sh:527-534, both on the branch and at the merge. The one commit that has ever changed the pin, 6e31f895, staged all six workflows. 

build.rs is confirmed. A commit staging only build.rs gets past the manifest, .iss and workflow arms and answers `affected` (which-checks.sh:542-545). the_scoped_runs (check.sh:347-364) maps only src/*.rs and tests/*.rs. No src file compiles build.rs in, and no guard record has file = "build.rs" (the only mention, guards.toml:30033, is a comment in a record whose file is src/application/about.rs). So no library test runs. Of the three test files that read build.rs, house_style and the_words_that_say_nothing are whole-tree guards and do run. The third does not: tests/the_about_dialog_names_its_owners_and_its_links.rs:588, test_the_build_script_stamps_the_same_copyright_on_the_executable. 

The finding's WIXEN_BUILD example is weak. Dropping the rustc-env line breaks env! at src/common/version.rs:31, and clippy catches that by compiling. The only version test that touches BUILD (version.rs:782) checks current().starts_with(NUMBER), which holds for any value. 

Real exposure is small. build.rs has changed 5 times since March, always beside src/ files, and the about.rs record already couples a copyright change to the target that reads build.rs. The phase gate and CI's Test Suite cover the rest. Not in the ledger: 583 is the sibling hole for documents read at test time, and 354 is the MSRV floor.
verdict.corrected_problem: A commit staging only build.rs answers `affected`. It maps to no module and no guard record, so the one test that reads build.rs as data, test_the_build_script_stamps_the_same_copyright_on_the_executable in tests/the_about_dialog_names_its_owners_and_its_links.rs:588, does not run at the commit or at its merge. It runs only at the phase's closing gate or in CI. rust-toolchain.toml is not exposed: house_style, which runs on every scoped commit, refuses a channel bump unless every workflow moves in the same commit, and a workflow path answers `all`.
verdict.corrected_fix: Add build.rs only, not rust-toolchain.toml, to the arm that answers `all` for *.iss (which-checks.sh:481, `*.iss | build.rs)`), with one which-checks.test.sh case. A smaller alternative uses the coupling the gate already reads: a guards.toml record with file = "build.rs" and suite = "the_about_dialog_names_its_owners_and_its_links" that breaks the LegalCopyright line, measured with scripts/guards.sh --remeasure.

all.title: The release quality gate runs every dependency's build script and the whole suite holding a token that can push to the repository
all.location: .github/workflows/release.yml:43-67 (workflow-level permissions: contents: write; quality-gate sets no job permissions; actions/checkout persists the token by default)
all.what_this_is: The quality gate only reads the code: fmt, clippy and cargo test. The write permission exists for the next job, which runs cargo release and pushes the tag.
all.problem: Workflow-level contents: write applies to every job without its own permissions block, and actions/checkout leaves the token in .git/config. So in quality-gate, every build.rs and proc macro in the dependency tree and every test can read a token that can push commits and move tags. ci.yml is read-only for the same work.
all.concrete_case: A compromised release of any crate in Cargo.lock adds a build.rs that reads http.https://github.com/.extraheader from .git/config. In ci.yml it gets a read-only token. In the release quality gate, the job a person dispatches deliberately to publish, it gets a token that can push to main or retag a release before build-release-assets runs.
all.fix: Add 'permissions: contents: read' under the quality-gate job. Optionally also 'persist-credentials: false' on its checkout.
all.if_skipped: The one workflow that publishes binaries to testers is also the one where a dependency compromise can write to the repository.

verdict.reason:
The lines say what the finding claims. release.yml:43-44 sets contents: write for the whole workflow. quality-gate (47-67) has no permissions block of its own. Its checkout at 52-53 is plain actions/checkout@v4, which persists the token in .git/config by default. ci.yml:22-31 is contents: read. No ledger entry in .planning/WINDOWS.md covers it: the release.yml rows are 326, 327, 483 and 616, and none is about token scope.

The finding overstates what the fix buys, though. Its own concrete case, a compromised crate in Cargo.lock whose build.rs reads the extraheader, still happens in the very next job. build-release-assets checks out with the write token persisted (89-93). It then runs `cargo install cargo-release --locked` (99) and `bash scripts/build-installer.sh`, which runs `cargo build --release` at line 208. That compiles every build.rs and proc macro in the dependency tree with a token that can push, and it does so after the tag is already on the remote. So the 'if skipped' line ('the one workflow where a dependency compromise can write to the repository') is still true after the two-line fix.

What the fix does remove is the write token from code that only quality-gate runs: test code, dev-dependencies, and crates enabled only by --all-features. That is real defence in depth for two lines, but it is narrow. The workflow has also never been dispatched (ledger 326), so for now the risk only exists on paper. Worth doing as cheap hardening, not as a fix for the stated case.
verdict.corrected_problem: quality-gate takes contents: write from the workflow level and keeps the token in .git/config, though it only reads. So test code, dev-dependencies and --all-features-only crates run holding a token that can push. The same exposure for the main dependency tree stays in build-release-assets: its checkout persists the write token, and it then runs cargo install cargo-release and cargo build --release. Scoping quality-gate narrows the exposure and does not remove it.
verdict.corrected_fix: Add `permissions: contents: read` under the quality-gate job, and optionally `persist-credentials: false` on its checkout. Say plainly that this does not cover build-release-assets. Closing that would mean building in a read-only job and only tagging and publishing in a write job, which changes when a tag exists. Guardrail 7 and ledger 327 put that decision with Pratik.

all.title: An all-users uninstall erases the administrator's data, not the mail of the person who used the program, and the comment says the opposite
all.location: installer/Wixen-Mail-Setup.iss:586-602 ([UninstallRun] --erase-all-data with runascurrentuser), 604-607 ([UninstallDelete] {localappdata}), 474-502 (the leftovers message, shown only when the exe is already gone)
all.what_this_is: Uninstalling runs wixen-mail.exe --erase-all-data, which clears the unencrypted mail cache and the credential-store entries of whoever it runs as.
all.problem: runascurrentuser makes the step inherit the uninstaller's account, and an all-users uninstall runs elevated. When the elevation is another account's (the borrowed-password case the [Run] comment at 205-211 describes), the erase clears that account's data and leaves the user's. The comment at 592-595 claims this flag prevents exactly that. To my reading [UninstallRun] has no runasoriginaluser, which the [Run] section uses for this case. Not verified against the Inno help, because it sits under AppData.
all.concrete_case: A standard user picks 'Install for all users', types an administrator's password at the prompt, uses the program, and later uninstalls the same way. --erase-all-data runs as the administrator: it finds nothing of theirs, and the user's %LOCALAPPDATA%\wixen-mail cache and their Credential Manager tokens stay on disk. No message appears, because TheProgramIsAlreadyGone() is false.
all.fix: In CurUninstallStepChanged, also show the existing 'your mail and settings are still on this computer' message when IsAdminInstallMode() is true, since the erase cannot be known to have reached the right account. Correct the comment at 592-595.
all.if_skipped: People who uninstall to get rid of their mail are told nothing while an unencrypted copy and their sign-in tokens remain.

verdict.reason:
Confirmed by reading the code and its history. Line 602 runs `--erase-all-data` with `runascurrentuser`. Inno's help describes that flag as inheriting "Setup/Uninstall's user credentials (typically, full administrative privileges)", and it is already the default for entries that are not postinstall, so the flag changes nothing. `runasoriginaluser` is valid only in [Run]. Commit d6fe9361 (2026-07-28) shows how this happened: the compiler refused `runasoriginaluser` in [UninstallRun], and the commit message says that section "spells the same idea runascurrentuser". It does the opposite. So the comment at 592-595 is wrong, and the step runs as whatever account the uninstaller runs as.

The case is real. The setup offers "for all users" through `PrivilegesRequired=lowest` plus a dialog override, and an uninstall of an all-users install is elevated. A standard user who typed an administrator's password gets the erase run as that administrator. That account's credential store and %LOCALAPPDATA% are cleared, which is a no-op. The [UninstallDelete] entry for `{localappdata}` (604-607) resolves the same way. The message at 489-502 is gated on `TheProgramIsAlreadyGone()`, which is false here, so nobody is told.

The same gap also hits any second Windows account that used an all-users install, even when the elevation is the person's own. The code half-admits this at 443-446 ("has not been measured"), which contradicts the confident comment at 592-595. Nothing about it is open in `.planning/WINDOWS.md`, and no test pins the flag.

The proposed fix is wrong as written, so I corrected it. Reusing the existing message would open with "could not clear its own data, because the program was already gone", which is false here. It would also tell the common case (an administrator uninstalling their own install, where the erase did reach them) that their mail is still on the computer, which is also false.

One thing I could not check: the [Code] at 513 already calls `ExecAsOriginalUser` during uninstall. If Inno supports that call at uninstall time, a later change could move the erase there and check its exit code. Whether it does is in the Inno help under AppData, which I was not allowed to read, and the message is needed either way for other accounts.

Group is should rather than must: it is a privacy gap (the cache is unencrypted and the tokens stay), but it needs an all-users install plus a second account.
verdict.corrected_problem: installer/Wixen-Mail-Setup.iss:602 runs `--erase-all-data` with `runascurrentuser`, which per Inno's help inherits the uninstaller's credentials and is already the default. An all-users uninstall is elevated, so the erase, and the [UninstallDelete] `{localappdata}` line at 607, act on the elevating account only. A standard user who borrowed an administrator's password, or any other Windows account that used an all-users install, keeps its unencrypted %LOCALAPPDATA%\wixen-mail cache and its Credential Manager tokens. No message appears, because `TheProgramIsAlreadyGone()` is false. The comment at 592-595 (from d6fe9361) says this flag prevents exactly that, and it does not.
verdict.corrected_fix:
1. Correct the comment at 592-595 to say what is true: `runascurrentuser` is the default here, and it runs the erase as whoever the uninstaller runs as, which is the elevating account in an all-users uninstall. `runasoriginaluser` is not allowed in [UninstallRun].

2. In CurUninstallStepChanged, add a separate MsgBox when `IsAdminInstallMode() and not TheProgramIsAlreadyGone()`. Do not reuse the existing message, whose first line blames the missing program and whose "still on this computer" would be false for the account that was erased. Suggested wording: "Wixen Mail cleared its data for the Windows account '<GetUserNameString>'. If Wixen Mail was used under any other Windows account on this computer, that account's mail (%LOCALAPPDATA%\wixen-mail, not encrypted) and its wixen-mail entries in Credential Manager are still there; sign in as that account to remove them." That is about 8 lines and true in both the common case and the borrowed-password case. Leave per-user installs unchanged, since there the erase runs as the person.

all.title: A red commit passes even when a test binary in its scoped run crashes, because red mode discards cargo's exit status and the verdict reads only FAILED lines
all.location: scripts/check.sh:948 (run_the_tests_that_reach_what_changed || true); scripts/red-commit.sh:137-205
all.what_this_is: In red mode, red-commit.sh verdict holds the run to 'every named test ran, every named test failed, nothing else failed', reading cargo's 'test NAME ... ok|FAILED' lines.
all.problem: A test binary that aborts (an access violation in a wx call, a stack overflow, a process exit) prints no FAILED line for the rest of its tests and no 'test result:' line. Affected mode catches that through cargo's exit status. Red mode throws the status away, and the verdict sees no unnamed failure. This is the 'one named failure carries the unnamed ones through' case the verdict's own comment says it stops.
all.concrete_case: A red commit names application::foo::tests::test_x and also makes the wired target's binary crash in its third test. --lib application::foo:: reports test_x FAILED. The --test line prints 'Running ... wired', two ok lines, then cargo's 'process didn't exit successfully ... 0xc0000005'. The verdict counts nothing unnamed as failed, and the commit is accepted with most of wired unrun.
all.fix: In verdict, count lines beginning '     Running ' and lines beginning 'test result: ' in the log, and refuse when the first count is larger, with 'a test binary stopped before reporting'.
all.if_skipped: The red path, which the project calls stronger evidence than an ordinary commit, is the one path where a crash reads as clean.

verdict.reason:
I read the code and the finding holds. scripts/check.sh:948 runs the scoped tests as `run_the_tests_that_reach_what_changed || true`, so in red mode cargo's exit status never reaches anything. The verdict in scripts/red-commit.sh (lines 137-205) only looks at `test NAME ... ok|FAILED|ignored` lines. It checks the log for `error:` lines only when no test ran at all (line 168).

Here is how a crash gets through. A test binary dies from an access violation, a stack overflow or a process exit. Cargo prints `error: test failed` and `process didn't exit successfully ... (exit code: 0xc0000005 ...)`, and with --no-fail-fast it carries on to the next target. The tests that never ran print nothing, so none of them shows up as failed. Meanwhile the named test, which lives in the separate `--lib` binary, reports FAILED. So `ran` > 0, `problems` = 0, and the commit is accepted.

Checks on the premise:
- Compile errors cannot get through this way, because `cargo clippy --all-targets` runs first (check.sh:720). Only runtime crashes are left.
- No case in red-commit.test.sh or check.test.sh feeds the verdict a log with a crashed binary.
- .planning/WINDOWS.md has no entry for this. Ledger 39 is about shell suites and is fixed.
- Crashes really happen here: CLAUDE.md records the 2026-09-03 rodio crash, where about 3,500 tests never ran.
- check.sh:788-802 already refuses a shell suite that "died partway through" for exactly this reason. Its comment says in red mode such a run "would read as a clean run with one expected failure in it". So the same reasoning was applied to shell suites and never to cargo binaries.

Why the group is nice and not should:
- Red commits are refused on main, so this only happens on a branch.
- The green commit that follows runs in affected mode, which keeps the exit status (check.sh:966). If the crash happens again, that commit is refused.
- So the damage is limited to one red commit falsely claiming that nothing else failed.

The proposed fix works and is close to minimal:
- Cargo prints exactly one `     Running ` line (status padded to 12 columns) per test binary. Libtest prints one `test result: ` line per binary that finishes, including runs where the filter matched 0 tests.
- The shell suites write to the same log but print neither line (shell-suite.sh only prints `test ... ok|FAILED`, `FAIL [..]` and summary lines), so they do not upset the count.
- The only thing that could inflate the second count is a failing test whose captured output contains `test result: ` at column 0, which is negligible.
verdict.corrected_problem:
The red-mode verdict misses a test binary that crashes, and so does everything else in red mode. When a binary aborts, its remaining tests print no lines and libtest's `test result:` line never appears. Red mode discards cargo's exit status (check.sh:948), so a red commit whose named test fails in one binary is accepted even though another binary died partway through.

There is also a second case. If the crash is in the same binary as the named test, before that test reports, the commit is refused, but the message is the wrong one: "named as failing and never ran ... Either the name is wrong, or this commit's scoped tests do not reach the module". The real cause, a crash, is not mentioned.

check.sh:788-802 already guards shell suites against exactly this, but nothing does the same for cargo binaries.
verdict.corrected_fix:
TDD:
- Red: add a case to scripts/red-commit.test.sh. Feed the verdict a log with two `     Running ` lines, a `test a::named ... FAILED` line, and a `test result:` line for the first binary only. Assert that the verdict refuses.
- Green: in `verdict`, after the ran==0 block, add the check below. It counts problems, so every problem is still reported together.

```
local started finished
started=$(grep -c '^     Running ' "$output_file" || true)
finished=$(grep -c '^test result: ' "$output_file" || true)
if [ "$started" -gt "$finished" ]; then
    echo "red-commit: $((started - finished)) test binary(ies) stopped before reporting, so the tests after the stop said nothing." >&2
    problems=$((problems + 1))
fi
```

This needs no change to check.sh.

all.title: A documents-only commit pays a full clippy run and a forced crate rebuild for Rust that by definition did not change
all.location: scripts/check.sh:714-720 (touch src/lib.rs and clippy run in every mode, after the mode is already known at 653-655); 827-852 (docs_only branch)
all.what_this_is: docs_only is the answer for a commit whose paths are all .md or .txt files that no source compiles in (which-checks.sh:165-178).
all.problem: The mode is decided before the touch, but touch src/lib.rs and clippy --all-targets run anyway. With no Rust, manifest or compiled-in file changed, clippy cannot find anything the previous gated commit did not. The touch also makes the crate and the eight document-reading test binaries rebuild before they run. Measured clippy median per hook run: 27 s (docs/development/measurements.md:570-571). CLAUDE.md records a documents-only run of 2m56s against 36 s warm.
all.concrete_case: A plan's closing commit that touches only docs/changelog.md and .planning/*.md re-lints all 149 integration targets and relinks the eight document targets just to read markdown.
all.fix: Wrap the touch and the clippy stage in if [ "$mode" != docs_only ]. Keep rustfmt. Update the one CLAUDE.md sentence that lists clippy for documents-only commits.
all.if_skipped: About half a minute or more on every documents commit, the most common commit in a plan's wrap-up.

verdict.reason:
The finding is real. I read the code and confirmed it.

- **The lines say what the finding claims.** `check.sh:653-655` settles the mode, then `:714` runs `touch src/lib.rs` and `:719-720` runs `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` in every mode, with no mode check. The `docs_only` branch only starts at `:827`.
- **`docs_only` really means no Rust changed.** `which-checks.sh` answers it only when every staged path is a `.md` or `.txt` file that `is_a_document` (`:165-178`) clears. Anything compiled in under `src/` is excluded by the include scan, and `tests/` compiles in no `.md` (its one include is an `.html` fixture). `build.rs` watches only `assets/icon.ico`. So clippy has no changed Rust to judge.
- **What clippy can still see is not the commit.** It lints the working tree, so in this mode it can only report unstaged Rust or a new lint from a toolchain upgrade. CI and the once-a-phase full gate both run clippy anyway.
- **The touch only exists for clippy.** The comment at `:8-11` says so, and cargo tracks includes and mtimes for the tests on its own. The touch also forces the crate and the eight document targets in `:102` to rebuild.
- **The cost is measured.** 12-04 and 12-05 record `docs_only` hook runs of 86 s and 83 s, of which clippy was 30 s and 28 s. The `tests/*.rs` count is 149, as the finding says.
- **Not already in the ledger.** No entry in `.planning/WINDOWS.md` covers it.

It stays at **nice**, not should. The saving is about 30 s or more per documents commit, but `CLAUDE.md:304` and `:312` record Pratik's settled rule that a documents commit runs formatting, clippy and the document targets. Changing what the gate runs is his call.

The fix as written is incomplete:

- **It breaks a test.** Two cases in `check.test.sh` run `check.sh docs_only` from an empty `mktemp -d` folder and rely on it stopping at `touch src/lib.rs`. The case at `:686-693` greps for `stopped in start after N s: start N s`. With the touch skipped, the run reaches `cargo fmt`, fails there and reports "stopped in rustfmt", so the check suite goes red. The comments at `:617-618` and `:672-675` say the same thing.
- **The guard has to be spelled `!=`.** The ordering reading at `check.test.sh:778` finds the first mode branch by `if [ "$mode" = `. A guard spelled with `=` above the suite loop would turn "the suites run before any mode branch" red. The finding's `!=` happens to avoid this.
- **More than one sentence names clippy for documents commits.** `CLAUDE.md` has two (`:304` and `:312`), plus `which-checks.sh:43` and the message `check.sh` prints at `:847`.
- **The size is wrong.** The change adds lines rather than removing two (`lean_lines` says -2).
verdict.corrected_problem:
The gate settles the mode at `scripts/check.sh:653-655`. It then runs `touch src/lib.rs` (`:714`) and `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` (`:720`) in every mode, `docs_only` included.

A `docs_only` commit stages only `.md` and `.txt` files that no source compiles in (`which-checks.sh:165-178`), so clippy has no changed Rust to judge. It can only report:

- unstaged Rust in the working tree, which is not part of the commit, or
- a new lint from a toolchain upgrade, which CI's Clippy job and the once-a-phase full gate already catch.

The touch is there only to keep clippy's fingerprint fresh (`check.sh:8-11`). It also forces the crate and the eight document-reading targets (`check.sh:102`) to rebuild before they run.

Measured `docs_only` hook runs: 86 s with clippy at 30 s (12-04-SUMMARY), and 83 s with clippy at 28 s (12-05-SUMMARY). Every plan's closing documents commit pays this.
verdict.corrected_fix:
1. **Red first, in `scripts/check.test.sh`.** Add a case named, for example, "a documents-only run does not lint":
   - Put a fake `cargo` first on PATH in `$work` that logs its arguments and exits 0.
   - Run `check.sh docs_only` from `$work`.
   - Assert that no logged call holds `clippy`. Today this is red, because the run stops at `touch src/lib.rs` before it.

2. **Fix the existing cases this change would break.** The timing cases at `check.test.sh:676-693` rely on `docs_only` stopping at the touch. Switch them to ask `affected`, which still touches and so still stops in start, and update the comments at `:617-618` and `:672-675`.

3. **Green, in `scripts/check.sh`.** Wrap only the touch and the clippy stage:

   ```bash
   if [ "$mode" != docs_only ]; then
       touch src/lib.rs
       begin_stage "clippy"
       cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings
   fi
   ```

   Keep the touch before the rustfmt stage, as it is today. Spell the test `!=`: `check.test.sh:778` treats any `if [ "$mode" = ` line as the first mode branch, and that line must stay below the suite loop.

4. **Update the text that lists clippy for documents commits.** Change the `docs_only` message at `check.sh:847`, the `docs_only` row of the table at `which-checks.sh:43`, the comment at `check.sh:8-11`, and the two sentences at `CLAUDE.md:304` and `:312`. `CLAUDE.md` states the current behaviour as Pratik's rule, so confirm the change with him before landing it.

all.title: The calendar's XML reader never decodes XML escapes, though the address-book copy of the same reader does
