all.location: src/service/caldav.rs:1283-1293 (extract_xml_value), used raw at 746, 755-757, 822-827, 457-460; compare src/service/carddav.rs:350-386 (value_in, xml_unescaped)
all.what_this_is: CalDAV and CardDAV answers are multistatus XML that the code reads by hand. CardDAV wraps the shared extract_xml_value in value_in, which turns & < > " ' back into characters. CalDAV calls extract_xml_value directly and never decodes anything, so calendar-data, href, getetag and displayname reach the rest of the program still escaped. carddav.rs:357-359 says so ("a gap there rather than a decision") and STATE.md:3937 says the gap is "recorded", but no WINDOWS.md entry holds it.
all.problem: One rule (take XML's escaping off a value) is applied in one reader and not in its twin. XML requires every & and < in element text to be escaped, so any CalDAV server that does not use CDATA sends escaped iCalendar text. Neither reader handles numeric references such as . No test in caldav.rs contains an entity.
all.concrete_case: Certain: an event titled "Dinner & drinks" arrives in <c:calendar-data> as SUMMARY:Dinner & drinks. parse_report_events (826) hands that to the iCalendar reader unchanged, so the event is stored and read aloud with "&" in its title. A calendar named "Work & Home" is listed as "Work & Home" (755). Probable, not verified here because nothing has met a server: libxml-based writers, which SabreDAV and therefore Nextcloud, ownCloud and Baikal use, write each CR as  and quotes as ". Then every calendar-data line ends in "", component_named_after refuses "VCALENDAR" as a component name, and every event counts as unreadable, so the sync reports "none could be read" on every calendar. Separately, the ETag kept after a write here comes from the PUT response header with plain quotes (caldav_sync.rs:523, 545). The next report's tag is "...", so both_copies_moved (caldav_sync.rs:893) raises a conflict on an event only this computer changed.
all.fix: Move xml_unescaped from carddav.rs into caldav.rs and apply it inside extract_xml_value. Extend it to decimal and hex character references (, ") in the same single pass. Then delete carddav's value_in wrapper and call extract_xml_value directly. Add one CalDAV fixture with &, " and  in it.
all.if_skipped: Every CalDAV event or calendar name containing &, < or > is shown and spoken with its escapes, and on SabreDAV-family servers CalDAV, and probably CardDAV too, may read nothing at all. The day phase 14 meets a Nextcloud account will show which.
all.ledger_entry: Not in WINDOWS.md. Mentioned only in a carddav.rs comment and STATE.md:3937, and both describe only the named entities.

verdict.reason:
I read every line the finding cites and its central claim holds. extract_xml_value (caldav.rs:1283-1293) slices out the raw text between the tags and never decodes it. Every CalDAV caller uses that raw text: hrefs and etags at 457/460 and 822/823, displayname, ctag and color at 755-757, and calendar-data at 826-827, which goes straight into every_event_in_the_resource. carddav.rs:350-402 wraps the same function in value_in/xml_unescaped, and its own comment at 357-359 calls the CalDAV side a gap. No CalDAV test contains an entity: the grep for & finds nothing in caldav.rs. WINDOWS.md has no entry for this. Only STATE.md:3937 and the 05.1-05 summary mention it, and both cover only the five named references.

The finding understates three things.
(1) The bad value travels back to the server. the_properties_this_program_owns (caldav.rs:1916) always rewrites SUMMARY from the local row, so editing only the time of an event called "Dinner & drinks" PUTs "Dinner & drinks" to the server as literal text. Every other client then shows it, and each read and edit cycle adds another layer of escaping.
(2) There is a third copy of the decoder. free_busy.rs:417 (without_the_escapes) is a multi-pass replace chain, and its comment describes exactly the harm CalDAV suffers.
(3) A quoted TZID such as "(US & Canada)" arrives as "...", so delimiter_colon cannot see the quotes and splits at the colon inside them.

Two of its sub-claims are wrong or overstated.
(a) Lines ending in  do not make the sync report "none could be read". component_named_after refuses "VEVENT", so events_in finds nothing. every_event_in_the_resource then falls back and reads the whole document as one event. The result is at most one event per resource, with "" stuck to its UID and its DTSTART possibly taken from the VTIMEZONE block: the events are misread, not counted as unreadable.
(b) The false ETag conflict is real but needs a narrow window. The If-Match tag comes from the GET header (caldav_sync.rs:283/304), and the next pull of a row that is not pending stores the escaped tag. So the conflict fires only when somebody edits again after a push and before the next pull.

The  and " behaviour of SabreDAV comes from libxml's xmlEncodeSpecialChars. Nothing in this repo has met such a server, so that part stays unverified here. The & case needs no server knowledge, because XML itself requires & to be escaped in text.
verdict.corrected_problem:
The CalDAV reader never takes off XML's escaping. extract_xml_value (caldav.rs:1283) returns raw element text, and every CalDAV caller (457, 460, 746, 755-757, 822-827) uses it as-is. CardDAV decodes the five named references (carddav.rs:360-402), and free_busy.rs:417 has its own multi-pass copy. None of the three decodes numeric references.

Certain consequences:
- An event titled "Dinner & drinks" is stored and spoken as "Dinner & drinks", and a calendar called "Work & Home" is listed with "&" in its name.
- Editing any field of that event writes "SUMMARY:Dinner & drinks" back to the server as literal text (caldav.rs:1916), so the damage reaches every other client and gets worse with each round trip.
- A quoted TZID parameter arrives as "..." and delimiter_colon splits inside it.

Probable, on servers whose XML writer encodes CR as  and quotes as " (the SabreDAV family; unverified here):
- No BEGIN:VEVENT line is recognised, so each resource is read whole through the fallback. That gives at most one event, with "" on its UID and possibly a DTSTART taken from the VTIMEZONE block. The events are misread rather than counted unreadable.
- Stored ETags carry ". A row edited again after a push and before the next pull raises a false conflict at caldav_sync.rs:893.
verdict.corrected_fix:
Write the test first (TDD): a parse_report_events fixture whose SUMMARY holds & and <, whose getetag is "v1", whose lines end in , and whose displayname is "Work & Home".

Then make the change:
1. Move carddav's single-pass xml_unescaped into caldav.rs as pub(crate).
2. Extend it to decode &#N; and &#xH; when they name a valid char. Leave anything else as it arrived.
3. Apply it inside extract_xml_value.
4. Remove carddav's value_in wrapper and call extract_xml_value directly. If the wrapper stays, values are decoded twice and carddav's existing test that &lt; reads back as < breaks.
5. Replace free_busy.rs's without_the_escapes with the shared function, so one rule lives in one place.

That is about 10-15 lines of change plus the test.

all.title: A shadow accessibility tree that reaches no screen reader, and an announcement log that keeps every spoken line for the whole session
all.location: src/presentation/accessibility.rs:22-25, 67-192, 421-429, 470-473; accessibility/keyboard.rs (61 lines), focus.rs (60), automation.rs (166); accessibility/screen_reader.rs:491, 657-660, 666-684; guards/guards.toml:11265-11367
all.what_this_is: Accessibility keeps three in-memory structures. KeyboardHandler is a key-to-action map that its own comment calls a map "nothing reads back today" (accessibility.rs:71-74). FocusManager holds the id of a string. AutomationStore is a HashMap of made-up nodes ("main_window", "folder_tree", six module panes). Every change to them is also pushed onto ScreenReaderBridge.event_log. None of it touches UI Automation or MSAA. The real speech path is live region and notification inside deliver().
all.problem: This is guardrail 2's trap: code that looks like accessibility and is not. Seven guard records spend sweep time proving the shadow tree "is not a stub". Worse, announce_with pushes a full clone of every released line onto event_log (657). Nothing clears that Vec, and only tests read it (events(), 679). The held list beside it is capped at 8 (MAX_HELD, 431); the log has no cap.
all.concrete_case: Reading a 20 KB newsletter aloud (announce_content) leaves those 20 KB of somebody's mail in event_log until the program exits. The queue releases up to 4 lines a second (announcements.rs:23-26), so a day of syncing with progress speech accumulates tens of thousands of entries that nobody will read. At startup, initialize calls the shadow set_focus("folder_tree") (135), so the screen reader is told "Focus moved to Folders" because a string was stored, not because anything asked the window where focus is.
all.fix: Delete keyboard.rs, focus.rs and automation.rs. Remove register_node, set_focus, update_node_state, live_region_update, automation_snapshot and notify_event, keeping only the "Wixen Mail is ready" announcement in initialize. Make event_log #[cfg(test)], so the tests' lines_released still works. Retire the guard records at guards.toml:11265-11367 in the same commit. Remove "Keyboard Handler" and "Focus Manager" from docs/architecture.md:23-24 and 79-88.
all.if_skipped: Memory grows with every spoken line, private text is kept in memory for the life of the process, and guard sweeps keep paying to protect code no assistive technology can see.
all.ledger_entry: Not in WINDOWS.md (searched AutomationStore, FocusManager, KeyboardHandler, event_log, register_shortcut).

verdict.reason: I read every line the finding cites, and both halves hold. (1) Event log: `ScreenReaderBridge::announce_with` (screen_reader.rs:657-660) pushes a clone of every released line onto `event_log`. Nothing removes entries from it. `events()` is `pub` but only tests call it (accessibility.rs:515/949/1014/1041/1076, screen_reader.rs:902). Full message bodies really do go in: Space or Shift+Space on the mail list goes through `wire_read_aloud` to `read_the_whole_message` to `announce_content` (wx_app.rs:3981-4015, 12216), then `flush_announcements`, then `announce_with`. `announce_what_was_typed` lines, which are kept out of the log file on purpose, land in it too. The held list is capped at MAX_HELD = 8 and this log has no cap. The growth is slow, a few MB a day at the 4-a-second release cap, and the privacy angle is weak because the same mail already sits unencrypted in the database. That makes it should, not must. (2) Shadow tree: `KeyboardHandler`, `FocusManager` and `AutomationStore` are written only at `initialize` (the one production call is wx_app.rs:1013) and read only by tests. `update_node_state`, `live_region_update` and `automation_snapshot` have no non-test callers. The real Ctrl+Shift+1-6 handling lives in wx_app.rs:2991-3006. The startup `set_focus("folder_tree")` queues "Focus moved to Folders" from a hard-coded string, and the test at accessibility.rs:780 shows it waiting to be handed over with "Wixen Mail is ready". This is not in WINDOWS.md. It was found before: .planning/sweeps/ui-and-storage.md item 9, and 04.2 PLANS-README.md:334-350 gave it to phase 6, but no phase 6 plan touched it and automation.rs still opens with its one-line doc comment. So it is real and unowned. Two things in the finding are wrong. The guard range 11265-11367 holds seven records, but one of them (11318-11326, `feedback_settings`) guards a real getter, so six guard the shadow tree, and the fix as written would retire a live guard. And deleting automation.rs also deletes `AutomationEvent`, so a cfg(test) `event_log` has to change type, not just get an attribute.
verdict.corrected_problem: `ScreenReaderBridge.event_log` (screen_reader.rs:491) gets a full clone of every line released to the screen reader (announce_with, 657-660). That includes whole message bodies read with Space or Shift+Space on the mail list (wx_app.rs:3981-4015 → 12216) and typed-name lookups that are kept out of the log file on purpose. Nothing ever clears it, and only tests read it, so it grows for the life of the process with no cap. The held list next to it is capped at 8. Separately, KeyboardHandler, FocusManager and AutomationStore (keyboard.rs, focus.rs, automation.rs) are a shadow accessibility tree. They are written once in `initialize`, read only by tests, and never reach UI Automation or MSAA. This was flagged in sweeps/ui-and-storage.md item 9 and handed to phase 6 by 04.2 PLANS-README.md:334-350, which never did it. It is not in WINDOWS.md.

Delete the tests that exist only for the shadow tree (`test_every_node_registered_at_startup_is_enabled`, `test_updating_a_nodes_state_reaches_the_tree_and_tells_the_bridge`, `test_live_region_update_notifies_the_tree_and_announces_the_text`, `test_focus_event_and_announce`, and the snapshot and keyboard asserts in `test_accessibility_initialize`). Retire the six shadow-tree guard records (guards.toml:11265-11316 and 11328-11367) but keep the `feedback_settings` record at 11318-11326. all.title: A second translation system that translates nothing, and says in its comments that it does
all.location: src/service/spellcheck/mod.rs:1052-1258 (Locale, TextDirection, DOCUMENT_LOCALE, set_document_locale, translate_document_term, I18n); src/vendor/paperback/html_to_text.rs:46-54, 380-382; src/service/mod.rs:56; guards/guards.toml:12487
all.what_this_is: A hand-made I18n registry, separate from the real Fluent catalogue in common/catalogue.rs. Its only production use is the two labels the HTML converter writes before an image or figure description ("[Image: ...]").
all.problem: set_document_locale (1109) has no caller outside its own test, and load_translations and load_translations_file have none either, so the registry only ever holds English. 39 of its 41 keys (menu.*, action.*, status.*, compose.*, settings.*, document.table_marker) are asked for by nothing. The table marker is the hard-coded literal "[Table]" at table_text.rs:88. The comment at html_to_text.rs:48-51 says a French screen reader user will not hear "Image" in English, and they will.
all.concrete_case: On a French Windows machine, a newsletter with : html_to_text.rs:382 calls t("document.image"). DOCUMENT_LOCALE is None, so translate_document_term builds I18n::with_locale("en"), which is a fresh 41-entry HashMap and 82 String allocations, and returns "Image". The user hears "[Image: chat]". This repeats for every described picture in every body rendered.
all.fix: Replace t() with two literals (if is_figure { "Figure" } else { "Image" }), or with two messages in the Fluent catalogue when version 2 arrives. Delete lines 1052-1258 and their tests, the I18n and Locale re-export at service/mod.rs:56, and the guard record at guards.toml:12487. Correct the "three translatable strings route through the i18n registry" lines in html_to_text.rs:25-27 and paperback/mod.rs.
all.if_skipped: About 200 lines claim a translation path that does not exist, beside the Fluent catalogue that does, and the next person translating version 2 has two systems to reconcile.
all.ledger_entry: Not in WINDOWS.md.

verdict.reason: Confirmed by reading the code. Outside the tests in src/service/spellcheck/mod.rs, nothing calls set_document_locale (1109), load_translations (1206), load_translations_file (1210), set_locale (1223) or tf (1244). That means DOCUMENT_LOCALE is always None, and translate_document_term (1119) always builds I18n::with_locale("en"), allocating the full 41-entry English table on every call. Only document.image and document.figure are ever requested, from html_to_text.rs:380/382. A grep over src finds none of the other 39 keys outside the table and its tests. The table marker is the literal "[Table]" at table_text.rs:88, so the 'three strings' claim at paperback/mod.rs:18-19 and :128 is false (only two are routed). The I18n/Locale re-export at service/mod.rs:56 has no user: wx_managers.rs:956 uses wxdragon's Locale, not this one. The test comment at spellcheck/mod.rs:1556 says Locale::display_name 'is the name read out in the settings list', but nothing in production reads display_name. This is not in WINDOWS.md. It is a 'stub presented as complete' under guardrail 3: the comments at spellcheck/mod.rs:1156-1158 and html_to_text.rs:48-51 present a translation path that cannot run, beside the real Fluent catalogue in common/catalogue.rs. Two corrections to the finding. First, the 'French user hears English' case is real, but deleting the registry gives byte-for-byte the same output, and the rest of v1 is English too, so the harm is misleading code and docs plus four guard records guarding dead code, not something users notice. Second, the fix understates its own cost: it touches four guard records, not one, and changes the test count every other spellcheck record checks.
verdict.corrected_problem: A second translation registry, separate from the Fluent catalogue in common/catalogue.rs, cannot translate anything. No production path calls set_document_locale, load_translations, load_translations_file, set_locale or tf, so only English is ever held. 39 of its 41 keys are asked for by nothing, and Locale (display_name, direction) is read only by its own tests. Its only production use is the two labels html_to_text.rs:380/382 write before an image or figure description, and each call rebuilds the 41-entry English table. Comments in several places claim it translates what it cannot. spellcheck/mod.rs:1156-1158 says a user working in another language does not hear these words in English. html_to_text.rs:48-51 says the same. paperback/mod.rs:18-19 and :128 say 'three translatable strings route through' the registry, but the third, the table marker, is the literal "[Table]" at table_text.rs:88. Four guard records (guards.toml 12487, 12499, 12509, 12519) guard functions nothing calls. Users hear the same thing either way; the harm is a false translation story and dead guarded code that the version 2 translation work would have to reconcile.
verdict.corrected_fix:
1. In html_to_text.rs, replace t() with literals: `let label = if is_figure { "Figure" } else { "Image" };`. Delete the t() helper and its doc comment (46-54).
2. In spellcheck/mod.rs, delete lines 1052-1258: Locale, TextDirection, DOCUMENT_LOCALE, set_document_locale, translate_document_term, I18n and Default for I18n. Also delete the eight tests that cover them: test_i18n_english_defaults, test_i18n_fallback, test_every_language_is_named_the_way_somebody_would_say_it, test_locale_rtl_detection, RestoreDocumentLocale and its test, test_load_translations_file_reads_every_entry_in_the_table, test_set_locale_changes_which_language_is_read_back and test_tf_fills_in_its_placeholders. Reword the module doc at lines 8-10.
3. At service/mod.rs:56, drop I18n and Locale from the re-export.
4. In guards.toml, remove all four records under the 'document locale and i18n' heading (12487, 12499, 12509, 12519). The test count for spellcheck/mod.rs then falls from 64 to 56, so run `scripts/guards.sh --remeasure` on the remaining records it prints (about 28).
5. Correct the 'routes through Wixen Mail's own i18n registry' header lines in html_to_text.rs, table_text.rs, text.rs and types.rs, the 'three translatable strings' lines at paperback/mod.rs:18-19, and the comment at :128. Keep test_image_alt_text_is_kept_and_labelled_in_our_language; it still holds with literals.
6. When version 2 arrives, the two labels become Fluent messages in the existing catalogue.

all.title: The original skeleton's account manager, search engine and cache service still exist, used only by tests/integration_tests.rs and described in docs/architecture.md as the real design
all.location: src/application/accounts.rs (144 lines); src/application/search.rs (106); src/service/cache.rs (78); src/common/types.rs:294-335; src/data/email_providers.rs:23-42; src/data/account.rs:216-233, 293-330; src/application/mod.rs:166, 170; src/service/mod.rs:48; tests/integration_tests.rs:20-54, 328-390, 483-498; docs/architecture.md:97-124, 164-178
all.what_this_is: AccountManager is a Vec<Account>. SearchEngine is a Vec of strings searched with contains. CacheService is an unbounded HashMap<String, Vec<u8>>. ServerConfig, Credentials and AccountSettings exist only to fill the scaffold Account, plus EmailProvider::get_imap_config and get_smtp_config. Account::from_provider and from_account_config are only called in their own tests.
all.problem: No shipped code constructs any of these. git grep finds only the definitions, the pub use lines and tests/integration_tests.rs. They read as the application's architecture and are not it. Real accounts live in data/account.rs and config, and real search is message_cache/searching.rs. The docs repeat claims the code does not support. common/types.rs:315 says Credentials are "encrypted at persistence boundary by MessageCache", while message_cache/mod.rs:1692 says nothing is written encrypted any more. docs/architecture.md promises a Cache Service with "size-based eviction", an Account Manager that "stores account credentials securely", and a Security Service using DPAPI.
all.concrete_case: tests/integration_tests.rs:20 builds an AccountManager, adds two Account::new_simple accounts whose password is the string "password" (accounts.rs:49), and passes. The application never makes either type. A reader of docs/architecture.md:119-124 looking for "virtual folder creation" in the Search Engine finds a 30-line substring filter that nothing calls.
all.fix: Delete the three modules, their re-exports, ServerConfig, Credentials, AccountSettings, get_imap_config, get_smtp_config, from_provider and from_account_config, and the integration tests that exercise only them (no guard record names those tests). Redraw docs/architecture.md from the real module list, or cut the boxes that have no code behind them.
all.if_skipped: About 575 lines, plus a design page, keep describing a program that was never built, and the false encryption comment can be quoted as fact.
all.ledger_entry: Not in WINDOWS.md (searched CacheService, SearchEngine, architecture.md, integration_tests.rs).

verdict.reason:
I read every line the finding cites and they say what it claims. AccountManager (accounts.rs:64-91) is a Vec. SearchEngine (search.rs:16-68) is a lowercase `contains` over a Vec of strings. CacheService (cache.rs:10-50) is an unbounded HashMap. They are re-exported at application/mod.rs:166 and 170 and service/mod.rs:48.

git grep turns up no caller in src or nvda-tests apart from their own unit tests and tests/integration_tests.rs:20-50, 327-381 and 482-494. ServerConfig, Credentials and AccountSettings (types.rs:294-335) are used only by that scaffold, by its own tests at types.rs:583-596, and by get_imap_config and get_smtp_config. Those two are called only by tests at email_providers.rs:251-282. lettre's Credentials in smtp.rs is a different type. data::Account::from_provider and from_account_config are called only from account.rs:535 and 581, both tests.

The comment at types.rs:315 says credentials are "encrypted at persistence boundary by MessageCache". That is false: message_cache/mod.rs:1692-1694 says nothing is written encrypted any more, and Credentials is never persisted at all. That false claim, in a project that forbids claiming encryption it does not have, is why this sits at should and not nice.

It is not in the ledger. I searched .planning/WINDOWS.md for the module paths, architecture.md, built-and-left, ServerConfig and from_provider and found nothing. .planning/sweeps/logic-layers.md section 6 noticed accounts.rs and search.rs and deferred their deletion to "a dead-code-hunter job", but it never ledgered it and it missed cache.rs. No plan decided to keep them; the last change to them was the edition move.

The finding holds, with these gaps:
1. Removing from_provider and from_account_config leaves all of email_providers.rs with no caller. That includes the presets, detect_provider_from_email and 8 tests. presentation::ui_types::AccountConfig (ui_types.rs:296) is left with no caller too. Deleting get_imap_config and get_smtp_config alone also breaks two tests in email_providers.rs that the fix never mentions.
2. Two guard records, "mail waiting to go sits where the tree order says" and "a name written back out is quoted when it needs to be", list src/common/types.rs at tests = 30. Deleting test_server_config and test_credentials makes it 28, which turns the count check red until those two records are re-measured.
3. A few more places point readers at the scaffold:
   - docs/architecture.md:284-296 shows the scaffold Account struct with EncryptedCredentials.
   - docs/plans/20260924-pro-licence.md:56 says `application::accounts` holds the accounts.
   - .planning/codebase/TESTING.md:77 recommends Account::new_simple.
   - saved_searches.rs:21 links to [`crate::application::search`], which would become a broken intra-doc link.
4. Part of the doc complaint is overstated. The credential store really is DPAPI-backed, as architecture.md:369 says, and PGP and S/MIME code exists. Virtual folders are real too, as saved searches in the folder tree. What is false is that those things live in the Search Engine, Account Manager and Cache Service boxes, and the Cache Service's size-based eviction has no code at all.
verdict.corrected_problem:
The scaffold types are never built by shipped code:
- src/application/accounts.rs (AccountManager and its Account)
- src/application/search.rs (SearchEngine and SearchQuery)
- src/service/cache.rs (CacheService)
- ServerConfig, Credentials and AccountSettings in common/types.rs

Their only users are their own unit tests and four tests in tests/integration_tests.rs. data::Account::from_provider and from_account_config are called only by tests. Through them, so is all of src/data/email_providers.rs, its presets and detect_provider_from_email included, and so is presentation::ui_types::AccountConfig.

Several places describe this scaffold as if it were the program:
- types.rs:315 says Credentials are encrypted by MessageCache, which is false.
- docs/architecture.md draws Account Manager, Search Engine and Cache Service boxes, with features such as size-based eviction, and shows the scaffold Account struct at lines 284-296.
- docs/plans/20260924-pro-licence.md:56 cites application::accounts as where accounts live.
- .planning/codebase/TESTING.md:77 recommends Account::new_simple.

The real code is elsewhere: data/account.rs and message_cache/accounts.rs for accounts, message_cache searching and saved_searches.rs for search, and service::credentials for secrets.
verdict.corrected_fix:
Delete these:
- src/application/accounts.rs, src/application/search.rs and src/service/cache.rs, with their `pub mod` and `pub use` lines.
- ServerConfig, Credentials and AccountSettings, with their two tests in types.rs.
- from_provider and from_account_config, with their tests in account.rs.
- The whole of src/data/email_providers.rs and its `pub mod` and `pub use` in data/mod.rs. Nothing else reaches it once those two constructors go. If the presets are kept for later instead, delete only get_imap_config and get_smtp_config and rewrite the two TLS tests to read the struct fields directly.
- ui_types::AccountConfig.
- test_multi_account_workflow, test_search_across_folders, test_cache_overwrite and test_cache_missing_key in tests/integration_tests.rs.

In the same commit:

Then fix the documents:

all.title: Three dependencies are declared for code that does not use them, and three comments say otherwise
all.location: Cargo.toml:93, 121-122; src/service/outward.rs:1616, 1622-1623, 1641-1645; src/service/security.rs:436-451; docs/changelog.md:14357; .cargo/audit.toml:43-45
all.what_this_is: icalendar and quick-xml are direct dependencies with no use anywhere in src, tests or build.rs; both CalDAV and iCalendar are parsed by hand. rand 0.10 is used once, inside #[cfg(test)] impl SecurityService::encrypt (security.rs:436-451), so it is a test-only crate declared as a shipped one.
all.problem: icalendar alone pulls iso8601 and nom-language into the build (Cargo.lock:2577-2587). The comments mislead a reviewer. The changelog line and audit.toml:43-45 say "the quick-xml 0.41 that parses CalDAV responses", and nothing in the program calls quick-xml. outward.rs:1641-1645 classifies image as decoding only the program's own compiled-in icon with ico, png and bmp, while service/picture.rs:47 decodes strangers' attachments with jpeg on. That is the reason a reviewer would read that entry for.
all.concrete_case: git grep -E "icalendar::|quick_xml::" across *.rs returns nothing. The only mentions are the name strings in A_CRATE_THAT_CANNOT. A security reviewer reading audit.toml concludes the CalDAV parser is quick-xml and audits the wrong code, while the real hand parser is the one in finding 1.
all.fix: Delete Cargo.toml:121-122 and the two list entries, since test_neither_list_of_crates_has_gone_stale requires the lists and the manifest to move together. Move rand = "0.10" to [dev-dependencies]; every_dependency already reads that section. Correct the image comment in outward.rs and the quick-xml sentence in audit.toml.
all.if_skipped: Two unused parsers stay in the dependency audit's scope, and the documents keep pointing at a parser that does not run.
all.ledger_entry: Map lead C, not in WINDOWS.md. Confirmed here and extended with rand and the three false comments.

verdict.reason:
I checked each claim against the code and confirmed it. Cargo.toml:121-122 declares icalendar 0.17 and quick-xml 0.41. A grep of every .rs file (src, tests, build.rs) finds neither crate's paths anywhere. The only mentions are the two name strings at outward.rs:1622-1623. `git log -S` finds no commit that ever added or removed `quick_xml::` or `icalendar::` in src, so both have been unused since they were added. rand 0.10 (Cargo.toml:93) is used only at security.rs:443/451, inside the `#[cfg(test)] impl SecurityService` that starts at line 436. The image entry at outward.rs:1641-1645 is out of date: Cargo.toml:236-241 now turns on jpeg, and service/picture.rs decodes picture attachments people are sent. audit.toml:43-45 and changelog:14357 both say a quick-xml 0.41 parses CalDAV responses, and nothing in the program does. WINDOWS.md has no entry for icalendar, quick-xml, rand or unused dependencies.

Parts of the finding are overstated, so the payoff is smaller than it says:
(1) quick-xml 0.41 stays in Cargo.lock and in the shipped program either way. phonenumber 0.3.10 lists it as both a normal and a build dependency (its Cargo.toml, and Cargo.lock:4254). Removing our line takes nothing out of the audit's scope.
(2) rand 0.10 stays in the tree through rodio and quinn-proto (Cargo.lock:4584, 4911). Moving it to [dev-dependencies] fixes the label and changes no shipped code.
(3) The two lists in outward.rs answer "can this crate reach a server?", and "image cannot" is still true. Only the description of what image decodes is stale.

Only icalendar really adds weight: icalendar, iso8601 and nom-language, three crates that only it pulls in (nom 8 stays because lettre and pgp use it).

The fix as written also misses three things:
- A_CRATE_THAT_CANNOT is declared `[&str; 56]`, so the length has to change too.
- The rand08 comment at Cargo.toml:337 says "the `rand` 0.10 named above". That stops being true once rand moves below.
- tests/house_style.rs:2154-2158 asserts that "Fixed iCalendar property lookup matching on a prefix" does not fire. That case only tests something because icalendar is a dependency, a word the reader sees and has to leave alone because no version follows it. With icalendar gone it passes for nothing, which is the "guard that reads documents needs a companion" trap CLAUDE.md warns about.

It is still worth doing: about ten lines, no behaviour change, and a security decision record that names the wrong parser. No guard record in guards/guards.toml anchors on any line this touches.
verdict.corrected_problem:
The manifest declares two crates that nothing uses: icalendar 0.17 and quick-xml 0.41 (Cargo.toml:121-122). Both CalDAV and iCalendar are parsed by hand, and git history shows neither crate was ever called from src. rand 0.10 (Cargo.toml:93) is used only inside `#[cfg(test)] impl SecurityService` (security.rs:436-451), yet it is declared as a normal dependency. icalendar alone brings in three crates nothing else needs: icalendar, iso8601 and nom-language.

Removing quick-xml and moving rand only fix the labels. quick-xml 0.41 stays in the program through phonenumber, which lists it as both a normal and a build dependency, and rand 0.10 stays through rodio and quinn-proto. The text is also wrong in three places:
- audit.toml:43-45 and changelog:14357 say "the quick-xml 0.41 that parses CalDAV responses", when that copy belongs to phonenumber.
- outward.rs:1641-1645 says image decodes only the compiled-in icon with ico, png and bmp. Since 0.65.0 it also decodes picture attachments people are sent, and jpeg is on. The entry's real answer, that image cannot reach a server, still holds.
- After the fix, the rand08 comment at Cargo.toml:337 ("the rand 0.10 named above") is wrong.

There is also a hidden coupling. tests/house_style.rs:2154-2158 uses "iCalendar" as its example of a word that matches a dependency and must not fire. Once icalendar is gone, that case checks nothing.
verdict.corrected_fix:
1. Delete the `icalendar` and `quick-xml` lines at Cargo.toml:121-122. Move or reword the "# CalDAV / iCalendar support" header, since it would otherwise sit above scraper, ego-tree and the other crates.
2. In outward.rs, remove "icalendar" and "quick-xml" from A_CRATE_THAT_CANNOT and change its type from `[&str; 56]` to `[&str; 54]`.
3. Move `rand = "0.10"` to [dev-dependencies]. Both every_dependency readers already read that section, so the "rand" list entry stays. Reword the rand08 comment at Cargo.toml:337-338 so it no longer says "named above".
4. In tests/house_style.rs:2154-2158, swap the iCalendar example for another dependency that is also an ordinary word, written without a version, for example "image" or "open". The negative case then keeps exercising the reader.
5. Rewrite the image comment at outward.rs:1641-1645: it decodes the app's own icon and picture attachments, with ico, png, bmp and jpeg on, and has no notion of a destination.
6. Correct audit.toml:43-45 to say quick-xml 0.41.0 arrives with phonenumber, as both a dependency and a build dependency, and that nothing here parses CalDAV with it.
Leave the historical changelog entry as it is, or add one line under [Unreleased]. Optionally correct .planning/codebase/STACK.md:51 and INTEGRATIONS.md:38, which repeat the same claim.

all.ledger_entry: Not in WINDOWS.md.

verdict.reason:
I checked all ten names and each one is only ever defined. A whole-tree grep (excluding target/) for each name finds its definition and nothing else in src/, tests/, guards/ or the docs. The one other hit is a planning note for img_tag_re.

- **html_renderer.rs:217-230:** the three regexes are pub and nothing calls them.
- **pgp/mod.rs:537-545:** the doc comment says "Asked by the surfaces that offer to import one". Nothing asks it. The only real caller of keys::a_key_is_here (keys.rs:784) is this wrapper, apart from tests at keys.rs:1458, 1475 and 1515.
- **outlook_data_file.rs:1938:** this is a third wording of the password sentence. The one actually spoken is importing_an_outlook_data_file.rs:437, which builds its own text from came.a_password_is_on_it (fed by has_a_password_on_it at line 103). Line 363 has another wording.
- **update_download.rs:61-72:** neither constant is read anywhere. Nothing in the module checks hosts, and the only grep hits for "host" are comments. The privacy test at update_check.rs:999 ties only update_check's own constants (WHERE_THE_ASKING_GOES and the others). So changing objects.githubusercontent.com at docs/privacy.md:859 fails nothing.

all.title: vCard line unfolding is a hand copy of the iCalendar unfolding, kept in step by comments
all.location: src/data/message_cache/contacts.rs:2141-2225 (unfold_vcard_lines, put_back_together, laid_out_by_hand, indented, opens_or_closes_a_card); src/service/caldav.rs:2889-2975 (unfolded, put_back_together, laid_out_by_hand, indented)
all.what_this_is: Both formats fold long lines the same way (RFC 5545 3.1 and RFC 6350 3.2), and both files implement the same "was this indentation folding or somebody's hand layout" heuristic. put_back_together and indented are byte-for-byte the same, and laid_out_by_hand differs only in which marker line it checks.
all.problem: Each copy's comment says the two "agree on purpose" (contacts.rs:2192-2193). Agreement held by prose is the failure mode this project keeps recording, and the data layer already calls service code freely (messages.rs alone has 45 crate::service:: uses).
all.concrete_case: caldav's opener check (component_named_after) already accepts BEGIN:VCARD in any case. The next fix to folding, for example a CR-only line ending or a tab rule, lands in caldav.rs, the calendar import gets it, and contacts imported from a file or CardDAV keep the old behaviour with no test noticing.
all.fix: Make unfold_vcard_lines call crate::service::caldav::unfolded(block) and delete the four copied helpers. caldav's version also drops trailing empty lines, so check that contact_from_vcard_block ignores them first. Mind the 35 guard records fingerprinting contacts.rs; the --remeasure run is the cost.
all.if_skipped: Two copies of a parser for strangers' bytes drift apart one fix at a time.
all.ledger_entry: Not in WINDOWS.md.

verdict.reason: The finding holds. I read both copies. `put_back_together` and `indented` are the same code in contacts.rs:2157-2170 and 2209-2211 and in caldav.rs:2914-2927 and 2963-2965. `laid_out_by_hand` (contacts.rs:2194, caldav.rs:2948) differs only in which marker check it calls. The comments at contacts.rs:2129-2130 and 2192-2193 are the only thing keeping the two in step. Contacts is the only reader that keeps its own copy: note_document.rs:41/87, ical_subscription.rs:98, invitations.rs:1354 and when_people_are_free.rs:164 all call `caldav::unfolded`. The data layer already calls into service code in 24 files, so there is no layering reason against it. Nothing about this is in WINDOWS.md. Both copies were written on 2026-08-07 (9c458b20, 8a3a5a9f), and the line-splitting and marker code has not changed in either file since, so they have not drifted yet. That makes this cleanup rather than a live bug, hence nice. A fix to folding made in caldav.rs would still miss contacts imported from a file or over CardDAV, and no test compares the two copies. Three claims needed correcting: (1) the line splitting is not the same in both, since contacts uses `.lines()` with `trim_end_matches('\r')` and caldav splits on CRLF and LF with one `strip_suffix('\r')`, though they agree on real input; (2) caldav's marker check accepts any one-word component on BEGIN or END, so it is broader than the VCARD-only check, which in practice does no harm because base64 and folded values cannot produce one; (3) the real cost is two guard records with byte-identical anchors, not a count remeasure.
verdict.corrected_problem: The vCard reader keeps a hand copy of the iCalendar unfolding: `put_back_together` and `indented` are the same code in both files, and `laid_out_by_hand` differs only in its marker check (VCARD only, where caldav accepts any one-word component). The two stay in step only because comments say they agree. Every other reader of the same line format (notes, subscriptions, invitations, free/busy) already calls `caldav::unfolded`. They have not drifted since both were written on 2026-08-07. Two minor differences exist: how lines are split (`.lines()` with `trim_end_matches('\r')` against a CRLF/LF split with one `strip_suffix('\r')`), and how wide the marker check is.
verdict.corrected_fix: Change the body of `unfold_vcard_lines` to `crate::service::caldav::unfolded(block)` and keep the function, so the tests at contacts.rs:2430-2630 and 2888 still name it and the per-file test counts do not change. Delete `put_back_together`, `laid_out_by_hand`, `indented` and `opens_or_closes_a_card` from contacts.rs and replace their prose with a pointer to caldav. Dropping trailing empty lines does no harm, because `contact_from_vcard_block` (contacts.rs:1476) only acts on lines `vcard_named` matches. Guard records: the contacts.rs record "a leading indented line with nothing above it stands on its own rather than vanishing" (guards.toml:10213) anchors on code that will be deleted, so retire it. Then re-measure the caldav.rs record "a document whose first line is indented keeps that line" (guards.toml:24203), because breaking caldav's code will now also turn `test_a_line_indented_with_nothing_above_it_stands_on_its_own` red. No other record anchors on the deleted helpers. That comes to about 60 lines removed.

all.title: The per-folder POP readers that caused re-downloads are still public, beside the account-wide ones that replaced them
all.location: src/data/message_cache/messages.rs:756-776 (pop_uidls), 1037-1066 (pop_download_times); tests at 3332, 3385
all.what_this_is: pop_uidls(folder_id) and pop_download_times(folder_id) read POP identifiers and download times for one folder. Their replacements, pop_uidls_for_account (789) and pop_download_times_for_account (814), read the whole account and the shared Trash.
all.problem: No shipped code calls the per-folder pair; one test each does. The replacements' own docs (778-784, 808-813) explain why the per-folder reading is wrong: a message moved to Trash or deleted here is re-downloaded on the next check, and a message that left the inbox never leaves the server. Shorter names that look right, with no warning on them, invite a later caller to bring that back.
all.concrete_case: A future "POP sync for one folder" helper reaches for cache.pop_uidls(inbox), the obvious name. Every POP message the person deleted reappears on the next check, which is the bug 13-44.7 fixed.
all.fix: Delete both functions and point their two tests at the _for_account versions, or delete those tests if the account-wide tests already cover the same rows.
all.if_skipped: The bug's previous shape stays one autocomplete away.
all.ledger_entry: Not in WINDOWS.md.

verdict.reason:
Checked against the code, and the finding holds. `pop_uidls(folder_id)` at `messages.rs:761` and `pop_download_times(folder_id)` at `messages.rs:1042` are both `pub`, and each reads only `WHERE folder_id = ?1`. I searched the whole tree, leaving out `target/`, and nothing in shipped code calls either one. `pop_sync.rs:261` and `:309`, `local_delete.rs`, `emptying_the_trash.rs` and `taken_off_this_computer.rs` all call the `_for_account` versions. The only callers are two test lines, `messages.rs:3332` and `:3385`. The `_for_account` doc comments at `:778-788` and `:808-813` say in plain words that reading one folder brings deleted POP mail back on the next check and keeps aged mail on the server. Neither per-folder reader carries any warning, and both have the shorter, more obvious names.

This is not in `.planning/WINDOWS.md`. Ledger 770 and 9881 mention only the `_for_account` widening in 13-44.7. No guard record anchors on either function or names the two tests. The record at `guards.toml:37002` anchors on `pop_uidls_for_account`'s WHERE clause, so deleting these does not move it.

It stays at nice because nothing is broken today. The harm needs a future caller who picks the wrong name. The fix is about 50 deleted lines with no change in behaviour.

One part of the proposed fix is wrong. Both tests already assert the `_for_account` half. In each, the per-folder call is the control that proves the move really took the row out of the inbox; the message on line 3333 says "the folder-scoped read found it, so this proves nothing". So "point them at the `_for_account` versions" makes no sense, and deleting the tests would lose the same-account move-to-Trash case, which is a different case from the shared-Trash tests in `pop_sync`.
verdict.corrected_problem: `MessageCache::pop_uidls(folder_id)` at `src/data/message_cache/messages.rs:756-776` and `MessageCache::pop_download_times(folder_id)` at `:1037-1066` are public and read one folder only. That is the scope the `_for_account` doc comments at `:778-788` and `:808-813` say is wrong for POP: a deleted message is downloaded again on the next check, and mail that left the inbox never ages off the server. No shipped code calls them. Their only use is as the control assertion in two tests, `test_mail_moved_to_the_trash_is_still_mail_this_computer_has` (`:3332`) and `test_the_download_time_of_moved_mail_still_counts_towards_the_policy` (`:3385`). Both have shorter, more obvious names than the correct readers and no warning on them, so a later caller can bring back the re-download bug that 13-44.7 fixed.
verdict.corrected_fix: Delete both functions. In the two tests, keep the `_for_account` assertions and replace each per-folder control with one that does not need a per-folder POP reader. Use the check the neighbouring test already uses at `:3410`, `assert!(cache.get_message_list(inbox, "acc").unwrap().is_empty(), "the message is still in the inbox, so this proves nothing")`. Keep the tests rather than deleting them: they cover a move to Trash within the same account, which the shared-Trash tests in `pop_sync` do not. The test count in `messages.rs` stays the same, so no guard record needs re-measuring. No behaviour changes, so no new red test is needed. Before deleting, take the control red once: comment out `move_message` and check that each test still fails on its control.
